Negative result (TE < 0.4 same-family, or < 0.3 cross-architecture, or not above controls) refutes H1 for that regime. Systems/controls: (a) random-direction transfer through T, (b) naive same-index feature transfer without alignment, (c) no steering, (d) the source direction inserted into the target WITHOUT the alignment map (unaligned control); tested across all size pairs, cross-architecture pairs, and the molecular pair. Absolute property gain, validity retention, and novelty/diversity also reported.

Experiment 2 (H2 - cheap models as steerability-screening proxies): Tests whether source-model steerability predicts target-model steerability, so the small model can pre-select which directions will steer the big one. Decisive metric: Spearman rho between source-model native steerability and target-model steerability of the transferred direction (and of the natively rediscovered counterpart). Convincing result: rho >= 0.5, with precision@10 >= 0.7 for using the small model to pick the target's steerable directions, and compute saved (big-model generation runs avoided to find 10 good directions) >= 50%. Decision band: rho in [0.3, 0.5] or precision@10 in [0.5, 0.7] -> a useful but noisy proxy. Negative result (rho <= 0.3 or precision@10 near random) refutes H2. Data: a large per-property direction bank (tens of directions) across the size and architecture pairs, bootstrap CIs.

Experiment 3 (H1 robustness - transfer preserves compositionality; and failure analysis): Tests whether jointly transferring 2-3 directions preserves multi-constraint control on the target, and characterizes where transfer breaks. Decisive metric: joint constraint-satisfaction rate on the target under transferred directions, versus the same on natively validated directions. Convincing result: transferred joint satisfaction >= 0.7x the native joint satisfaction with comparable interference. Decision band: [0.4, 0.7]x -> partial preservation. Negative result (< 0.4x) means transfer does not carry compositional control. Failure analysis reports which property types and layer/architecture pairs fail and whether alignment quality (SVCCA/R^2) predicts Transfer Efficiency - a scientifically informative characterization of the limits of feature universality even under a broadly negative outcome.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Cross-architecture representation spaces (masked vs autoregressive; different tokenizers) may be too dissimilar for a linear alignment; we mitigate by also testing same-family size-scaling transfer (easier) and reporting where the linear assumption fails, which is itself informative. 2) In-silico oracles/validity are proxies for wet-lab function; claims concern model-internal controllability and design compute-efficiency, not experimental viability. 3) Alignment may require a sizable paired-activation corpus; we quantify sensitivity to corpus size and use held-out objects to avoid leakage. 4) The DiMaS finding that features can be decodable-but-not-steerable means some directions may fail to transfer steerability even if the property signal transfers; we treat this as a measured outcome (the steerability-proxy test) rather than an assumption. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound; we control with multiple layers and both SAE-feature and difference-of-means directions. 6) If transfer efficiency is low, the negative result still provides a valuable, publishable characterization of the limits of feature universality for controllable generation.

Name: symmetry_shortcut_crystal
Title: Symmetry Without Understanding? Auditing Whether Crystal Generative Models Causally Represent Space-Group Constraints or Silently Fake Them
Short Hypothesis: Crystal generative models conditioned on a target space group satisfy the constraint not because they possess a compact, causally-manipulable internal representation of the requested symmetry, but via a shallow lattice/Wyckoff-copying shortcut. We hypothesize (i) there is a decodable but only weakly causally-steerable internal 'space-group' direction; (ii) steering it to request a NEW space group frequently yields structures whose achieved symmetry silently mismatches the request (wrong space group, lower symmetry, or broken periodicity) while still passing validity/stability checks; and (iii) an intervention-free internal symmetry-consistency signal predicts these silent failures better than output-side likelihood or formation-energy proxies.
Related Work: Symmetry-aware crystal generation is a rich area: SymmCD (2025), DiffCSP++/Space-Group-Constrained Generation (2024), WyCryst (2023), and PGCGM (2022) either hard-code space-group/Wyckoff constraints or condition on them. Critically, Ishii et al. (2026, WyckoffDiff-Adaptor) show that conditional symmetry control 'may not be sufficiently effective when space group constraints are applied as a condition'—i.e., models silently violate the requested symmetry—but treat this as an architecture problem, not a representational one. Interpretability in materials (CGCNN 2018, Site-Net 2022, RankAAE 2023) is confined to PREDICTIVE property models with attention/latent-descriptor analysis; none examines the internal mechanism of GENERATIVE crystal models, and none asks whether symmetry—the defining, physics-critical property of crystals—is a genuine causal handle or a copying shortcut. No prior work (a) locates and causally tests a space-group representation inside a crystal generator, (b) shows symmetry-conditioned generation silently fakes the requested symmetry via a shortcut, or (c) provides an internal symmetry-reliability audit that catches these failures. This distinguishes the proposal from all symmetry-architecture work (which changes the model) and mirrors, in a new object class and for a new property (crystallographic symmetry vs stereochemistry), the shortcut-auditing lens of prior molecular proposals. CLOSEST-PRIOR-WORK CONTRAST: (i) known failure phenomenon -- Ishii et al. 2026 report silent symmetry violation but treat it as architecture; (ii) architecture fixes -- SymmCD/DiffCSP++/WyCryst hard-code or condition symmetry; (iii) predictive-model interpretability -- CGCNN/Site-Net/RankAAE analyze property predictors, not generators; (iv) molecular shortcut-auditing -- our prior lens, here transferred to crystallographic symmetry. Setting-specific difference: crystal symmetry is a discrete, globally-defined group constraint (not a local per-token property), invariant to equivalent cell/origin re-descriptions -- so a genuine representation must be re-description-invariant, a test with no molecular analogue. Novelty is the mechanistic explanation plus a released, model-agnostic audit artifact, not the mismatch itself.
Abstract: Symmetry is the defining property of a crystal: its space group dictates physical behavior and is the primary control knob in crystal generative models, which hard-code it or condition on it. Recent work shows conditional symmetry control can silently fail -- models emit structures lacking the requested space group. Our novelty is NOT rediscovering that mismatch but explaining it mechanistically and converting the explanation into a reusable audit. We ask: do crystal generators possess an internal, causally-manipulable representation of the requested symmetry, or satisfy the constraint through a shallow lattice/Wyckoff-copying shortcut? Using open symmetry-conditioned diffusion generators (DiffCSP++/SymmCD-style) on Materials Project data, we (1) LOCATE candidate space-group representations by probing the denoiser's activations, controlling for trivial copying of the conditioning token; (2) CAUSALLY test whether a compact intervention converts generation from space group A to B -- yielding a structure whose ACHIEVED symmetry (pymatgen SpacegroupAnalyzer over a tolerance sweep) matches B while composition and atom count are held fixed -- the operational definition of a genuine handle, distinguished from a copied conditioning signal; (3) INTERPRET whether located units encode true symmetry (invariant to equivalent cell re-descriptions and origin choices) or surface lattice/Wyckoff statistics; and (4) AUDIT reliability via the SILENT SYMMETRY-ERROR RATE and an intervention-free internal symmetry-consistency score benchmarked against likelihood, formation-energy proxies, and a simple output-side symmetry heuristic. We deliver a model-agnostic, plug-in-without-retraining symmetry-reliability audit suite plus a controlled re-description dataset, and propose a minimal reporting standard. Stakeholders: crystal-generation researchers and computational materials scientists screening generated candidates, where silent symmetry errors waste relaxation compute and corrupt downstream property assumptions.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: open symmetry-conditioned crystal diffusion generators with accessible per-step denoiser activations -- a coordinate-based diffusion (DiffCSP++-style) and a Wyckoff-based diffusion (SymmCD/WyckoffDiff-style) checkpoint, trained on Materials Project / MP-20. Base weights frozen; only probes/SAEs trained. Achieved-symmetry ground truth: pymatgen SpacegroupAnalyzer over a tolerance sweep (record achieved space group, crystal system, point group, Wyckoff multiplicities). Validity gates: bond-length/overlap checks, charge neutrality, StructureMatcher novelty; stability proxy = energy-above-hull from a pretrained universal ML interatomic potential (CHGNet/MACE-MP), NO DFT. Probes: linear/MLP on denoiser residual activations at multiple timesteps/layers; difference-of-means directions and full activation-patching for intervention; norm-matched random-direction and matched-non-symmetry-feature controls. 500 generations per condition. DELIVERABLE: a released model-agnostic symmetry-consistency AUDIT SUITE (usable as a plug-in pre-flight filter on existing generators without retraining) and a CONTROLLED RE-DESCRIPTION dataset (structures paired with symmetry-preserving cell/origin re-descriptions). All match rates, AUROCs, and subgroup effects are reported with bootstrap confidence intervals over >=3 seeds and multiple-comparison control across space-group strata; numeric decision thresholds below are pre-registered, and where arbitrary we also report the corresponding relative comparison and CI. Per-step denoiser activations and activation patching are confirmed extractable for the named open checkpoints via forward hooks on the denoiser network.

Experiment 0/1 (H1 -- Baseline reproduction, then: is the space group decodable?). Establishes that the model unconditionally reproduces target space groups above chance (so absence/weak-steerability claims are meaningful) and that space group is decodable internally. Data: 5,000 conditioned generations spanning the space-group vocabulary; probes trained on denoiser activations. Baseline metric: requested-vs-achieved space-group match rate vs a frequency-matched random-request chance level. Decoding: probe accuracy for target space group, crystal system, and lattice class vs timestep/layer, against a control probe that predicts the raw conditioning-token embedding (to gauge trivial copy-of-condition). Decisive metric: symmetry-probe accuracy minus condition-copy-probe accuracy. Convincing baseline+decodability: baseline match rate clearly above chance AND space-group probe accuracy >= 0.7 that exceeds the condition-copy control by >= 0.1. Decision band: probe-minus-copy gap in [0.0, 0.1] means the decodable signal is largely a copy of the conditioning input -- flagged. Negative baseline: if the model does not reproduce target space groups above chance, the study is under-powered for the steerability claim and reported as inconclusive.

Experiment 2 (H1 -- The space-group direction is only WEAKLY causally steerable). Tests whether intervening on the decoded direction switches the achieved space group from A to B. Data/systems: generations conditioned on space group A; intervene via probe-derived direction, difference-of-means (B-minus-A), and full activation-patching from a B-conditioned run, vs random-direction and matched-non-symmetry controls; dose-response swept. Causal controls are strengthened: timestep-matched random patching, layer-matched non-symmetry directions, and A-vs-B runs sharing the same random seed so only the symmetry intervention differs; composition and atom count are held fixed throughout so 'space-group switching' is unambiguous. Decisive metric (primary): SYMMETRY-SWITCH SUCCESS RATE = fraction of interventions yielding a finished structure whose SpacegroupAnalyzer symmetry equals B while composition and validity/stability are preserved and the change is specific. Convincing support for H1 (decodable-but-weakly-steerable): switch success in (5%, 40%] -- clearly above the random control (weakly causal) yet far below the conditioning baseline's match rate -- with failures skewed to subgroups of A/B. Decision band: success <= 5% means essentially NO causal handle (stronger than "weak"); >= 40% with specificity means a GENUINE strong handle -- either extreme is reported as such rather than as the hypothesized weak-steerability. Negative for the phenomenon: a strong, specific handle (>=40%) refutes the shortcut framing and is an equally publishable positive finding.

Experiment 3 (H2 -- Silent symmetry mismatches that pass validity/stability). Tests that requesting a new space group frequently yields valid+stable structures whose achieved symmetry silently differs from the request. Data/systems: across the full space-group vocabulary (stratified by crystal system, symmetry order, and training frequency), request each space group; among VALID+stable outputs measure the mismatch. Decisive metric (primary): SILENT SYMMETRY-ERROR RATE = fraction of valid+stable outputs whose achieved space group differs from requested, decomposed into correct-crystal-system-but-wrong-group, dropped-to-subgroup, and fully-broken-symmetry, stratified by requested symmetry order and training frequency. Convincing positive: silent error rate rising with symmetry order to >= 30% for high-symmetry / low-frequency requests, tolerance-robust across the SpacegroupAnalyzer sweep. Decision band: error rate in [15%, 30%) means mismatch exists but is modest -- reported as such; error rate that flips sign of conclusion across tolerances is reported as tolerance-sensitive and excluded from strong claims. Negative: error rate < 15% (models reliably achieve the requested symmetry) refutes H2. Interpretation sub-test (supports H1/H2): controlled crystal pairs dissociating space group from surface descriptors (same group / different lattice params or origin; different groups / similar lattice params) test whether the located feature is invariant to equivalent cell re-descriptions (true symmetry) or tracks lattice-parameter/Wyckoff-token statistics (shortcut) -- a feature that changes meaning under symmetry-preserving re-description is scored as a shortcut.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Internal symmetry-consistency signal beats output-side proxies at flagging silent failures). Tests that an intervention-free internal signal predicts silent symmetry errors better than likelihood or formation-energy proxies. Data/systems: for each generation compute an internal symmetry-consistency score (probe confidence / feature coherence read mid-generation); baselines -- generation likelihood, e-above-hull/formation-energy proxy, validity checks, a SIMPLE OUTPUT-SIDE SYMMETRY HEURISTIC (estimating symmetry from the partial/finished structure directly, no internals), and a black-box raw-activation probe; target label = silent symmetry error from Experiment 3. Decisive metric (primary): detection AUROC and calibration ECE for flagging silent symmetry errors. Convincing positive: internal-signal AUROC >= 0.80 with ECE<=0.10 while output-side likelihood/energy proxies stay in [0.45, 0.60] (near chance), with quantified compute saved by aborting untrustworthy requests before full generation + relaxation. Decision band: internal AUROC in [0.65, 0.80), or its edge over the black-box probe in [0.03, 0.10) AUROC, means the internal signal works but its advantage over cheaper signals is marginal -- the interpretability (shortcut-vs-concept) diagnosis is then the contribution. Negative: output-side proxies already reach AUROC>=0.70, or the internal signal fails to beat them, refutes H3. Robustness across the two generator architectures, two tolerances, and high- vs low-symmetry groups.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The core claim is partly an ABSENCE claim (no clean causal symmetry handle); we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (probe direction, difference-of-means, full activation patching), sweeping strength, and requiring the step-1 baseline to confirm the model does reproduce target space groups—so a null switch result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable symmetry handle) is equally publishable and useful for symmetry-controlled design. 2) Achieved-symmetry ground truth depends on SpacegroupAnalyzer tolerance; we sweep tolerances and report sensitivity, restricting strong claims to tolerance-robust cases. 3) Stability is assessed by ML interatomic potentials (CHGNet/MACE), an in-silico proxy for DFT/synthesizability; claims concern requested-vs-achieved symmetry (an objective crystallographic fact) and model-internal representation, not experimental synthesizability. 4) Requires generators with accessible per-step activations; scope limited to open, instrumentable models. 5) An internal probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, the interpretability diagnosis (shortcut vs concept) and the reliability-audit payoff are the contributions and are reported honestly. 6) Symmetry and lattice statistics may be irreducibly entangled for some space groups; the controlled re-description pairs (step 4) are designed to separate them and we report where separation is impossible.

Name: regulatory_grammar_syntax_steering
Title: Motifs Without Grammar: Do Genomic Language Models Causally Steer Cis-Regulatory Syntax, or Just Sprinkle Motifs?
Short Hypothesis: We make three typed, separable claims. (Finding) Genomic language models (Evo 2 / regLM-style) possess interpretable, causally-steerable features for the PRESENCE of transcription-factor motifs. (Mechanism) They do NOT possess a robust steerable direction for motif SYNTAX — the inter-motif spacing, strand orientation, and helical-phasing constraints that make a cis-regulatory element functional; syntax is DECODABLE from activations but, under every intervention family we test, weakly steerable (we scope this as 'no robust steerable syntax direction found,' not universal absence). (Audit) Because content-based validity/activity checks look only at motif identity, steering to 'add motif X' silently places motifs in syntactically invalid configurations that break predicted activity, and an intervention-free internal syntax-consistency signal flags these silent failures better than output-side checks.
Related Work: Genomic interpretability is active but confined to motif PRESENCE. Per-claim positioning with deltas: (i) SAE motif-feature work (Evo 2 SAEs 2025; small gene-LM SAEs 2025) discovers presence features and shows single-property steering — delta: we ask the orthogonal question of whether SYNTAX, not content, is a steerable handle. (ii) ARGMINN (2024) reads motif spacing preferences from a bespoke predictive architecture — delta: reading syntax from weights is not evidence a general gLM CAUSALLY controls syntax during generation; we test the intervention, not the read-out. (iii) regLM (2024) and DREAM (2024) steer CREs toward target activity/cell-type via LMs + supervised scorers — delta: they optimize scalar activity and never separate the content vs syntax controllability axis. Benchmark critiques (DART-Eval 2024; gLM representational-power 2024; Karollus 2022, models ignoring distal enhancers) hint gLMs capture correlational content over causal grammar but never test this at feature-steering controllability. Setting novelty: promoter/proximal-enhancer syntax is a distinct controllability regime because function there depends on cooperative TF spacing/phasing rather than on any single motif's presence, so content-steering can succeed on its own metric while destroying function — a failure mode absent from prior single-property CRE steering. Our contributions are thus three separable items: a new empirical finding (presence steerable), a mechanistic diagnosis (syntax decodable-but-not-steerable), and an internal audit method — not a new generator.
Abstract: The function of a cis-regulatory element is determined not just by which transcription-factor (TF) motifs it contains, but by their SYNTAX: the spacing, orientation, and helical phasing that let bound proteins cooperate. Interpretability-guided DNA design increasingly steers genomic language model (gLM) features to insert desired motifs, judged by whether the motif appears and predicted activity rises. We surface a phenomenon we call the syntax blind spot: steering an interpretable feature to add a motif reliably increases motif content but places motifs in syntactically incoherent configurations that activity models score as non-functional — and content-based checks never notice. We make three typed claims: (finding) motif PRESENCE is a causally-steerable feature; (mechanism) motif SYNTAX is decodable yet has no robust steerable direction under the interventions we test, unlike presence; (audit) an intervention-free internal syntax-consistency signal flags silently-broken designs better than output-side checks. Using an open gLM (Evo 2 / a regLM-style autoregressive model) with sparse autoencoders and cheap in-silico oracles (FIMO/JASPAR for content; spacing/orientation/10.5-bp phasing statistics for syntax; a supervised sequence-to-activity model for function), we (1) LOCATE presence and syntax features and VALIDATE that content and syntax are separable in probe space before any causal claim; (2) CAUSALLY test whether steering each controls its intended axis with matched-length/GC, shuffled-feature, and raw-hidden-state controls plus a power analysis for the null; (3) quantify the syntax tax content-steering incurs on activity; and (4) audit reliability. Either outcome is actionable: steerable syntax gives grammar-aware design knobs; non-steerable syntax means design tools need explicit grammar constraints and audit layers before wet-lab validation.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: (primary) a regLM-style autoregressive gLM, ~10M params, trained on the Vaishnav 2022 yeast random-promoter GPRA library (~20M sequences; 1M subsample, one GPU); (cross-model) Evo 2 (7B, public) FROZEN at its published biologically-relevant layer (~26). Base models FROZEN; only BatchTopK SAEs trained (expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations, seeds 0/1/2). OPERATIONAL SYNTAX DEFINITION: for an ordered motif pair (A,B), syntax = the tuple (inter-motif gap in bp, relative strand orientation, helical phase = gap mod 10.5). CONTENT oracle: FIMO/JASPAR PWM calls (identity+position); to handle FIMO false positives we require q<0.05 AND confirm with a second caller (HMMER/MOODS) and count a motif present only on agreement. FUNCTION oracle: the GPRA-trained CNN (yeast) plus Enformer (human) as an ORTHOGONAL second function oracle; claims restricted to where the two agree in rank (Spearman>=0.5). Validity gate: GC bounds + pseudo-perplexity. Data: 50,000 held-out promoters for feature-property linking; 5,000 DISSOCIATION PAIRS with identical motif content but functional vs scrambled spacing. Steering = add alpha*d_hat at the SAE layer; alpha in {0,1,2,4,8} residual-RMS units.

Experiment 0 (disentanglement validation, PREREQUISITE): before any causal claim, verify content and syntax are separable in probe space — train probes for motif identity and for the syntax tuple on the dissociation pairs; require content-probe AUROC>=0.8 with near-chance syntax leakage and syntax-probe AUROC>=0.7 with near-chance content leakage (cross-prediction AUROC<=0.6). If not separable for a motif combination, that combination is excluded and reported.

Experiment 1 (finding - PRESENCE is causally steerable): identify presence features (held-out probe AUROC>=0.8), steer to ADD a target motif to sequences lacking it; 500 sequences per (feature,alpha,seed) for the 15 most frequent JASPAR yeast motifs. Controls: random-direction, shuffled-feature, matched-length and matched-GC. Decisive metric FIRST: two-caller motif-installation rate. Decision band: >=0.60 AND >=0.40 above best control for >=2/3 motifs => presence is a handle; gain [0.15,0.40) => inconclusive; <0.15 => not steerable (undercuts premise, reported).

Experiment 2 (mechanism - SYNTAX decodable but not steerable): (a) DECODABILITY: probe SAE features/raw activations for the syntax tuple, controlling for content (report AUROC/R^2). (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head with a FORMAL objective: shift inter-motif gap toward a target helical phase (e.g. 5 bp -> 21 bp) while holding content fixed, using best syntax direction (SAE feature, difference-of-means functional-vs-scrambled, activation-patching from correct-syntax), compared against raw-hidden-state directions and NULL syntax features. Decisive metric FIRST: efficacy ratio r = (normalized achieved gap shift)/(presence-installation efficacy). POWER: pre-compute the N of generations needed to detect r=0.5 at 80% power; report the achieved MDE so the null is statistically supported. Decision band: syntax decodable (AUROC>=0.70) AND r<=0.33 (CI upper bound below 0.33) => mechanism confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial; r>=0.67 => syntax IS steerable (refutes, equally publishable).

Experiment 3 (audit part A - silent breakage): steer presence features, 500 sequences per level. Among content-satisfying, valid, low-perplexity sequences, measure activity loss from bad syntax. Decisive metric FIRST: SILENT-BREAKAGE RATE = fraction below the 10th percentile of natural-CRE activity despite passing content+validity; plus Spearman rho between cheap checks (content-satisfaction, perplexity) and true activity. Decision band: breakage>=0.30 AND |rho|<=0.20 => silent blind spot confirmed; [0.10,0.30) or |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; <0.10 or |rho|>=0.40 => not silent.

Experiment 4 (audit part B - internal flag): no-intervention score = syntax-probe confidence / SAE-feature coherence read mid-generation. Decisive metric FIRST: AUROC for detecting eventually-non-functional sequences from Exp 3, vs output-side detectors (content-satisfaction, perplexity, function-oracle confidence). Decision band: internal AUROC>=0.75 AND >=0.10 above best output-side => flag confirmed; margin (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; <=0.05 => internal signal no better (reported; mechanism diagnosis still stands). ROBUSTNESS: Evo 2 vs regLM, promoter vs proximal-enhancer; counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Function and syntax are assessed by in-silico oracles (GPRA CNN, Enformer, FIMO/JASPAR); these are proxies, so claims concern model-internal, in-silico-verified syntactic controllability, NOT biological truth about regulatory grammar — stated explicitly. Sequence-to-activity models capture promoters better than distal enhancers (Karollus 2022), so core claims are on promoter/proximal-enhancer regimes and enhancer results are reported separately. We use two function oracles and two motif callers and restrict claims to where they agree. 2) The syntax-non-steerability claim is scoped as absence-under-tested-interventions; we mitigate with multiple intervention types, strength sweeps, a power analysis / reported MDE, and head-to-head calibration that PRESENCE features ARE steerable in the same pipeline — so a null is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive steerable-syntax result is equally publishable and valuable for grammar-aware design. 3) Content and syntax may be entangled for some motif combinations; Experiment 0 validates separability in probe space and excludes/reports inseparable cases. 4) SAE quality/layer could confound Location; controlled with multiple SAE variants, the Evo 2 published layer, raw-activation probes, shuffled-feature and null-feature controls. 5) An internal syntax probe might not beat a raw-activation probe on AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis and audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 6) If no syntax tax is found (content steering preserves grammar/activity), that is a valuable positive result establishing gLM feature-steering as grammar-safe for regulatory DNA design.

Name: internal_validity_foresight
Title: Failure Foresight: Do Interpretable Features Predict Invalid Scientific Generations Early Enough to Abort and Save Compute?
Short Hypothesis: The contribution is a compute-efficiency policy for VALIDITY, not merely the observation that features predict failure. During iterative/autoregressive generation of proteins and molecules, a small set of interpretable sparse-autoencoder features acts as an early internal 'validity alarm' predicting, well before generation completes, whether the finished object will be structurally INVALID—unfoldable, chemically invalid, degenerate. Unlike toxicity or factual hallucination, structural invalidity is an unambiguous physical/chemical fact with a hard evaluator, which makes both the label and the abort decision crisp. Monitoring these features enables a cheap early-abort-and-restart policy that raises valid objects produced per unit compute far above running every generation to completion, and does so more efficiently and interpretably than output-probability or perplexity-based early stopping or a compute-matched black-box probe.
Related Work: A large body of interpretability work uses SAE features to detect and mitigate hallucinations in text and vision-language models (RAGLens 2025; SSL/SAVE/SAFE 2025; 'Do I Know This Entity?' 2024; H-Neurons 2025) and to detect hallucinations early from internal states in factual QA (Varshney et al. 2024; MHAD 2024; HaMI 2025; HD-NDEs 2025). Separately, interpretability-for-design work on proteins/molecules (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; ProtoMech 2026; molecular-LM SAEs) focuses on STEERING features to add properties, and evaluates validity only as a side constraint. No prior work (a) treats interpretable features as a predictive EARLY-WARNING signal for the objective, structurally-verifiable INVALIDITY of a to-be-generated scientific object, (b) uses that signal to drive an early-abort-and-restart policy that improves valid-yield-per-compute, or (c) compares such interpretable monitoring against output-probability/perplexity early-stopping baselines on a compute-efficiency frontier. We convert the 'model self-knowledge' insight from the text-hallucination literature into a concrete, compute-saving reliability tool for scientific design, where validity is an unambiguous physical/chemical fact rather than fuzzy factuality. No prior SAE-auditing or early-failure-detection paper frames the decision as a compute-allocation policy—an abort-and-restart frontier trading detector cost and false-abort rate against generation budget saved—so that contribution is not covered by existing hallucination-detection or interpretability-auditing work.
Abstract: Generative models for scientific design routinely emit invalid objects—proteins that do not fold, molecules that violate chemistry, degenerate sequences—and practitioners pay the full cost of generation and validation before discovering the failure, wasting large fractions of a screening budget. We ask whether a model's own interpretable internal features reveal, early in generation, that it is heading toward an invalid object, and whether acting on that signal saves substantial compute. Building on evidence that sparse-autoencoder (SAE) features encode a form of model self-knowledge, we train SAEs on intermediate activations of protein and molecular generators and search for a compact 'validity-alarm' feature set whose early activations predict the eventual validity of the finished object, verified by hard structural evaluators (ESMFold pLDDT and pseudo-perplexity; RDKit validity and synthetic accessibility). We evaluate two claims separately: (i) alarm features forecast invalidity earlier and more accurately than output-probability/perplexity signals and at least as well as a compute-matched black-box probe; and (ii) an early-abort-and-restart controller built on them Pareto-dominates run-to-completion and output-side early stopping on the valid-objects-per-compute frontier, after charging the detector's own overhead. Probability-based stopping reacts only to output-side uncertainty and a black-box probe is opaque; interpretable alarms are both earlier and human-readable, yielding failure diagnoses (e.g., frustrated partial structures). First adopters are protein- and molecule-generation teams running large in-silico screens who need higher valid throughput per GPU-hour. Results would establish interpretable features as a practical reliability-and-efficiency layer for scientific generation.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Generators (instrumentable for per-step activations, frozen): (a) a protein generator - an autoregressive protein LM (ProtGPT2/p-IgGen) and/or a masked-diffusion protein LM; (b) a molecular generator - a GPT-style SMILES LM and/or a SMILES/graph diffusion model. Hard automatic VALIDITY labels for finished objects: proteins - ESMFold pLDDT above threshold AND pseudo-perplexity below threshold AND non-degenerate (low repeat/entropy); molecules - RDKit parseable/valence-valid AND passing basic sanity (SA score, ring/atom-count bounds). Corpus: 20k generations per model under normal sampling, saving full per-step activation trajectories, giving a balanced valid/invalid set. TopK SAEs (k=32, dictionary 16,384) on the residual stream at a mid layer (intrinsic-dimension-elbow). At each progress fraction (10/25/50/75%) each SAE feature's mutual information / AUROC about eventual validity is measured on a training split, and a compact "validity-alarm" feature set is selected by information; all thresholds are fixed on a held-out split. Generation seeds: 5.

Experiment 1 (H1 - SAE features are an early validity alarm): Tests whether a small SAE-feature set forecasts eventual invalidity well before generation completes, earlier than output-side signals and competitively with a black-box probe. Decisive metric: forecast AUROC of the alarm features as a function of generation-progress fraction, summarized as the earliest progress fraction reaching AUROC 0.8. Convincing result: alarm features reach AUROC 0.8 at <= 50% progress, earlier (by >= 10% of the trajectory) than the best output-side signal and within 0.03 AUROC of a black-box MLP probe on raw activations, while remaining sparse. Decision band: AUROC-0.8 point in (50%, 75%] progress, or an earliness margin in [3%, 10%] of the trajectory -> foresight exists but is late/marginal. Negative result (never reaches AUROC 0.8 before completion, or no earlier than output-side signals) refutes H1. Baselines at the same progress point: running token log-probability, partial pseudo-perplexity, predictive entropy, and the raw-activation MLP probe (matched for parameter count and inference compute). Results are stratified by failure type (gross degenerate vs subtle near-miss invalidity) to report where foresight is easy versus hard. Alarm-feature interpretability is checked by auto-labeling top features and confirming faithfulness (clamping the feature shifts validity outcomes).

Experiment 2 (H2+H3 - early-abort-and-restart raises valid yield per compute, beating perplexity-based stopping): Tests whether monitoring the alarm features to abort-and-restart produces more valid objects per unit compute than running to completion and than output-side early stopping. Decisive metric: number of VALID objects produced per unit compute (total forward/decoding steps and ESMFold calls avoided, NET of the SAE monitoring overhead—the extra encoder passes—so 'compute saved' already charges the detector's cost), traced as a frontier over the abort threshold. Convincing result: the SAE-alarm controller yields >= 20% more valid objects per unit compute than run-to-completion and strictly beats output-probability/perplexity early stopping, while retaining >= 90% of the run-to-completion set's diversity/novelty and reporting the false-abort rate (valid generations wrongly killed). Decision band: improvement in [5%, 20%] over run-to-completion, or a tie with perplexity stopping -> a modest or contested gain. Negative result (no compute-frontier improvement, or diversity collapses below 90%) refutes H2/H3. Systems on the same frontier: (a) run-to-completion, (b) output-probability/perplexity-threshold stopping, (c) black-box raw-activation-probe abort, (d) random-abort at matched abort rate. Conditional/steered setting: repeat the frontier comparison when generation is steered toward a target property (invalidity more frequent), testing whether the alarm features remain useful precisely when validity is scarce.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Validity labels from ESMFold/RDKit are in-silico proxies for wet-lab viability; claims concern model-defined structural validity and generation efficiency, not experimental function. 2) Early prediction may be easy for gross degenerate failures but hard for subtle ones; we stratify results by failure type and report where foresight is impossible. 3) SAE-feature alarms might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, sparsity, interpretability, and compute-frontier gains constitute the contribution—and we report this honestly. 4) Restart-based abort assumes generations are roughly i.i.d. in cost; for conditional generation restarts may correlate—mitigated by seed/prompt diversification and reported. 5) Aborting could bias the output distribution (collapse diversity); we explicitly measure diversity/novelty retention. 6) Requires generators with accessible intermediate activations, limiting scope to instrumentable open models. 7) Threshold tuning could overfit; we select thresholds on a held-out split and report frontier robustness across seeds.

Name: epistemic_selfsignal_design
Title: Does the Generator Know It's Guessing? An Internal Epistemic Self-Signal That Governs Design Quality in Scientific Generative Models
Short Hypothesis: Scientific sequence/graph generative models carry a compact, interpretable INTERNAL EPISTEMIC self-signal during generation that encodes how uncertain the model is about the object it is producing, and—mirroring the shared uncertainty/correctness circuits found in text LLMs (SCIURus)—this self-signal is causally SHARED with actual design quality: it fires low exactly when the finished object is novel/out-of-distribution and low-quality (unfoldable, invalid, off-property), it is better calibrated than output likelihood/perplexity, and steering it changes both the model's internal confidence and the true quality of generated designs together. We do NOT presume the text-LLM shared-circuit (SCIURus) result transfers; the PRIMARY contribution is to ADJUDICATE, in scientific generators, between a shared uncertainty/correctness circuit and a DISSOCIATION (uncertainty that merely tracks OOD-ness without predicting quality), using causal, specificity-controlled interventions, with the calibrated readout and the epistemic-gated controller as secondary payoffs.
Related Work: Two literatures meet for the first time. (1) Text-LLM internal-uncertainty work shows models 'know what they know': SCIURus (2025) finds factuality and uncertainty share the same circuits; 'Internal Causal Mechanisms Robustly Predict OOD Behaviors' (2025) shows causal internal features predict correctness under shift; 'Do I Know This Entity?' (2024) and P(IK)-probe work map self-knowledge features. ALL are in text and concern factual QA, not generation of scientific objects. (2) Scientific interpretability-of-generation (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; chemistry-LM SAEs 2025; single-cell SAEs 2024) discovers/steers features for TARGET PROPERTIES and never studies whether the generator internally represents its own epistemic uncertainty about the object it is building, nor whether that self-signal is causally tied to design quality. Molecular-OOD work (MOOD 2024) shows external PREDICTOR calibration collapses under covariate shift but says nothing about a GENERATOR's internal self-signal. No prior work (a) locates an internal epistemic self-signal inside a scientific generator, (b) tests whether it is a shared circuit with true design quality (the SCIURus phenomenon transferred to a new, high-stakes object class where quality is objectively verifiable), or (c) uses it as a calibrated, causally-validated confidence readout for design. This is distinct from all my prior proposals, which audit controllability of a specific property; here the object of study is the model's self-knowledge and its causal link to quality. Recent text-model evidence also reports DISSOCIATION between uncertainty and correctness representations; we therefore frame the contribution as adjudicating whether scientific generation patterns with the shared-circuit or the dissociated regime, rather than assuming either, and as isolating unique information beyond token entropy, length, and novelty distance that black-box confidence probes conflate.
Abstract: Generative models for proteins and molecules routinely emit confident-looking designs that are actually invalid, unfoldable, or property-wrong—especially in the novel, out-of-distribution regions where design is most valuable. In text language models, recent work shows that uncertainty and correctness are computed by shared internal circuits: the model 'knows what it knows.' We ask whether scientific generators possess an analogous internal epistemic self-signal during generation, whether it is causally and specifically shared with the true quality of the object being produced or merely tracks novelty, and whether it can serve as a calibrated confidence readout that output likelihood cannot. Using ESM-2 protein language models and a SMILES chemical language model with sparse autoencoders, we (1) LOCATE candidate epistemic self-signal features by probing intermediate activations for how novel/OOD and how ultimately-valid the object being generated is, verified by hard oracles (ESMFold pLDDT, pseudo-perplexity, RDKit-validity) and novelty measures (identity/Tanimoto to the training set); (2) test the SHARED-CIRCUIT hypothesis via causal ablation and patching—does perturbing the located self-signal move BOTH the model's internal confidence AND the true design quality together, as SCIURus finds for text?; (3) evaluate the self-signal as a CALIBRATED confidence readout, comparing its ability to flag low-quality/OOD designs against likelihood, perplexity, and a black-box activation probe; and (4) deploy it as an epistemic-gated generation controller that abstains or resamples on low-confidence designs, measuring valid-yield-per-compute. We adjudicate shared-circuit vs dissociation while controlling for token entropy, length, and novelty distance. If a specific, better-calibrated signal exists, a designer can triage candidates before expensive oracle/wet-lab checks (fewer oracle calls, higher top-k yield); if not, we show scientific generators do not 'know what they know', a safety-relevant null.
Experiments:
Shared setup (fixed once, reused below). MODELS (frozen): ESM-2 150M and 650M (proteins); a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~85M, MOSES-trained or public checkpoint). Frozen; only SAEs/probes trainable. SAEs: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka on the residual stream at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer (plus a second layer), width 16x, k=32, Adam lr 1e-3, ~40M activation tokens, seeds {0,1,2}; reconstruction accepted at fraction-variance-unexplained <=0.2. QUALITY oracles (hard): proteins -- ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity + non-degeneracy (foldable & valid); molecules -- RDKit-validity + SA + non-degeneracy. NOVELTY/OOD: identity/edit distance to nearest training protein (mmseqs2/BLAST) or Tanimoto nearest-neighbour distance to nearest training molecule. CORPUS: generate ~20,000 objects per model spanning in-distribution (typical sampling) and OOD (high-temperature, steered-off-mode, rare-scaffold-conditioned) regimes so quality and novelty both vary widely; split into probe-train / val / test at the CLUSTER level -- proteins by sequence-identity/family bands (mmseqs2 clusters), molecules by Bemis-Murcko scaffold / nearest-neighbour Tanimoto bands -- so near-duplicate generations cannot leak across splits (seed-only splitting is insufficient). Compute: two ESM-2 sizes + small SMILES LM + ESMFold on 1-2 GPUs, academic-feasible.

PRE-REGISTERED PRIMARY ENDPOINT: the causal, specificity-controlled coupling test (Experiment 2) -- a shared uncertainty/quality circuit is claimed only if the epistemic ablation moves internal confidence AND oracle quality together (coupling r >= 0.5, CI excluding 0) while matched-energy, reconstruction-preserving-null, and equally-sparse non-epistemic directions do NOT (|r| <= 0.2); calibration and controller are secondary. UNIQUE-INFORMATION control (applied throughout): every quality-prediction claim is re-tested with partial correlation controlling for token entropy, sequence/graph length, and novelty distance, so the self-signal must add information beyond these. Layer/feature selection uses a held-out model/layer with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the feature/layer grid to avoid cherry-picking. MID-GENERATION READOUT: for masked-infilling ESM-2, 'generation progress' is the fraction of positions unmasked along a fixed infilling schedule, and the self-signal is read from the partially-infilled activation at that fraction.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- a compact interpretable epistemic self-signal is decodable mid-generation): Tests that a small internal feature set predicts eventual quality and novelty before the object is finished. At generation-progress fractions {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}, probe SAE features and raw activations to predict (a) eventual design quality (valid vs invalid/low) and (b) novelty/OOD-ness, selecting a compact self-signal feature set by information-based selection. Decisive metric first: probe AUROC for eventual quality at each progress fraction (established BEFORE the object is complete), then R^2 for novelty, then whether the SAME features predict both (a first sign of sharing), against a raw-activation-probe baseline. Convincing: at progress <=0.5, quality AUROC >= 0.75 from a compact feature set (<=32 features) and the same set predicts novelty with AUROC >= 0.7. Undecidable band: quality AUROC in [0.6, 0.7) at 0.5 progress -> a self-signal exists but is weak/late; report, do not headline the "compact early" claim. Negative result (quality AUROC < 0.6 at all pre-completion fractions): no decodable epistemic self-signal exists -- a clean negative that scientific generators do not "know what they know", and H2-H4 are reported as not applicable.

Experiment 2 (H2 -- the self-signal is causally SHARED with true design quality, not merely correlated): Tests the shared-circuit prediction (SCIURus analog). Ablate/patch the located self-signal features and measure whether BOTH the internal confidence read-out (self-signal value / P(valid) probe) AND the TRUE finished-object oracle quality move together; conversely patch self-signal activations from high-confidence into low-confidence generations. Decisive metric first: confidence-quality COUPLING = correlation between the intervention-induced change in internal confidence and the change in oracle quality across a dose sweep; then specificity -- ablating a pure target-property feature must NOT move the epistemic signal, and random-direction, matched-energy, reconstruction-preserving-null, and equally-sparse non-epistemic controls must NOT couple confidence and quality. Convincing: coupling r >= 0.5 (CI excluding 0) under the epistemic ablation, patching high->low confidence raises BOTH internal confidence and oracle quality, and controls show coupling |r| <= 0.2 (specific). Undecidable band: coupling r in [0.2, 0.4) OR controls also show |r| in [0.2, 0.4) -> coupling present but not clearly specific; report as suggestive. Negative result (coupling |r| < 0.2, or controls couple as strongly): the signal is not a shared correctness circuit -- reported as a non-specific/absent result, distinguishing "detects novelty" from "predicts quality".

Experiment 3 (H3 -- the self-signal is better calibrated than output likelihood/perplexity, especially OOD): Tests calibration as a confidence read-out. Systems compared: intervention-free self-signal (read mid-generation) vs generation likelihood, pseudo-perplexity/token-entropy, RDKit/validity heuristics, and a black-box raw-activation probe. Decisive metric first: calibration ECE for flagging invalid/off-property/novel-but-broken designs, then AUROC, both STRATIFIED by novelty (in-distribution vs OOD tertiles). Convincing: in the OOD tertile the self-signal keeps ECE <= 0.1 and AUROC >= 0.75 while likelihood/perplexity degrade to AUROC <= 0.65 (a >= 0.1 AUROC advantage where output-side signals fail, mirroring predictor-calibration collapse on novel inputs). Undecidable band: OOD self-signal-minus-likelihood AUROC gap in [0.0, 0.05] -> no calibration advantage; report parity. Negative result (self-signal ECE > 0.2 OOD or no advantage over likelihood): the internal signal is not better calibrated -- the calibration contribution is withdrawn.

Experiment 4 (H4 -- gating/steering the self-signal changes true design quality; an epistemic-gated controller pays off): Tests that acting on the self-signal moves real quality and yields a usable controller. Deploy the self-signal as a generation-time gate (abstain/resample when internal confidence is low); sweep the threshold. Decisive metric first: valid+in-quality objects per unit compute (a valid-yield-per-compute frontier) vs run-to-completion, likelihood/perplexity gating, and a black-box-probe gate; then false-abort rate; then precision@k when the self-signal RANKS candidates for oracle evaluation (the practical triage use case); then diversity/novelty retention (guard against collapse to memorized in-distribution outputs). Convincing: the self-signal gate dominates likelihood gating on valid-yield-per-compute by >= 20% at matched false-abort rate, with novelty retention within 10% of run-to-completion. Undecidable band: valid-yield improvement in [5%, 20%) or novelty loss in [10%, 25%) -> a modest/costly controller; report the frontier. Negative result (improvement < 5% or novelty loss > 25%): gating on the self-signal does not help beyond output-side signals -- reported honestly; the phenomenon (Experiments 1-3) stands or falls on its own.

Experiment 5 (interpretation + robustness of H1-H4): Auto-label the self-signal features (max-activating partial generations -- do they fire on frustrated partial folds / chemically inconsistent prefixes?). Repeat across both domains, both ESM-2 sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, and two layers; report the fraction of cells where the self-signal, the shared-circuit coupling, and the OOD-calibration advantage replicate, and whether coupling weakens for subtle vs gross failures. A finding stable in <50% of cells is reported as regime-specific.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) In-silico quality oracles (ESMFold, RDKit) are proxies for wet-lab function; claims concern model-internal epistemic self-knowledge and design reliability, not experimental viability—stated explicitly. 2) The shared-circuit claim requires distinguishing genuine coupling from a trivial 'ablation breaks everything' artifact; we mitigate with random-direction and matched-property-feature controls, and a specificity test that property-feature ablation leaves the epistemic signal intact while epistemic-signal ablation couples confidence and quality—if coupling is non-specific, we report that as a negative result. We claim 'causally shared' only if effects are bidirectional, specific, and non-destructive across both models and domains; otherwise coupling is reported as correlational. 3) The self-signal may merely track OOD-ness rather than a genuine correctness representation; the novelty-stratified calibration test and the causal coupling test separate 'detects novelty' from 'predicts quality', and both are informative. 4) An internal SAE-based self-signal might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, interpretability (naming what the signal fires on), the shared-circuit causal finding, and the OOD-calibration/compute-saving payoff are the contributions, reported honestly. 5) Gating could bias outputs toward memorized in-distribution designs; we explicitly measure diversity/novelty retention. 6) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 7) If no shared, better-calibrated self-signal exists, that is a clean, publishable negative result establishing that scientific generators—unlike text LLMs—do NOT 'know what they know' about their own designs, a safety-relevant finding.

Name: infeasibility_frustration_features
Title: Confidently Impossible: Do Interpretable Features Reveal When a Scientific Generative Model Is Fulfilling a Physically Infeasible Design Spec?
Short Hypothesis: We define a new problem, INFEASIBILITY DETECTION for scientific design specs, distinct from factuality hallucination: when a multi-constraint specification is physically INFEASIBLE (no valid object can satisfy it), scientific generative models do not refuse or signal failure but confidently emit a plausible-looking object that silently violates exactly one constraint. We hypothesize the model internally represents the over-constraint: a compact set of interpretable sparse-autoencoder 'frustration' features fires specifically under infeasible specs, is causally involved in which constraint gets sacrificed, and yields an early, calibrated infeasibility alarm that output-side confidence signals (perplexity, constraint-satisfaction probability) and a constraint-only heuristic fail to provide. We keep four claims separable -- the objective feasibility labels, the silent-violation behavior, the internal frustration features, and the early alarm -- so each stands or falls on its own.
Related Work: SAE interpretability of scientific models (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; Steering PLMs/ASPO 2025; the antibody SAE 2025; ProtoMech 2026; Matryoshka SAEs on ESM2-3B 2025) discovers and steers features toward SATISFIABLE single or multiple properties, always assuming a valid target exists, and evaluates whether the property appears. Hallucination-detection SAE work in text/vision LMs (SSL 2025; 'Do I Know This Entity?' 2024) shows features can flag when a model lacks knowledge, but concerns fuzzy factuality, not physically-verifiable constraint infeasibility. Constraint-based design/steering (compositional steering; conditioned generation) presumes feasibility and reports average satisfaction, never asking what happens when the requested constraint set is CONTRADICTORY. No prior work (a) constructs graded feasible-vs-infeasible design specs for proteins/molecules with objective, physics-based feasibility labels, (b) shows models silently and confidently violate constraints under infeasible specs, or (c) identifies interpretable 'frustration/infeasibility' features that fire selectively and act as a calibrated early alarm. This reframes interpretability from a controllability tool into an epistemic-honesty/safety instrument for design, distinct from all my prior steering-focused proposals and from hallucination work in non-scientific domains. DELTA AT A GLANCE. vs hallucination-detection SAEs (SSL 2025; 'Do I Know This Entity?' 2024): they flag fuzzy factual uncertainty, whereas we flag physically-verifiable, over-constrained INFEASIBILITY with objective labels. vs constrained-generation/steering (compositional/conditioned design): they assume a feasible target and report average satisfaction, whereas we study what happens when the constraint set is CONTRADICTORY. Four separable novel contributions: (a) objective feasibility labels, (b) the silent-violation behavior, (c) interpretable frustration features, (d) the early calibrated alarm -- each evaluated independently so the failure of one does not sink the others.
Abstract: Scientific design increasingly means asking a generative model to satisfy several hard constraints at once, yet some constraint combinations are physically infeasible -- no valid protein or molecule can meet them (a compact fold with extreme surface-exposed hydrophobicity; a small molecule combining mutually exclusive substructure and property demands). We define a new problem, infeasibility detection for scientific design specs, and surface a safety-relevant behavior: rather than refusing, models confidently emit a fluent, plausible object that silently violates one constraint, and standard output-side confidence does not flag it. We then ask whether the model internally represents the infeasibility. Using ESM-2 protein language models and a SMILES chemical language model with sparse autoencoders (SAEs), we build formal feasibility ladders -- specs graded from clearly satisfiable to provably infeasible, with objective labels triangulated from three model-independent signals (natural co-occurrence support, structural-incompatibility rules, and long-budget oracle-search failure) and feasibility defined operationally and separately from mere rarity. We report four separable results: (1) the labeled ladders themselves; (2) the silent-violation behavior and the blindness of output-side confidence; (3) a compact set of interpretable 'frustration' features that fire specifically under infeasible specs, controlling for constraint identity, and are causally involved in which constraint is sacrificed; and (4) an early, calibrated mid-generation infeasibility alarm that beats perplexity, a constraint-satisfaction probe, and a constraint-only heuristic. A positive alarm supports a concrete workflow -- abort generation, reroute to constraint relaxation/repair, or flag the spec for human revision -- saving downstream synthesis and folding/validation compute. Adopters include design pipelines, active-learning and uncertainty-estimation groups, and safety auditors.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: ESM-2 at 150M and 650M parameters and a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~90M), all base weights frozen. SAEs: TopK (k=32, dictionary 16384) and Matryoshka on the mid-layer (60% depth) residual stream, trained on 200M activations, seeds {0,1}, FVU reported. Constraint evaluators (hard, non-model): proteins -- secondary-structure fraction (DSSP on ESMFold), GRAVY, net charge, molecular weight, motif presence (HMMER/regex); molecules -- RDKit logP, QED, ring/aromatic counts, functional-group SMARTS, molecular weight. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT>=0.6 + pseudo-perplexity within 1.5x baseline (proteins); RDKit-validity + SA<=6 (molecules). FEASIBILITY LADDERS: for 24 constraint pairs/triples per domain, a graded ladder from clearly feasible to provably infeasible, with objective labels triangulated from three model-independent signals -- (a) empirical joint co-occurrence support over a 1M-object natural corpus (spec outside joint support = candidate-infeasible), (b) SMARTS/structure-incompatibility rules (mutually exclusive substructures; protein structure-property conflicts such as >80% beta-sheet AND high solvent-exposed hydrophobicity), (c) an oracle-search control -- a genetic optimizer over sequences/molecules with a large fixed budget whose persistent failure corroborates infeasibility. Core claims are restricted to ladder rungs where all three signals agree; label confidence reported per rung. To validate the labels we add STRESS TESTS where oracle-search is known to fail for reasons OTHER than infeasibility (deceptive but satisfiable specs with tiny feasible basins; rugged-but-feasible landscapes); rungs where oracle-failure is not corroborated by signals (a)/(b) are excluded from infeasible labels. SAE frustration features are selected on a TRAIN set of constraint families, and all reported discrimination/alarm numbers are computed on HELD-OUT constraint families and spec instances to preclude leakage. Constraint steering uses property-feature and difference-of-means directions.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- Silent violation under infeasible specs, and output-side confidence is blind). Tests that as feasibility drops, models emit valid, fluent objects that violate exactly one constraint rather than refusing, and that output-side confidence does not track feasibility. Data/systems: steer generation toward each spec across all ladder rungs, 500 generations per rung; compare behavior across the feasibility gradient. Decisive metric (primary): SILENT-VIOLATION RATE = fraction of infeasible-spec generations that remain valid/fluent but violate exactly one constraint (vs refusing/degenerating), with the sacrificed-constraint identity tallied for systematicity; secondary: discrimination (AUROC) of output-side confidence (pseudo-perplexity, generation likelihood, a constraint-satisfaction probe) for true feasibility. Convincing positive: silent-violation rate >= 60% on all-signals-agree infeasible rungs AND output-side-confidence AUROC in [0.45, 0.60] (near chance). Decision band: silent-violation rate in [40%, 60%) means the behavior is common but not dominant -- reported as such; output-side AUROC in (0.60, 0.70] means output confidence is a weak-but-nonzero feasibility signal, tempering the "fail to provide" claim. Negative: silent-violation rate < 40% (models often refuse/degenerate) OR output-side AUROC > 0.70 (output confidence already flags infeasibility) refutes H1's framing and removes the need for an internal alarm.

Experiment 2 (H2 -- A compact set of frustration features fires specifically under infeasible specs). Tests that identifiable SAE features discriminate infeasible-vs-feasible specs while controlling for constraint identity (so they detect CONFLICT, not one property). Data: SAE features scored at multiple generation-progress fractions across the ladders. Systems: per-feature discrimination of infeasible-vs-feasible, computed WITHIN matched constraint identity, vs the best single-property feature as a baseline. Decisive metric: AUROC (and mutual information) of the top-m frustration-feature set for infeasibility, and its sparsity (how many features reach AUROC>=0.75). Convincing positive: a compact set (<= 20 features) reaches AUROC >= 0.80 for infeasibility while single-property-feature baselines stay <= 0.65 -- i.e. the signal is conflict-specific, not property-specific. Decision band: top-set AUROC in [0.65, 0.80) means partial internal representation of infeasibility -- reported as weak evidence; if the property-feature baseline also reaches >= 0.65 the features may track a single property, flagged as unresolved. Negative: no feature set exceeds AUROC 0.65 for infeasibility beyond the property baseline means the model does not compactly represent over-constraint, refuting H2.

Experiment 3 (H2 -- Frustration features are causal for conflict resolution). Tests that intervening on the frustration features changes the model's silent-violation behavior specifically. Data/systems: ablate the frustration-feature set and, separately, amplify it, vs random-direction and matched-single-property-feature controls, on infeasible-spec generations. Decisive metric: change in which constraint is sacrificed (shift rate) and in violation magnitude under ablation; change toward hedging/lower-confidence completions under amplification. Convincing positive: ablation shifts the sacrificed-constraint distribution or violation magnitude by an effect size >= 0.5 SD beyond both controls (CI excludes controls), establishing specificity. Decision band: effect in [0.2, 0.5) SD above controls is weak causal support -- reported as correlational-leaning. Negative: intervention indistinguishable from controls means the features are not causal for conflict resolution and the "model knows" claim reduces to a decodable correlate, reported honestly.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Early, calibrated infeasibility alarm beating output-side signals). Tests that the frustration-feature score read off mid-generation gives an earlier and better-calibrated infeasibility alarm than output-side confidence and a black-box probe. Data/systems: deploy the frustration-feature score at generation-progress fractions {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}; baselines -- partial perplexity/likelihood, a constraint-satisfaction probe on the partial object, a CONSTRAINT-ONLY HEURISTIC that predicts infeasibility from the requested constraint values alone (no model internals), and a black-box raw-activation probe. Decisive metric (primary): forecast AUROC for infeasibility vs generation progress, plus calibration ECE; secondary: earliest progress fraction at which AUROC>=0.80 (earliest-reliable-detection) and precision@k for flagging infeasible specs. Convincing positive: the frustration-feature alarm reaches AUROC>=0.80 by 50% progress with ECE<=0.10, beating output-side baselines by >= 0.10 AUROC at that progress point, with quantified compute saved by aborting infeasible requests before full generation + ESMFold/validation. Decision band: alarm AUROC in [0.70, 0.80) at 50% progress, or advantage over the black-box probe in [0.03, 0.10) AUROC, means the internal alarm works but its edge over cheaper signals is marginal -- reported with the interpretability/localization payoff as the differentiator. Negative: the frustration-feature alarm does not beat partial-perplexity/constraint-probe baselines (advantage <= 0.03 AUROC) means output-side signals suffice and the internal-alarm contribution collapses to interpretation only.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Feasibility labels are the crux and are imperfect: empirical co-occurrence support, SMARTS/structure incompatibility rules, and oracle-search failure are all in-silico proxies for true physical infeasibility. We mitigate by triangulating three independent signals and restricting core claims to specs where all three agree, and by reporting label-confidence-stratified results. 2) 'Infeasible' vs merely 'rare/hard' is a continuum; the oracle-search control and graded ladder are designed to separate genuinely impossible from hard-but-possible, but boundary cases will be noisy—reported explicitly. 3) In-silico validity/property evaluators (ESMFold, RDKit) are proxies for wet-lab truth; claims concern model-internal epistemic signals, not experimental viability. 4) Frustration features might merely track the individual conflicting properties rather than their conflict; the constraint-identity control in feature selection and the causal conflict-resolution test are designed to rule this out. 5) The internal alarm may not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, interpretability (localizing the conflict), calibration, and early detection are the contribution and are reported honestly. 6) If models turn out to reliably signal infeasibility via output confidence, that is still a valuable positive result about epistemic honesty in scientific generative models. 7) SAE quality/layer choice could confound; controlled via multiple SAE variants, layers, and difference-of-means baselines. 8) Negative-result reading: if a constraint-only heuristic or output-side confidence already predicts infeasibility well, the internal-alarm contribution is withdrawn and we report that practitioners can rely on those cheaper checks; if none suffices, the result establishes that explicit feasibility checking remains necessary before synthesis/validation.

Name: provenance_shortcut_steering
Title: Designing the Database, Not the Molecule: Do Interpretable Features Reveal That Steered Scientific Generators Chase Dataset Provenance Instead of Physics?
Short Hypothesis: When we steer a protein/molecule generative model toward a desired PHYSICAL property (e.g., high thermostability), the model frequently satisfies the target by moving along interpretable features that encode DATASET PROVENANCE (source organism, protein family, structural-database membership, assay batch) rather than the underlying physics. The apparent property gain is a shortcut: it reproduces the provenance signature correlated with the property in the training data, and interpretable features expose this so we can detect it and steer against it.
Related Work: Prior pLM-SAE work (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; 'From Mechanistic Interpretability to Mechanistic Biology' 2025; functional-annotation SAE work 2025) repeatedly finds that pLMs represent proteins via a mix of generic biophysical features AND strong 'family-specific'/organism-specific features, and steering studies add a target property by moving along whatever feature correlates with it. Separately, data-leakage and batch-effect work ('Beware of Data Leakage from Protein LLM Pretraining' 2024; thermostability leakage; batch-effect correction literature) shows downstream property predictors are inflated by provenance confounds. Recent critical work ('Dead Salmons of AI Interpretability' 2025; 'Automated Interpretability Metrics Do Not Distinguish Trained and Random Transformers' 2025; single-cell FM interpretability 2026 finding attention captures co-expression not causal signal) warns that interpretable-looking signals may be spurious. NO prior work connects these: no one asks whether interpretable-feature STEERING for design achieves property gains by exploiting provenance-artifact features rather than causal physics, quantifies how often this happens, or uses interpretability to disentangle a provenance-shortcut direction from a physics direction. This is distinct from all my prior proposals (compositionality, off-mode reach, steerability prediction, leakage, reliability collapse), which all assumed the property gain, when achieved, is legitimate. EXPLICIT NOVELTY CLAIMS: (1) generation-time provenance shortcuting (a GENERATOR shifts provenance to hit a property), distinct from prior leakage work on inflated PREDICTORS; (2) interpretability-mediated ATTRIBUTION of the shortcut to specific feature directions; (3) a provenance-shortcut score predicting design degeneration; (4) provenance-invariant steering as a fix, validated by a planted-shortcut positive control. Closest baselines by name: standard feature steering, random-direction steering, supervised provenance classifiers, projection/adversarial debiasing, and leakage-aware evaluation. Affected communities: protein design, molecular generation, interpretability, and ML-for-science benchmarking; the audit is intended as a reporting checklist.
Abstract: Steering interpretable features is the standard way to make protein and molecule generators produce a desired physical property, with success judged by a property predictor. We surface a generation-time phenomenon distinct from known dataset-leakage effects (which concern inflated PREDICTORS): a GENERATOR can satisfy a physical-property target by shifting the DATASET PROVENANCE of its output -- source organism, protein family, structural-database subset, or assay batch that co-occurs with the property in training -- rather than its physics, and interpretability lets us attribute the shortcut to specific feature directions. Training sparse autoencoders on ESM-2 and a SMILES chemical LM, we operationally separate physics-aligned directions (property correlation surviving provenance stratification) from provenance-aligned directions (high mutual information with provenance labels), predefining properties where family is plausibly causal versus clearly non-causal so the shortcut is isolable. We test three claims with pre-registered decision rules: (1) standard steering moves substantially along provenance features (a provenance-subspace displacement fraction), and its gain shrinks under a provenance-controlled oracle (a spurious-gain metric); (2) a per-generation provenance-shortcut score predicts a designer-relevant failure -- outputs collapse onto one provenance group and lose novelty, a wasted-screening cost; and (3) orthogonalizing the steering direction against provenance features preserves genuine, controlled-oracle gain while restoring novelty, validated by a synthetic planted-shortcut positive control. Baselines include standard and random-direction steering, supervised provenance classifiers, and projection-based debiasing. We deliver a provenance-shortcut audit -- usable as a reporting checklist for protein-design, molecular-generation, interpretability, and ML-for-science benchmarking -- that separates designing-the-molecule from designing-the-database. The primary high-stakes setting is protein thermostability, where a provenance shortcut wastes expensive stability screening.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: ESM-2 at 150M and 650M parameters (proteins) and a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~90M), base weights frozen. SAEs: TopK (k=32, dictionary 16384) and Matryoshka on the mid-layer (60% depth) residual stream, trained on 200M activations, seeds {0,1}, FVU reported. Target PHYSICAL properties with cheap evaluators: proteins -- thermostability proxy (fine-tuned head), GRAVY, secondary-structure fraction (DSSP on ESMFold); molecules -- logP, a solubility proxy, QED. PROVENANCE labels per training object: proteins -- source organism/taxon, Pfam family, PDB/CATH structural-database membership; molecules -- source assay/dataset (ChEMBL target/document id), scaffold class. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT>=0.6 + pseudo-perplexity within 1.5x baseline (proteins); RDKit-validity + SA<=6 (molecules). Steering budget in normalized activation-norm units; SAE-feature, difference-of-means, and norm-matched random-direction interventions. ~8 property x domain settings; 500 generations per condition. FEASIBILITY/DATA: SAEs trained on ~200M activations (~1-2 GPU-days each on one A100); provenance metadata coverage -- proteins: organism/taxon and Pfam family for >95% of training objects, PDB/CATH membership for the structured subset; molecules: ChEMBL assay/document id and Bemis-Murcko scaffold for the full training set. We PREDEFINE, per property, whether provenance is plausibly CAUSAL (e.g., family-defining catalytic motifs) or clearly NON-CAUSAL-but-correlated (e.g., thermostability co-occurring with thermophile source), and analyze the two groups separately; the primary high-stakes property is protein thermostability. Layer (60% depth) and dictionary size (16384) are fixed a priori, with robustness to both reported as an ablation. A feature is called provenance-aligned only by a pre-registered rule (provenance mutual information above, and provenance-stratified property partial-correlation below, fixed thresholds) to avoid post hoc labeling.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- Features split into physics-aligned vs provenance-aligned, and standard steering rides provenance). Tests that standard property steering moves substantially along provenance-encoding features. Data: per SAE feature compute correlation with the target property and mutual information with provenance labels over 2,000 held-out natural objects; partition into provenance-aligned (high provenance MI), physics-aligned (property correlation surviving provenance stratification / partial correlation), and mixed. Systems compared: standard steering via best-property-correlated SAE feature and difference-of-means direction vs a norm-matched random direction; decompose the steering displacement onto provenance vs physics feature subspaces. Decisive metric (primary): PROVENANCE-SUBSPACE DISPLACEMENT FRACTION = share of the steering displacement lying in the provenance subspace. Convincing positive: displacement fraction >= 0.4 (median over settings) and clearly above the random-direction control's incidental overlap. Decision band: fraction in [0.2, 0.4) means steering partially rides provenance -- reported as a contributing, not dominant, shortcut. Negative: fraction < 0.2 (steering stays in the physics subspace) refutes H1 for that property -- a valuable positive result that steering targets physics, not database artifacts.

Experiment 2 (H2 -- The gain is spurious: it shrinks under a provenance-controlled oracle). Tests that the property gain scored by a provenance-decorrelated oracle is much smaller than by the naive predictor. Data/systems: for each steered generation, score property gain by (i) the naive predictor and (ii) a PROVENANCE-CONTROLLED oracle -- a predictor trained on a provenance-balanced/decorrelated split and/or an independent physics evaluator (FoldX/Rosetta-style stability; a second empirical logP model) that ignores provenance. Decisive metric (primary): SPURIOUS GAIN = naive-minus-controlled property-gain gap, as a fraction of the naive gain. Convincing positive: spurious gain >= 40% of naive gain (median, CI excludes 0) and correlated with the provenance-displacement fraction from Experiment 1 (Spearman rho>=0.5). Decision band: spurious gain in [15%, 40%) means part of the gain is real physics -- reported as a partial shortcut. Negative: spurious gain < 15% (controlled oracle largely confirms the naive gain) refutes H2 -- the gain reflects physics, and the shortcut account is withdrawn for that property.

Experiment 3 (H2/H3 -- The shortcut predicts designer-relevant failure). Tests that high-shortcut steering yields provenance-collapsed, low-novelty designs. Data/systems: per steered generation compute a provenance-shortcut score (share of gain attributable to provenance movement) and measure provenance clustering (collapse toward one organism/family/scaffold group in embedding space), novelty (identity/Tanimoto to nearest training object), and set diversity; regress these on the shortcut score. Decisive metric: Spearman rho / R^2 between shortcut score and provenance-collapse and novelty-loss. Convincing positive: rho >= 0.5 (CI excludes 0) for both collapse and novelty-loss -- the shortcut is a usable predictor of degenerate design. Decision band: rho in [0.3, 0.5) is a weak predictor -- reported with its error. Negative: rho <= 0.3 means the shortcut score does not forecast design degeneration, so its practical value is limited even if H1/H2 hold.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Provenance-invariant steering fixes it; positive control validates the pipeline). Tests that orthogonalizing the steering direction against provenance features preserves genuine (controlled-oracle) gain while restoring novelty and reducing collapse, and that the whole detection/fix pipeline recovers a known planted shortcut. Data/systems: (a) construct a debiased direction by projecting the property direction off the provenance subspace (Gram-Schmidt), compare provenance-invariant vs standard steering at matched displacement on controlled-oracle gain, provenance-collapse, novelty, validity; (b) POSITIVE CONTROL -- relabel a subset so a property artificially co-occurs with a tag, confirm the pipeline recovers the planted shortcut and the fix removes it. Decisive metrics: change in controlled-oracle gain and in novelty/collapse from invariant vs standard steering; and planted-shortcut recovery rate in the positive control.
