Decisive metric (primary): fraction of generations simultaneously oracle-property-satisfying, valid, and reliable (trustworthy yield), and trustworthy-yield-per-unit-compute; secondary: diversity/novelty retention and compute saved by not validating untrustworthy designs. Convincing positive: reliability-gating raises trustworthy yield by >= 20% relative to validity-only gating at equal or lower compute, without collapsing diversity (novelty retained within 10% of ungated). Decision band: improvement in [5%, 20%) is a modest, reported gain; improvement that comes only with a large diversity loss (>10%) is reported as a trade, not a free lunch. Negative: reliability-gating gives <= 5% trustworthy-yield improvement over validity-only gating, meaning the reliability axis adds no practical control value beyond existing checks.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The independent oracle (FoldX/Rosetta/second logP model/docking) is itself an in-silico proxy; the trustworthiness claim rests on DISAGREEMENT between two independent in-silico signals stratified by reliability, not wet-lab truth—stated explicitly. 2) The reliability score could merely correlate with off-distribution-ness rather than causing untrustworthy property claims; we mitigate by (a) validating it on natural objects with known coverage and (b) the reliability-stratified oracle test that ties low reliability to predictor failure, and by random-direction controls. 3) An internal SAE-based reliability score might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, interpretability (naming which features decohere) and the frontier/compute gains are the contribution and are reported honestly. 4) Reliability collapse might be trivially entangled with validity collapse; the core test specifically isolates the regime where objects remain valid and predictor-satisfying yet unreliable, and reports the gap—if no such gap exists, that is itself a clean, publishable negative result. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound both steering and reliability; controlled via multiple SAE variants, layers, and difference-of-means baselines. 6) In-silico property/validity evaluators are proxies; claims concern model-internal representational trustworthiness of controlled designs, not experimental function. 7) Generalization: we report whether a single reliability threshold and controller transfer across properties, model sizes, and the two modalities, rather than assuming universality; a threshold that must be re-fit per setting is reported as such.

Name: epistasis_steering_blindspot
Title: Levers for Positions, Not for Couplings: Can Interpretable Features Causally Control Epistasis in Protein Language Models?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable sparse-autoencoder features of protein language models give causal, steerable control over SINGLE-POSITION (additive) sequence properties, but we hypothesize they do NOT give control over EPISTASIS—the context-dependent coupling that makes one position's optimal residue depend on another. No prior work has tested causal steering of epistatic-coupling features in pLM SAEs. We commit to ONE primary hypothesis with ONE fallback: steering a feature to install a desired coupling (a compensatory pair, an allosteric/functional linkage) silently changes additive properties while the intended coupling fails to form—an 'epistasis blind spot' that single-mutant checks miss but a double-mutant-cycle oracle exposes (primary); the fallback is that coupling is only WEAKLY steerable relative to additive control. Whichever holds, the audit contribution stands: an internal coupling-consistency signal flags silently-uncoupled designs, telling engineers to run double-mutant-cycle checks before synthesis. We keep 'scientific phenomenon discovery' (is coupling a steerable object?) separate from 'design utility' (can we make couplings on demand?), so the result is informative even where the wet-lab oracle is imperfect.
Related Work: pLM interpretability/steering work (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; Steering PLMs/ASPO 2025; antibody-SAE 2025; ProtoMech 2026; Automated Neuron Labelling 2025; SAEs for low-N design 2025) discovers and steers features that all encode INTRINSIC, single-position or local-motif properties (secondary structure, GRAVY, molecular weight, zinc-finger motifs, thermostability) and evaluate whether that standalone property appears. Separately, a distinct biology literature establishes that pLMs INTERNALLY capture epistasis: ESM-2 stores coevolving-residue statistics like a Markov Random Field (Zhang et al. 2024), pLMs capture both structural-contact and long-range FUNCTIONAL couplings zero-shot (2025), and higher-order epistasis is present in sequence-function models (2024). Crucially, no work connects these: none asks whether the epistatic/coupling structure pLMs demonstrably represent is a CAUSALLY STEERABLE design lever, contrasts coupling-steerability against single-position steerability, or audits when a designer's coupling request silently fails. This distinguishes the proposal from all single-property steering work (which assumes an additive target) and from the epistasis-probing literature (which is purely descriptive/predictive, never touching feature-level steering of generation). Epistasis is the ideal testbed because it has an exact, well-established quantitative oracle — the double-mutant cycle (epistasis = ddG_AB - ddG_A - ddG_B) computable from deep mutational scanning (DMS) data or in-silico stability predictors. Compact contrast: [additive-property steering] InterPLM/ProtSAE/Steering-PLMs/antibody-SAE—steer single-position/local-motif traits, evaluate standalone appearance; [descriptive epistasis probing] Zhang 2024 (ESM-2 as MRF), zero-shot coupling capture 2025, higher-order epistasis 2024—show couplings are REPRESENTED but never intervene; [THIS proposal] causal feature-STEERING of couplings, contrasted head-to-head with additive steering and audited. The nearest baselines for coupling control (categorical-Jacobian reads, coevolution statistics) are PREDICTIVE, not generative interventions, so they do not imply steerability. Who would use it: protein designers (compensatory/allosteric design), SAE/interpretability researchers (limits of feature steering), and model-audit practitioners. We keep the scientific question (is coupling a steerable object?) separate from design utility (can couplings be installed on demand?) so the contribution survives an imperfect wet-lab oracle. Deliverable: a coupling-steering audit protocol and a labeled additive-vs-coupling steering benchmark.
Abstract: A protein's function is shaped not only by which residue sits at each position but by epistasis: the coupling that makes the best residue at one position depend on another, underlying compensatory mutations, allosteric linkages, and folding cooperativity. Interpretability-guided design steers language-model features to install properties, and pLMs are known to internally capture epistatic couplings—yet every demonstrated steering target is an additive, single-position property. No prior work has tested causal steering of epistatic-coupling features in pLM SAEs. We ask a minimal, defensible question: can interpretable features causally control epistasis, or only additive traits? Our one primary hypothesis, with a single fallback, is that additive control succeeds while coupling control is at best weakly steerable—an 'epistasis blind spot': steering to install a target coupling (a compensatory pair, a contact-based or long-range functional linkage) reliably shifts additive properties while the intended coupling fails to form, invisible to single-mutant checks but exposed by a double-mutant-cycle oracle. Epistasis is uniquely suited because it is exactly quantifiable (epsilon = ddG_AB - ddG_A - ddG_B) from combinatorial deep-mutational-scanning data. Using ESM-2 with TopK and Ordered sparse autoencoders, we LOCATE additive and coupling features, CAUSALLY contrast their steerability, quantify the blind spot, and AUDIT whether an internal coupling-consistency signal flags silently-uncoupled designs. The concrete workflow change if the blind spot holds: engineers steering pLMs should audit couplings with double-mutant-cycle-style checks before synthesis. Either result is publishable—a steerable coupling handle would directly enable compensatory/allosteric design; a clean negative, replicated across models and oracles, delimits what feature-steering can control.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (FROZEN): ESM-2 (150M and 650M); generation by masked infilling. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered SAEs (Ordered can recover steerability TopK lacks), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M residual-stream activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. ADDITIVE oracles: single-mutant effect on GRAVY, net charge, and a stability proxy (fine-tuned ddG head or FoldX), plus ESM-2 single-mutant log-likelihood. EPISTASIS oracle (exact operational definition): the double-mutant-cycle term epsilon = ddG_AB - ddG_A - ddG_B, taken from combinatorial deep-mutational-scanning (DMS) landscapes with measured double mutants - GB1 (Olson 2014, ~535,000 double mutants) plus 2-3 further combinatorial-DMS landscapes from ProteinGym-style resources - and from FoldX for position pairs not experimentally covered; the pLM categorical-Jacobian gives an internal pairwise-coupling read. In-silico epsilon is validated against measured doubles on the DMS-covered subset and strong claims restricted to where they agree. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity. First confirm the model natively spans a meaningful RANGE of couplings. Steering = add alpha*d_hat during infilling; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - single-position (additive) features are causally steerable): Identify additive features (correlate with a single position's property, controlling for context; probe AUROC/R^2) and steer to raise a target additive property (e.g., GRAVY) at a chosen position. Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: on-target additive effect size (Cohen's d, steered vs unsteered, within the validity budget). Decision band: d >= 0.8 AND >= 0.4 over control for >=2/3 of features => additive control genuine (H1 holds); [0.2,0.4) over control => inconclusive; < 0.2 => not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - epistasis is decodable-but-not-steerable, and steering to install a coupling silently changes additive properties while the coupling fails to form): (a) DECODABILITY: probe the pairwise epistasis magnitude / categorical-Jacobian coupling of a position pair, controlling for the two positions' additive effects via partial correlation; AUROC. (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: steer the best coupling direction (TopK/Ordered SAE feature, difference-of-means high-vs-low-coupling, activation-patching from strongly-coupled sequences, additive-orthogonalized direction) to install a target epistasis at a position pair while holding the two positions' additive contributions fixed. Decisive metrics FIRST: SILENT-DECOUPLING RATE = fraction of coupling-steered, valid sequences whose double-mutant-cycle epsilon did not form (|Delta epsilon| below oracle noise) or formed wrong-sign while additive properties shifted; and ratio r = coupling efficacy / additive efficacy from Experiment 1. Decision band: coupling decodable (AUROC >= 0.70) AND r <= 0.33 AND decoupling >= 0.30 => epistasis blind spot confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial (test Ordered SAEs); r >= 0.67 => a steerable epistasis handle exists, refuting H2 (equally publishable).

Experiment 3 (H3 - single-mutant checks miss the failure but the exact double-mutant-cycle oracle exposes it): For the Experiment-2 sequences, compare what a practitioner would inspect against ground truth. Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between the additive-property change / single-mutant scores / pseudo-perplexity and the true change in double-mutant-cycle epsilon. Decision band: |rho| <= 0.20 => single-mutant checks are blind to the coupling failure while the double-mutant-cycle oracle reveals it (H3 confirmed); |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial visibility; |rho| >= 0.40 => single-mutant checks already flag it (weakens the blind-spot framing). ROBUSTNESS: two model sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, contact-based (short-range) vs long-range functional couplings; test whether steerability is worse long-range than for contacts; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.

PRE-REGISTERED DEFINITIONS. 'Steerability' of a coupling = on-target |Delta epsilon| exceeding oracle noise AND correct sign at the alpha maximizing on-target change within the validity budget; 'blind spot' = single-mutant/pseudo-perplexity checks show |rho| <= 0.20 with true Delta epsilon while the double-mutant-cycle oracle shows the coupling failed. DMS SELECTION & COUNTS: primary landscape GB1 (Olson 2014, ~535k doubles); add 2-3 combinatorial-DMS landscapes with measured doubles from ProteinGym-style resources; test >=200 position pairs per landscape spanning weak/strong |epsilon|; estimate oracle noise from DMS replicate variance. We SEPARATE claims measured on real DMS doubles from FoldX-derived claims (FoldX used only where doubles are experimentally uncovered, reported separately).

ADDED CONTROLS: random SAE directions, matched-activation-norm directions, single-mutant-only targets (should show no coupling), and a black-box raw-activation probe/edit baseline. ABLATION (indirection test): verify apparent coupling steering is not merely indirect movement on additive traits or sequence likelihood—regress Delta epsilon on the induced additive shifts and on Delta log-likelihood; genuine coupling control must survive this partialling-out. CAUSAL vs PREDICTIVE internal signal: the audit signal is validated by INTERVENTION (does raising the coupling-probe read actually raise measured epsilon?), not correlation alone.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Epistasis has an exact operational definition (double-mutant cycle), but its measurement relies on either DMS data (limited combinatorial double-mutant coverage) or in-silico stability predictors (FoldX/Rosetta), which are proxies; we validate in-silico epistasis against measured double mutants on the DMS-covered subset and restrict strong claims to where they agree, framing claims as model-internal, oracle-verified coupling controllability rather than wet-lab function. 2) The coupling-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK and Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching, additive-orthogonalized directions), sweeping strength, requiring the model to natively span an epistasis range, and head-to-head calibrating that ADDITIVE features ARE steerable in the same pipeline — so a null coupling result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable epistasis handle) is equally publishable and directly enables compensatory/allosteric design. 3) Additive and epistatic effects are partly entangled; the partial-correlation feature selection and additive-matched dissociation pairs (step 5) isolate genuinely additive-independent coupling signal, and we report where separation is impossible. 4) Double-mutant-cycle evaluation is combinatorially heavier than single-mutant checks; we cap position pairs and use the internal audit precisely to reduce this cost. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes (categorical Jacobian), and random-direction controls. 6) An internal coupling probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (additive-steerable, epistasis-decodable-but-weakly-steerable) and the audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If coupling steering unexpectedly succeeds, it overturns the hypothesis but yields a strong positive finding that pLM epistasis is a controllable design lever.

Name: locality_count_generalization_design
Title: More Motifs Than Ever Seen: Does Conditional Score Locality Govern Count Generalization in Scientific Generative Design?
Short Hypothesis: Scientific generative models can design objects with MORE independent functional elements (motifs, catalytic sites, functional groups) than appeared in any training example ('count generalization') only when their internal conditional computation is LOCAL — i.e., each element's placement depends on a spatially/sequentially sparse neighborhood rather than the global configuration. We hypothesize (i) count generalization succeeds or fails per model/property, (ii) an intervention-free locality signature of the element-placement feature predicts which case holds, and (iii) causally enforcing locality (masking non-local dependencies of the placement feature) unlocks count generalization that a non-local model otherwise fails, at preserved validity. PRIMARY CLAIM: the causal locality-enforcement test on the masked-diffusion generator (H3); the novelty is the TRANSFER of the diffusion locality<->generalization theory into scientific sequence/graph design plus its mechanistic validation, not a new theory of locality.
Related Work: A recent line proves that compositional/length generalization in conditional diffusion models is equivalent to 'local conditional scores' (sparse pixel and conditioner dependencies) and shows a causal locality intervention restores length generalization in CLEVR/image models (Local Mechanisms of Compositional Generalization, 2025; Kamb & Ganguli 2024; Niedoba 2024). Compositional-generalization theory (kernel theory 2024; identifiability/object-centric 2023; complexity-based compositionality 2024) and disentanglement-for-C-OoD work (CLIP 2024, data-diversity 2025) all study this in vision/text. Separately, scientific-model interpretability (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; ProtoMech 2026; Circuits/Features/Heuristics in Molecular Transformers 2025) discovers and steers features for single-element properties but NEVER studies count generalization, never measures conditional-score locality, and never tests locality as its causal mechanism. My prior proposals audit compositional INTERFERENCE and off-mode reach but assume a fixed target count and never touch the locality-count-generalization link. This proposal is the first to (a) transfer the locality<->count-generalization theory into scientific sequence/graph design, (b) measure conditional locality of interpretable element-placement features, and (c) causally enforce locality to unlock designs exceeding training element counts — a Location + Causal Intervention mechanism claim in a high-stakes domain. Exact delta from the CLEVR result: prior work showed locality governs how many OBJECTS an image model can compose; we test whether the same locality principle governs how many independent FUNCTIONAL elements (catalytic sites, binding motifs, functional groups) a protein/molecule generator can pack beyond its training-count support -- nontrivial because scientific elements are discrete, oracle-countable, and often physically coupled rather than spatially separable pixels. We contrast prior work vs this proposal on five axes -- domain (vision -> protein/chemistry), object type (pixels -> sequences/graphs), locality signal (pixel-conditioner sparsity -> element-placement-feature receptive field), intervention (image-score masking -> denoiser feature masking), and outcome (image length generalization -> valid over-count design). Concrete qualitatively-different tasks: a protein with MORE tandem catalytic-triad-like motifs than any training protein, and a molecule with MORE independent halogen/hydroxyl decorations than any training molecule -- copy-count extrapolation against hard structural oracles, not spatial object counting.
Abstract: Real scientific design frequently demands packing MORE independent functional elements into one object than nature or the training set ever showed: an enzyme with several catalytic sites, a protein with multiple binding motifs, a molecule with many decorated functional groups. Whether generative models can do this — 'count generalization' — and why, is unknown. Recent theory for conditional diffusion proves that compositional/length generalization is equivalent to conditional score LOCALITY: each element's placement depending on a sparse local neighborhood rather than the global configuration. We transfer this theory into scientific design and test it mechanistically. Using protein language models (ESM-2), a SMILES chemical language model, and a masked-diffusion protein/molecule generator with sparse autoencoders, we (1) LOCATE interpretable element-placement features (features that fire when a motif/functional group is instantiated) and measure their CONDITIONAL LOCALITY — how sparsely each placement depends on distant positions/other elements, via ablation of distal context and Jacobian sparsity; (2) establish the count-generalization PHENOMENON by requesting objects with k functional elements for k beyond the training-count support and measuring valid success against hard oracles (HMMER/regex motifs, RDKit SMARTS); (3) TEST the hypothesis that locality predicts count-generalization success across models/properties; and (4) CAUSALLY ENFORCE locality — masking the placement feature's non-local dependencies during generation — and test whether it unlocks higher-count valid designs that the unmodified (non-local) model fails, at preserved validity. Beyond a probe, the payoff is a phenomenon-level rule for when repeated-element extrapolation works plus a cheap locality-masking recipe (primary endpoint: the causal test on the masked-diffusion generator) that converts otherwise-failed high-count generations into valid designs and cuts wasted sampling for protein and molecular designers.
Experiments:
Shared setup (fixed once, reused below). MODELS (frozen): ESM-2 150M and 650M (proteins); a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~85M, MOSES-trained or public checkpoint); and, for the causal locality intervention that needs per-step conditional scores, a masked-diffusion generator with accessible per-step activations -- a discrete diffusion protein LM (DPLM/EvoDiff-style, public) and a masked discrete-diffusion molecule model (DiGress/masked-SMILES-style). All generators FROZEN; only SAEs/probes trainable. SAEs: TopK on residual-stream / denoiser activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer (plus a second layer), width 16x, k=32, Adam lr 1e-3, ~40M activation tokens, seeds {0,1,2}; reconstruction accepted at fraction-variance-unexplained <=0.2. ELEMENT oracles (exact, countable): proteins -- discrete motif instances (zinc fingers, catalytic-triad-like motifs, specified short motifs) via HMMER/regex, counted per sequence; molecules -- functional-group instances via specified SMARTS (hydroxyls, halogens, aromatic rings), counted per molecule. VALIDITY gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity (proteins), RDKit-validity + SA (molecules). PRECONDITION: from the training corpus, record the DISTRIBUTION of element counts per object (the training-count support and its max), so "beyond training count" is well-defined per element type. Compute: two ESM-2 sizes + small SMILES LM + two public diffusion generators on 1-2 GPUs, academic-feasible.

PRE-REGISTERED PRIMARY ENDPOINT: the causal locality-enforcement gain (Experiment 4) on the masked-diffusion generator for ONE protein element (a specified short catalytic-triad-like motif) and ONE molecule element (halogen decoration); all other models/elements/layers are secondary robustness. Every experiment's success/undecidable/negative bands below are fixed before running. CONFOUND CONTROLS analyzed explicitly: training data-count diversity, sequence/graph length, motif rarity, and element independence are recorded per (model, element) and entered as covariates so the locality<->boundary link is tested above them.

Experiment 0 (pipeline validation on a synthetic benchmark): Before the scientific runs, validate the locality-measurement and locality-enforcement code on a synthetic countable-element sequence task with a KNOWN local generative process (elements placed by a fixed sparse rule), confirming the locality score recovers the planted radius and that enforcement restores over-count generation; a pipeline failing here is fixed before any protein/molecule claim.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- count generalization succeeds or fails, per model and property): Tests that some (model, element) pairs generate valid objects with MORE independent elements than any training example while others break down. Data: for each element type, request k elements for k spanning within-support up to beyond the training-max count, via three elicitation methods (count-conditioned prompting, iterative element insertion, feature-steered placement); generate 300 objects per k. Decisive metric first: VALID-COUNT-SUCCESS(k) = fraction of generations containing EXACTLY k valid, correctly-formed elements AND passing validity gates; then the count-generalization BOUNDARY = largest k with valid-success >= 0.5, normalized by training-max count; then the SILENT-COUNT-FAILURE profile (wrong count / degenerate / invalid). Random-count and unconditioned controls. Convincing existence of both regimes: at least one (model, element) pair has boundary/training-max >= 1.2 (genuine extrapolation) and at least one has boundary/training-max <= 1.0 (breakdown), each with valid-success curves separated from the unconditioned control. Undecidable band: boundary/training-max in [1.0, 1.2) -> extrapolation not clearly beyond training support; report as "at-support", not generalization. Negative result (no pair exceeds 1.0): no count generalization anywhere -- H2/H3 become vacuous; reported as a null with the failure profile.

Experiment 2 (locate element-placement features and measure their conditional locality): Prerequisite measurement for H2/H3. Identify SAE features that fire at the instantiation of each target element (concept-correlation / probe AUROC on held-out objects, localized to the element positions; retain features with AUROC >= 0.7). For each placement feature compute a LOCALITY score from (a) distal-context ablation -- change in the feature's activation / placement decision when distant positions and other already-placed elements are ablated/shuffled (local features barely change), and (b) Jacobian sparsity -- the spatial/sequential decay profile of the placement-logit gradient (a locality radius). Operationally the distal-ablation score is 1 - (mean |Delta placement-logit| under ablation of positions beyond radius r) / (mean |Delta placement-logit| under ablation of all context), and the Jacobian radius is the smallest r capturing >= 90% of the total |d placement-logit / d input| mass; the per-feature locality score is reported with its exact r. Decisive metric: per-feature locality score with test-retest reliability across seeds >= 0.7 (else the score is too noisy to use as a predictor and is reported as such).

Experiment 3 (H2 -- an intervention-free locality signature predicts which pairs generalize): Tests that locality predicts the count-generalization boundary. Across element types, models, and two layers, regress the normalized boundary (Experiment 1) on the placement feature's locality score (Experiment 2). Decisive metric first: Spearman rho / out-of-sample R^2 of boundary on locality, compared against concept-correlation and single-element steerability baselines (nested-model comparison), then reported per-property and pooled. Convincing: higher locality predicts larger boundary with |rho| >= 0.5 and adds >= 0.1 R^2 over both baselines, CIs excluding 0. Undecidable band: |rho| in [0.2, 0.4) or added-R^2 in [0.03, 0.1) -> weak predictor; report coefficients, withhold the claim. Negative result (|rho| < 0.2, added-R^2 < 0.03): locality does not track count generalization -- an informative refutation pointing to an alternative cause (e.g., data-count diversity), reported with whatever does correlate.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- causally enforcing locality unlocks count generalization a non-local model otherwise fails): The mechanism test, run on the masked-diffusion generator (conditional scores directly accessible). Pick a (model, element) pair that FAILS count generalization (Experiment 1) and whose placement feature is measured NON-local (Experiment 2). Intervene: at each denoising step, mask the placement feature's dependence on distal positions / other-element features, restricting its effective receptive field to the measured local radius. Decisive metric first: count-generalization gain = increase in valid-count-success beyond the training-max count vs the unmodified model, then validity retention, then whether the radius that works matches the Location-measured radius. Controls: enforcing locality on a random non-placement feature (should not help), a model already local (should be unaffected), matched-norm random masking. Convincing: valid-count-success beyond training-max rises by >= 0.2 absolute over the unmodified model at validity retained within 5% of baseline, controls show no such gain, and the effective radius matches the measured one within a factor of 2. Undecidable band: gain in [0.05, 0.2) absolute OR validity drop in [5%, 15%) -> partial/costly unlock; report the count-vs-validity frontier. Negative result (gain < 0.05 or validity drop > 15%): enforcing locality does not unlock generalization -- refutes the causal claim; report whether the failure is implementation fidelity (measured and stated) or genuine.

Experiment 5 (robustness / boundary of H2-H3): Repeat across both domains, both ESM-2 sizes, autoregressive vs masked-diffusion generation, and >=3 element types, stratifying by element independence (well-separated vs coupled elements). Report where locality<->count-generalization holds vs breaks, the fraction of cells replicating, and whether the link is stronger for physically independent elements (where non-locality is not required) than coupled ones. A finding stable in <50% of cells is reported as element-class-specific rather than general.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) In-silico oracles (HMMER/regex, RDKit SMARTS, ESMFold) are proxies for wet-lab function; claims concern model-internal count controllability and its locality mechanism, not experimental viability — stated explicitly. Element COUNTS, however, are exact/objective structural facts, which strengthens the core measurement. 2) The causal-locality-enforcement intervention (masking distal dependencies of a feature) is nontrivial to implement cleanly, especially for autoregressive models; we focus the causal test on the masked-diffusion generator where conditional scores are directly accessible (matching the source theory) and treat autoregressive results as corroborating, reporting implementation fidelity. 3) The locality<->count-generalization link may hold for physically-independent elements but fail for coupled ones (where non-locality is genuinely required); we stratify by element independence and report this as an informative boundary rather than a failure. 4) Count-conditioned generation may be hard to elicit; we use three elicitation methods (prompting, iterative insertion, feature-steered placement) and report the strongest fair comparison. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound both locality measurement and placement-feature identification; controlled with multiple layers, difference-of-means baselines, raw-activation probes, and random-feature controls. 6) If count generalization does NOT track locality (e.g., it is driven by data-count diversity instead), that is itself a valuable, publishable result adapting/refuting the diffusion-locality theory for scientific design and pointing to data diversity as the operative cause. 7) A positive causal result would provide a concrete, cheap recipe (locality masking) for exceeding training element counts — high practical value if it holds.

Name: antiproperty_design_asymmetry
Title: Design Everything But That: Do Scientific Generators Suffer an Ironic-Rebound Asymmetry Between Positive and Negative Property Specification?
Short Hypothesis: Scientific generative models can causally steer TOWARD a specified structural element (positive design: 'include motif X') but cannot reliably steer to EXCLUDE it while designing everything else freely (negative/anti-property design: 'design a valid object that does NOT contain X'). We hypothesize a positive-vs-negative specification asymmetry: attempting to suppress an element via its interpretable feature triggers an ironic-rebound-like effect—the forbidden element reappears at rates far above the unconditioned base rate—because suppressing a concept requires internally activating it, and a compact 'exclude-X' handle does not exist the way an 'include-X' handle does; an intervention-free rebound signature predicts which anti-property requests will silently fail. PRIMARY AXIS: the design-space ironic-rebound phenomenon (forbidden element appears above base rate under suppression) as a DOMAIN TRANSFER of text/human negation-hardness into scientific design with EXACT structural oracles; the subspace-projection fix and the rebound audit are secondary.
Related Work: Two literatures meet for the first time in scientific design. (1) Text/vision negation interpretability establishes that negation is uniquely hard: 'Strong hallucinations from negation' (2024) proves LMs' string distributions cannot respect logical negation; 'Don't Think of the White Bear' (2025) shows ironic REBOUND—negation instructions paradoxically increase a forbidden concept's accessibility via middle-layer heads that amplify it; INLP (2020) removes a linguistic feature only by null-space PROJECTION (single-vector suppression is insufficient); RePS (2025) and SRS (2025) note suppression is systematically harder and more entangled than positive steering. ALL of this is in text/CLIP with fuzzy concepts. (2) Scientific interpretability-of-generation (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; chemistry-LM SAEs 2025) steers features TOWARD single positive properties and evaluates whether the property appears; none studies negative specification. My own prior intervention_leak proposal asks whether single-feature suppression of a property leaks through alternative DECODING routes; this proposal is different and complementary: it studies the POSITIVE-vs-NEGATIVE SPECIFICATION ASYMMETRY itself—whether 'exclude X while designing everything else' is even a representable, steerable target class, tests the ironic-rebound analog (forbidden element appears ABOVE base rate under suppression), and contrasts it head-to-head against the trivially-easy positive case. This transfers a well-established text/human negation phenomenon into high-stakes scientific design (excluding toxicophores, off-target motifs, disallowed folds), where an anti-property that silently rebounds is a safety failure. We contrast four axes -- text negation (Strong-hallucinations/White-Bear: fuzzy concepts, no exact oracle, no design object), concept suppression (INLP/RePS/SRS: removal quality in text/CLIP, single-vector insufficiency noted), scientific POSITIVE steering (InterPLM/ProtSAE: include-X only, appearance-checked), and THIS proposal (positive-vs-negative head-to-head on de-novo scientific objects with exact SMARTS/HMMER/DSSP presence oracles and a base-rate-referenced rebound test).
Abstract: Real scientific design constantly specifies what must be ABSENT: a drug candidate must exclude toxicophores, an enzyme must avoid an off-target binding motif, a designed protein must not fold into a disallowed conformation. Yet interpretability-guided design, and the human/text literature it borrows from, has focused almost entirely on POSITIVE specification—steering a feature to ADD a desired element. Negation is known to be uniquely hard for language models: suppressing a concept requires internally activating it, producing ironic rebound where the forbidden concept becomes MORE accessible. We ask whether scientific generative models inherit this, surfacing a phenomenon we call the positive-vs-negative specification asymmetry: models causally steer toward a structural element easily, but attempting to EXCLUDE it while designing everything else freely fails—often making the forbidden element appear ABOVE its unconditioned base rate (a design-space ironic rebound). Using ESM-2 protein language models and a SMILES chemical language model with sparse autoencoders and hard, exactly-checkable oracles (RDKit SMARTS for toxicophores/functional groups; HMMER/regex for protein motifs; DSSP for disallowed structure), we (1) head-to-head measure positive (include-X) vs negative (exclude-X) specification success at matched steering budget; (2) test the rebound hypothesis—does single-feature suppression push forbidden-element occurrence above base rate?; (3) LOCATE and causally test whether an 'exclude-X' handle exists (does subspace null-projection succeed where single-feature suppression fails?); and (4) AUDIT reliability—does an intervention-free rebound signature (early amplification of the forbidden feature) predict silent anti-property failure? More broadly this is CONSTRAINT SATISFACTION in generative design: a 'must-not-contain' safety constraint may silently fail with false confidence, of direct concern to molecular- and protein-design practitioners. Pre-registered primary endpoint: the asymmetry gap (Experiment 1). We predict a stark asymmetry, an ironic-rebound analog, and that subspace projection plus a rebound audit partially restore reliable negative design.
Experiments:
Shared setup (fixed once, reused below). MODELS (frozen): ESM-2 150M and 650M (proteins); a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~85M, MOSES-trained or public checkpoint). Frozen; only SAEs/probes trainable. SAEs: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka on the residual stream at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer (plus a second layer), width 16x, k=32, Adam lr 1e-3, ~40M activation tokens, seeds {0,1,2}; reconstruction accepted at fraction-variance-unexplained <=0.2. ELEMENT oracles (hard, exact -- presence/absence objective): molecules -- structural-alert-level functional groups / PAINS / common reactive-group SMARTS (RDKit); proteins -- specific motifs (zinc finger, catalytic triad) via HMMER/regex and a disallowed secondary-structure target via DSSP-on-ESMFold. We restrict to structural-alert-level elements with unambiguous detectors and avoid synthesizable-threat detail. VALIDITY gates: RDKit-validity + SA (molecules), ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity (proteins). PRECONDITION: for each element record the UNCONDITIONED base rate (fraction of ordinary generations containing it) over 2,000 samples, so rebound is measured relative to it; select the SAE feature(s) best encoding each element by concept-correlation / probe AUROC. Use ~8-12 elements per domain spanning a range of base rates. Compute: two ESM-2 sizes + small SMILES LM + ESMFold on 1-2 GPUs, academic-feasible.

OPERATIONAL DEFINITION of the negative-specification intervention: 'exclude-X' = negatively clamping the element's SAE feature(s) (or projecting out its subspace) at generation time to a target at/below the 5th percentile of its natural on-distribution activation, all other positions/features free; 'exclusion success' = fraction of VALID generations whose exact oracle reports the element ABSENT. PRE-REGISTERED PRIMARY ENDPOINT: the asymmetry gap (Experiment 1) pooled across elements and both domains; rebound, subspace fix, and audit are secondary. Base-rate statistics: rebound is tested as occurrence minus the unconditioned base rate with a two-proportion test and Wilson CIs, and elements are stratified by base rate so rare-element rebound is not trivially inflated.

Experiment 1 (H1 & H2 -- positive inclusion succeeds but negative exclusion fails: the specification asymmetry): Head-to-head test. For each element, at matched steering budget and matched validity, run (a) POSITIVE design -- steer the element's feature to INCLUDE it (measure inclusion success + validity); (b) NEGATIVE design -- steer to EXCLUDE it (negatively clamp the feature) while generating everything else freely (measure EXCLUSION success = fraction of valid generations that do NOT contain the element). Generate 300 objects per condition per element. Decisive metric first: ASYMMETRY GAP = positive success minus negative success at matched budget/validity, across elements and both domains (mixed-effects, effect size, CIs); random-direction and matched-non-element-feature controls. Convincing: mean asymmetry gap >= 0.3 with CI excluding 0, driven by positive success >= 0.6 while negative success is low. Undecidable band: gap in [0.1, 0.3) -> asymmetry present but modest; report, do not headline. Negative result (gap < 0.1; exclusion as easy as inclusion): scientific generators handle anti-property design robustly -- a valuable positive result contrasting with text-LLM negation failures.

Experiment 2 (H3 -- ironic rebound: single-feature suppression pushes the forbidden element ABOVE its base rate): Tests the white-bear effect. Compare forbidden-element occurrence under single-feature SUPPRESSION against the UNCONDITIONED base rate, swept over suppression strength (6 levels). Decisive metric first: REBOUND RATE = fraction of elements whose suppression raises occurrence ABOVE base rate; then rebound magnitude (occurrence minus base rate) and its dependence on suppression strength (does stronger suppression paradoxically increase rebound?); then WHERE it rebounds during autoregressive/iterative generation (whether a small set of components re-amplifies the forbidden feature). Convincing: rebound rate >= 0.3 with rebound magnitude CIs excluding 0, and a positive strength->rebound slope for a majority of rebounding elements. Undecidable band: rebound rate in [0.1, 0.3) or magnitude CI overlapping 0 -> weak/inconsistent rebound; report. Negative result (rebound rate < 0.1; suppression monotonically lowers occurrence): no ironic rebound -- suppression works as intended, reported honestly.

Experiment 3 (H4 -- no compact 'exclude-X' handle exists; reliable negation requires removing a SUBSPACE): Tests the mechanism. Contrast three exclusion mechanisms at matched validity: (a) single-feature negative steering (hypothesized to fail/rebound), (b) SUBSPACE NULL-PROJECTION -- project out the top-k correlated feature directions / SVD subspace (the INLP analog), (c) activation patching from element-free generations. Decisive metric first: exclusion success vs subspace dimension k -- the minimal k that drives occurrence below base rate -- then whether projection succeeds where single-feature suppression fails, then the validity cost at that k. Convincing: single-feature suppression does NOT drive occurrence below base rate at any strength, whereas subspace projection reaches exclusion success >= 0.8 at some k >= 2 with validity retained within 10% -- establishing that negation needs a subspace, not a single 'not' vector. Undecidable band: projection reaches exclusion in [0.5, 0.8) at acceptable validity, or requires k so large validity drops 10-20% -> a costly handle; report the exclusion-vs-validity frontier. Negative result (single-feature suppression alone reaches >= 0.8 exclusion): a compact exclude-X handle DOES exist -- an equally publishable refutation.

Experiment 4 (H5 -- an intervention-free rebound signature predicts which anti-property requests silently fail): Tests the audit payoff. Deploy a REBOUND SIGNATURE read mid-generation (early amplification / coherence of the forbidden element's feature despite active suppression) as an alarm. Systems compared: rebound signature vs output-side signals (validity, pseudo-perplexity, the suppression's apparent forward-pass success). Labels from Experiment 2's eventual forbidden-element presence. Decisive metric first: detection AUROC for eventual forbidden-element presence, then calibration ECE, then compute saved by aborting doomed negative-design requests before full generation + oracle checking. Convincing: signature AUROC >= 0.75 and >= 0.1 above the best output-side signal, ECE <= 0.1. Undecidable band: signature-minus-output-side AUROC gap in [0.0, 0.05] -> no added value; report parity. Negative result (AUROC < 0.6): no usable rebound signature; the audit payoff is withdrawn, leaving the asymmetry/rebound phenomenon as the contribution.

Experiment 5 (robustness of H1-H5): MECHANISTIC MEDIATION check: verify each selected feature MEDIATES (not merely correlates with) the element -- ablating it lowers element occurrence and patching it into element-free runs raises it -- with matched-strength RANDOM-feature suppression and a NO-SAE (raw difference-of-means) exclusion arm as controls for generic OOD drift and validity collapse. Repeat across both domains, both ESM-2 sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, two layers, and all elements; report the fraction of cells where the asymmetry, rebound, and subspace-projection fix replicate, and whether rebound is stronger for elements with higher base rate or richer feature redundancy. Report validity/novelty retention throughout. A finding stable in <50% of cells is reported as element-class-specific.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Element presence/absence is defined by hard, exact oracles (RDKit SMARTS, HMMER/regex, DSSP), a strength that makes the asymmetry and rebound objective; the main proxy is downstream 'harm/function', which we do not claim—claims concern the objectively-checkable structural presence of forbidden elements, and we restrict to structural-alert-level elements with unambiguous detectors, responsibly avoiding synthesizable-threat detail. 2) The 'no exclude-X handle' claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple exclusion mechanisms (single-feature negative steering, subspace null-projection, activation patching), sweeping strength, and head-to-head confirming that POSITIVE inclusion succeeds in the same pipeline—so exclusion failure is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable exclusion handle exists) is equally publishable. 3) Rebound could be confounded with generic off-distribution drift from strong suppression; random-direction and matched-non-element-feature controls, plus measuring occurrence strictly relative to base rate, isolate the rebound-specific effect. 4) Base rates for rare elements may be low, making rebound-above-base-rate easy to trigger trivially; we include elements spanning a range of base rates and report rebound as an effect size relative to base-rate uncertainty. 5) Subspace projection may reduce validity or interpretability; we quantify the exclusion-vs-validity frontier rather than assume a free lunch. 6) SAE quality/layer choice could confound; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, and difference-of-means baselines. 7) If negative specification turns out as easy as positive (small asymmetry, no rebound), that is a valuable positive result establishing that scientific generators handle anti-property design robustly—unlike text LLMs on linguistic negation.

Name: relational_feature_steering
Title: Intrinsic Is Easy, Relational Is Hard: Do Interpretable Features Give Causal Control Over a Protein's Binding Context, or Only Its Standalone Properties?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable features of protein language models afford causal, steerable control over a protein's INTRINSIC (partner-independent) properties (fold, hydrophobicity, motifs), but no comparably compact, causally-steerable feature is FOUND -- under an expanded search over layers, token positions, schedules, and multi-feature directions -- for RELATIONAL properties: the context-dependent fact that a designed protein binds a SPECIFIED partner. We define relational steerability operationally (an intervention must raise the intended-partner interface score MORE than the best decoy, i.e. specificity, not generic bindability). We hypothesize relational control is absent, entangled with intrinsic features, or requires partner-conditioned representations, so steering toward 'binds partner X' silently degrades to generic bindability -- an unrecognized blind spot in interpretability-guided binder design.
Related Work: All interpretability-for-generation work on protein language models—InterPLM (2024), ProtSAE (2025), Steering Protein Language Models/ASPO (2025), the antibody-SAE paper (2025), Automated Neuron Labelling (2025), and CB-pLM (2024)—discovers and steers features encoding INTRINSIC, single-protein properties (secondary structure, GRAVY, molecular weight, zinc-finger/binding-site motifs) and evaluates whether that standalone property appears. Separately, a large partner-aware PPI literature (BIPSPI 2018; D-SCRIPT 2021; ReCLIP 2026; partner-specific interface prediction 2011) establishes that binding is intrinsically RELATIONAL—the same residue's behavior depends on the partner—but this line is purely PREDICTIVE and never touches the internal features of a GENERATIVE model or their steerability. No prior work asks whether a protein generative model represents relational, partner-conditioned properties as causally-steerable features, contrasts the steerability of intrinsic vs relational properties, or exposes that binder-design steering toward a NAMED partner may collapse to generic bindability. This proposal is the first to introduce the intrinsic-vs-relational axis into interpretability-of-generation and to audit partner-specific controllability—distinct from all prior single-property steering and from all predictive PPI work. CONTRIBUTION BULLETS: (1) conceptual -- introduce the intrinsic-vs-relational axis into interpretability-of-generation; (2) methodological -- partner-conditioned probing/steering and an operational definition of relational steerability (specificity over the best decoy, not generic bindability); (3) empirical -- the intrinsic-easy/relational-hard asymmetry; (4) applied -- a reusable partner-specificity audit. Closest baselines contrasted: intrinsic single-property steering (assumes an internal handle exists), predictive partner-aware PPI models (never touch generator internals or steerability), and controllable binder-design methods (report bindability, not audited specificity). Scope is single-sequence PLMs specifically. The setting is not reducible to prior property steering because the label is UNDEFINED without a partner.
Abstract: Interpretability-guided protein design steers PLM features toward desired properties -- but every demonstrated property is INTRINSIC to a single protein (fold, hydrophobicity, a local motif). Real binder design demands RELATIONAL control: producing a protein that binds a SPECIFIED partner -- a fact meaningless without the partner and, from decades of PPI research, irreducibly context-dependent. We introduce the intrinsic-vs-relational axis into interpretability-of-generation (conceptual novelty) and a partner-conditioned probing/steering audit (methodological novelty), and give an operational definition of RELATIONAL STEERABILITY: an intervention is relationally steerable only if it raises the intended-partner interface score MORE than the best decoy (specificity), not merely generic bindability. We hypothesize an intrinsic-easy/relational-hard asymmetry: compact steerable features exist for intrinsic properties, but no compact steerable feature is FOUND -- under an expanded search over layers, token positions, schedules, and multi-feature directions -- for partner-specific binding, so steering toward 'binds partner X' silently collapses to promiscuity. Using ESM-2 and an antibody PLM (p-IgGen) with sparse autoencoders, we (1) confirm intrinsic control succeeds (pipeline calibration); (2) contrast intrinsic-vs-relational steerability and measure a promiscuity-collapse rate, controlling for generic confounds (interface propensity, hydrophobicity, charge, length, disorder, foldability, novelty); (3) test whether relational information is absent, entangled, or requires partner conditioning; and (4) audit how often steered binders silently bind the wrong/any partner while validity and generic-bindability pass, scored by ESMFold-in-complex with calibrated AlphaFold-Multimer confirmation. We frame impact as changing evaluation norms and delivering reusable specificity-audit panels for therapeutic-design, biologics-engineering, and benchmark-creation communities, not as validated binder design.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: ESM-2 at 150M and 650M parameters and an antibody PLM (p-IgGen), base weights frozen. SAEs: TopK (k=32) and Ordered (for steerability) variants, dictionary 16384, on the residual stream at a layer chosen by an intrinsic-dimension heuristic, seeds {0,1}, FVU reported. INTRINSIC-property oracles (cheap): alpha-helix/beta-sheet fraction (DSSP on ESMFold), GRAVY, molecular weight, motifs (HMMER/regex). RELATIONAL oracle: binding to a SPECIFIED partner via in-silico complex prediction -- ESMFold-in-complex interface pLDDT/ipTM and interface contact count as a cheap first pass, AlphaFold-Multimer confirmation on a subset -- plus a SPECIFICITY panel of decoy partners (specificity = intended-partner score minus best-decoy score). Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT>=0.6, pseudo-perplexity within 1.5x baseline. Steering budget in normalized activation-norm units; SAE-feature, difference-of-means, partner-conditioned, random-direction, and matched-intrinsic-feature controls. To bound compute, partner panel = 20 targets, decoy panel = 10 per target, 300 steered designs per target. DATA/LABELS: partner panels and binder/non-binder labels are drawn from curated PPI datasets (experimentally-supported complexes and matched non-binders), split train/val/test with a <=30% inter-split sequence-identity cap (mmseqs2) and a 1:1 positive:negative balance; the 20 partners are held-out targets not used to fit any feature. INTERVENTION SEARCH (to justify any absence claim): before concluding no relational handle, we search multiple layers, token positions (including the prepended-partner region), steering schedules, and MULTI-FEATURE/compositional directions, not only single compact features. BASELINES beyond SAE features: supervised latent directions, activation patching from a bound-complex run, full-sequence partner-conditioned generation, and a retrieval/template control. CONFOUNDS regressed out or matched in all relational analyses: interface propensity, hydrophobicity, charge, length, disorder, foldability, and sequence novelty. RELATIONAL ORACLE: ESMFold-in-complex first pass with AlphaFold-Multimer confirmation on a calibrated subset (>=200 designs), with multiple interface scores (ipTM, interface pLDDT, contact count) reported alongside agreement/calibration analysis. All decision thresholds below are reported with bootstrap confidence intervals.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- Intrinsic properties are causally, specifically steerable). Tests that interpretable features give calibrated causal control over partner-independent properties, establishing the pipeline works. Data: intrinsic-property features located by probe AUROC>=0.8 on 2,000 held-out natural sequences. Systems: SAE-feature and difference-of-means steering vs random-direction control, strength swept. Decisive metric (primary): intrinsic property gain per unit budget within the validity gate, and effect specificity (target property moves, matched non-target intrinsic properties do not). Convincing positive: intrinsic property change >= 0.5 SD of the natural-sequence property distribution at a validity-preserving budget, clearly above the random-direction control, in >= 3 of 4 model x property settings -- confirming intrinsic control succeeds. Decision band: gain in [0.2, 0.5) SD means intrinsic control is weak in this pipeline -- reported as such, and it caps how strong the intrinsic-vs-relational contrast in Experiment 2 can be. Negative: no intrinsic feature steers its property above the random control means the pipeline lacks steering power, and no relational absence claim can be made (the study is reported as under-powered, not as confirming H2).

Experiment 2 (H2 -- No compact causally-steerable partner-specificity feature; relational collapses to generic bindability). Tests, in the SAME pipeline that just succeeded intrinsically, whether steering toward "binds partner X" yields intended-partner specificity or mere promiscuous bindability. Data/systems: relational features located both partner-agnostically and via partner-CONDITIONED activations (target partner prepended); steer toward each of the 20 partners via SAE-feature, difference-of-means (binders-of-X minus non-binders), and partner-conditioned directions, vs random and matched-intrinsic controls. Decisive metric (primary): the intrinsic-vs-relational STEERABILITY GAP -- relational specificity gain (intended-minus-best-decoy) per unit budget compared to the intrinsic gain from Experiment 1; and PROMISCUITY COLLAPSE RATE = fraction of steered binders whose binding score rises for intended AND decoy partners alike (zero specificity). Convincing support for H2: relational specificity gain <= 0.2x the intrinsic gain AND promiscuity collapse rate >= 60%, despite confirmed intrinsic control -- relational steering exists only as generic bindability. Decision band: relational-to-intrinsic gain ratio in (0.2, 0.5] or collapse rate in [40%, 60%) means relational control is weak-but-present -- reported as partial, not absent. Negative (refutes H2): relational specificity gain reaches >= 0.5x intrinsic gain with collapse rate < 40% means a genuine steerable partner-specific feature exists -- an equally publishable positive result.

Experiment 3 (H3 -- The relational signal is absent/entangled/partner-conditioned, not intrinsic specificity). Tests which of the three predicted regimes holds, using probing and interpretation. Data/systems: (a) partner-conditioned vs partner-agnostic probe AUROC for intended-partner binding -- does relational information exist without the partner in context? (b) controlled pairs -- same binder vs multiple partners, and different binders of the same partner -- to test whether located relational features encode partner-specificity or generic interface-propensity (a feature firing identically regardless of partner is generic); (c) a partner-conditioned architecture variant (partner prepended) to test whether relational steerability APPEARS when the partner is in context. Decisive metric: partner-conditioned minus partner-agnostic probe AUROC, and feature partner-invariance (activation correlation across partners). Convincing positive for "requires partner conditioning": partner-agnostic probe near chance (AUROC in [0.5, 0.6]) while partner-conditioned probe reaches >= 0.75, and relational steerability from Experiment 2 rises materially only in the partner-conditioned variant. Decision band: partner-conditioned advantage in [0.05, 0.15) AUROC means partner context helps only weakly -- the regime is reported as ambiguous between "absent" and "entangled". Negative: partner-agnostic probe already high AND features partner-specific means relational specificity is present intrinsically, refuting the entanglement/conditioning account.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Silent wrong-partner designs pass output-side checks; an internal probe flags them). Tests that steered binders bind the wrong/any partner while validity and generic-bindability checks pass, and that the internal specificity probe catches this. Data/systems: for the 20 target partners, request binders via steering; among valid, generically-bindable designs measure the failure and test detectors. Decisive metric (primary): SILENT WRONG-PARTNER RATE = fraction of valid, generically-bindable designs that bind a decoy at least as well as the intended partner; secondary: detection AUROC/ECE of output-side signals (validity, generic interface score, generation likelihood) vs the internal partner-conditioned specificity probe for catching wrong-partner designs. Convincing positive: silent wrong-partner rate >= 40% with output-side detection AUROC in [0.45, 0.60] (near chance) while the internal specificity probe reaches AUROC>=0.75 -- a usable pre-flight specificity filter, with quantified compute saved before expensive AlphaFold-Multimer confirmation. Decision band: wrong-partner rate in [20%, 40%) or internal-probe AUROC in [0.6, 0.75) means the blind spot is real but modest / the filter is weak -- reported with its error. Negative: wrong-partner rate < 20% and output-side checks already detect non-specific designs (AUROC>=0.7) means specificity is not a hidden blind spot, refuting H3's auditing claim.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The relational claim is partly an ABSENCE claim (no clean steerable partner-specificity feature); we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (SAE features, difference-of-means, partner-conditioned steering), sweeping strength, and calibrating that intrinsic control DOES succeed in the same pipeline, so a null relational result is meaningful rather than a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable partner-specific feature) is equally publishable and valuable for binder design. 2) Binding is scored by in-silico complex predictors (AlphaFold-Multimer/ESMFold interface metrics), which are proxies for wet-lab affinity/specificity; claims concern model-internal, in-silico-verified partner-specific controllability, not experimental binding—stated explicitly, and specificity uses relative (intended-vs-decoy) scores to reduce absolute-score bias. 3) Complex prediction is compute-heavier than single-sequence oracles; we cap partner and decoy panel sizes and use ESMFold-in-complex as a cheaper first-pass with AlphaFold-Multimer confirmation on a subset. 4) Relational information may simply be absent without the partner in context; the partner-conditioned probing/steering experiments are designed to detect exactly this and turn it into an informative finding about what representation relational control requires. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, difference-of-means baselines, and random-direction controls. 6) If relational steering unexpectedly succeeds with specificity, that overturns the hypothesis but yields a strong positive contribution. 7) We frame practical impact as changing evaluation norms and releasing reusable specificity-audit panels, not as validated binder design; wet-lab or stronger external validation is out of scope, and any design claim is in-silico only. We report what is learned under each outcome -- strong relational failure, weak relational control, or successful partner-specific steering -- so a null is informative rather than merely negative.

Name: rna_folding_mirage_steering
Title: The Folding Mirage: Do Interpretable Features Control an RNA's Local Motifs While Silently Breaking Its Global Thermodynamic Fold?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable sparse-autoencoder features of RNA language models afford causal, steerable control over LOCAL structural motifs (a hairpin, a stem, a poly-U tract), but NOT over the GLOBAL thermodynamic fold that defines RNA function. Consequently, steering a feature to insert a desired local structure silently produces sequences whose true minimum-free-energy fold and target-structure Boltzmann probability collapse — a 'folding mirage' — that motif-content and validity checks miss, but which an intervention-free internal thermodynamic-consistency signal flags. We do NOT propose steering itself (SAE-RNA already reports it); our claim is that local-motif steerability and global-fold steerability DECOUPLE, that the decoupling exceeds matched controls, and that the resulting mirage is auditable. The global-non-steerability part is scoped as 'no robust steerable global-fold direction found under tested interventions,' not universal absence.
Related Work: Positioning across four rows with per-row deltas. (i) Descriptive RNA-LM interpretability (SAE-RNA 2025; SPIRAL/BiRNA-BERT 2026; small gene-LM SAEs 2025) finds features for stems, hairpins, poly-tracts, ncRNA families — delta: descriptive only, no test of whether steering preserves the global fold. (ii) Steerability: SAE-RNA reports single-property steering — delta: we do not claim steering as novel; we test the local-vs-global CONTRAST and its reliability. (iii) Inverse folding / RNA design LMs (RNAinformer 2024; 'Designing RNAs with Language Models' 2026; AIDO.RNA 2025) hit target secondary structures via supervised/RL — delta: no interpretability, no feature-level steering, no audit of silent failure. (iv) Oracle-based steering-audit work in protein/molecule (InterPLM, ProtSAE) establishes the content-vs-global-property axis — delta: never applied to RNA, where the global functional property has an EXACT physics oracle. RNA is the ideal testbed because ViennaRNA computes the exact MFE structure, ensemble free energy, and Boltzmann probability of any target structure instantly and free, turning 'silent global failure' from a proxy into a computable quantity. Novelty is explicitly threefold: the empirical FINDING (local/global decoupling), the oracle-grounded evaluation SETTING (ViennaRNA as clean ground truth for steering reliability), and the intervention-free AUDIT mechanism. This is the first interpretability-of-generation study for RNA to contrast local-motif against global-fold steerability and to surface the folding-mirage phenomenon.
Abstract: An RNA's function is set by its global thermodynamic fold, not merely by which local motifs it contains: the same hairpin can sit in a functional structure or be buried in a completely different minimum-free-energy conformation. Interpretability-guided design increasingly steers language-model features to add desired structural elements, judged by whether the motif appears. We surface a phenomenon we call the folding mirage: steering an interpretable feature to insert a local structure (a hairpin, a stem) reliably increases that motif's presence but drives the sequence's true global fold — its MFE structure and the Boltzmann probability of the intended target — to collapse, invisible to motif-content and validity checks. We stress we do not propose steering itself; our claim is that local-motif and global-fold steerability DECOUPLE beyond matched controls, and that the mirage is auditable. We then ask: do RNA-LMs represent the global fold as a compact, causally-steerable feature the way they represent local motifs, or is global consistency emergent and weakly steerable? RNA is the ideal testbed because ViennaRNA gives the exact global fold, ensemble free energy, and target-structure Boltzmann probability for free. Using RiNALMo/RNA-FM with sparse autoencoders, we (1) LOCATE local-motif and global-fold features under pre-registered operational criteria; (2) CAUSALLY test each with hard controls (scrambled-feature, matched-activation, intervention-size matching) plus a specificity negative control; (3) quantify the mirage — the drop in target-structure Boltzmann probability that local steering incurs; and (4) AUDIT whether an internal thermodynamic-consistency signal flags mirages better than motif-content or likelihood. Either outcome matters: a mirage means RNA design evaluation must add global-fold checks; a null certifies feature-steering as thermodynamically safe.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (public, FROZEN): RiNALMo (650M) and RNA-FM (~100M); as encoders, generation is by masked infilling. Only SAEs trained: TopK and Ordered SAEs (Ordered latents ranked by importance, the antibody-SAE recipe recovering steerability TopK lacks), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. Oracle (exact, cheap): ViennaRNA — RNAfold MFE structure/energy, partition function for ensemble free energy, and the Boltzmann probability that a sequence folds into a specified TARGET (primary GLOBAL signal). LOCAL oracle: presence/position of a hairpin loop / stem / poly-U tract from the predicted structure. OPERATIONAL FEATURE CRITERIA (pre-registered, set before main experiments): a LOCAL-motif feature must have held-out probe AUROC>=0.8 for one specific motif AND near-chance AUROC for global-fold class; a GLOBAL-fold feature must predict MFE-per-nt / ensemble free energy (R^2>=0.40) AND not be explainable by any single local motif. PRE-REGISTERED PRIMARY ENDPOINT per experiment stated below (no metric shopping). Validity gate: GC bounds + pseudo-perplexity. Data: 20,000 held-out Rfam ncRNA spanning tRNA-scale (~76 nt) and longer families for feature-property linking; 5,000 DISSOCIATION PAIRS (same local hairpin in well-folded vs misfolded global context). Steering = add alpha*d_hat during masked infilling; alpha in {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - local-motif features are causally steerable): steer local-motif features to INSERT a target motif; 500 infilled sequences per (feature,alpha,seed). Controls: random-direction, scrambled-feature, matched-activation-norm. PRIMARY ENDPOINT: local-motif installation rate (target motif in the RNAfold structure). Decision band: >=0.60 AND >=0.40 over best control for >=2/3 motifs => local control genuine; gain [0.15,0.40) => inconclusive; <0.15 => not steerable (premise fails, reported).

Experiment 2 (H2 - global fold decodable but not steerable): (a) DECODABILITY: probe for global properties (MFE/nt, ensemble free energy, base-pairing fraction, fold class) controlling for local content; AUROC/R^2. (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head with intervention-SIZE matched to Experiment 1: steer best global-fold direction (TopK/Ordered SAE feature, difference-of-means well-vs-misfolded, activation-patching from correctly-folded) to RAISE target-structure Boltzmann probability while holding local content fixed. PRIMARY ENDPOINT: ratio r = global-fold efficacy / local efficacy (Exp 1). Decision band: global decodable (R^2>=0.40 or AUROC>=0.70) AND r<=0.33 => H2 confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial (test whether Ordered SAEs raise it); r>=0.67 => global fold IS steerable (refutes, equally publishable).

Experiment 2b (SPECIFICITY negative control): steer local-motif features on sequences where the target motif is thermodynamically compatible with the existing fold (small, peripheral); here local steering should NOT collapse the global fold. Confirms the mirage in Exp 3 is a genuine decoupling, not an artifact of any perturbation breaking folds.

Experiment 3 (H3 - the folding mirage): steer local-motif features, 500 sequences per level. PRIMARY ENDPOINT: SILENT-MISFOLD RATE = fraction of local-motif-satisfying, valid sequences with target-structure Boltzmann probability <0.10; plus mirage slope d(Boltzmann)/d(local gain) and Spearman rho between cheap checks (motif-content, perplexity) and true global health. Decision band: misfold>=0.30 AND |rho|<=0.20 => mirage + blind spot confirmed; [0.10,0.30) or |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; <0.10 or |rho|>=0.40 => no silent mirage (steering thermodynamically safe, positive result). The mirage is declared a NEW phenomenon only if the decoupling exceeds every matched control AND the specificity control (2b) is negative.

Experiment 4 (H4 - intervention-free thermodynamic-consistency flag): no-intervention score = global-fold-probe confidence / SAE-feature coherence read mid-generation. PRIMARY ENDPOINT: AUROC detecting misfolded (low-Boltzmann) sequences from Exp 3, vs output-side (motif content, perplexity, likelihood). Decision band: internal AUROC>=0.75 AND >=0.10 over best output-side => flag confirmed; (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; <=0.05 => no better (reported). APPLICATION SCENARIO tied to the audit: in a batch of steered tRNA-scaffold designs, the flag should let a designer discard mirages before ordering/synthesis, avoiding wasted wet-lab cost. ABLATIONS (primary): layer choice, sequence length (short vs longer), target motif class, steering strength calibration, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, RiNALMo vs RNA-FM. Corroborate a subset with a structure-aware model (ERNIE-RNA/structRFM). A finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Global fold is assessed by ViennaRNA (nearest-neighbor thermodynamic model), well-validated but in-silico; it ignores tertiary interactions/pseudoknots and cellular context, so claims concern thermodynamic-model-verified SECONDARY-structure global folding, NOT wet-lab or tertiary function — stated explicitly. We corroborate a subset with a structure-aware model and report agreement. 2) The global-non-steerability claim is scoped as absence-under-tested-interventions; we mitigate with multiple intervention types (TopK/Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching), strength sweeps, and head-to-head calibration that LOCAL features ARE steerable in the same pipeline — a null is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive steerable global-fold handle is equally publishable and useful for structure-aware design. 3) The mirage could be generic off-distribution drift; controlled with random-direction, scrambled-feature, matched-activation controls, a specificity negative control (Exp 2b), and by testing motif-specific displacement. 4) Local and global structure are partly entangled (a large motif dominates the fold); the dissociation pairs separate them and we report where separation is impossible. 5) SAE quality/layer could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) An internal consistency probe might not beat a raw-activation probe on AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (local-decodable, global-weakly-steerable) and audit payoff remain the contributions. 7) A null mirage is a valuable positive result establishing RNA-LM feature-steering as thermodynamically safe, directly reassuring RNA design and synthetic-biology practitioners.

Name: conservation_law_mirage_reactions
Title: Balanced by Habit, Not by Law: Do Reaction Generative Models Internally Represent Mass Conservation as a Steerable Feature, or Fake It?
Short Hypothesis: We advance three separable, typed claims. (C1, phenomenon) Autoregressive reaction-prediction models emit atom-balanced reactions (matching element counts across the arrow) not because they hold a compact, causally-steerable internal representation of the conservation LAW, but via a shallow atom-copying heuristic tied to local token context; steering an interpretable feature to alter a product's chemistry (add/remove an atom or functional group) therefore silently breaks mass balance—a 'conservation mirage' that ordinary SMILES-validity checks miss. (C2, mechanism) Mass/atom conservation is linearly DECODABLE from activations yet, under every intervention family we test, has no robust steerable direction the way local chemistry features do—a decodable-but-weakly-steerable GLOBAL invariant, scoped as 'no robust steerable balance direction found under tested interventions,' not universal absence. (C3, audit) An intervention-free internal balance-consistency signal flags mirage reactions better than validity or model likelihood. The broader lesson we test: in generative models a global conservation invariant can be behaviorally satisfied without being a steerable internal object, even while LOCAL properties are cleanly steerable.
Related Work: FlowER (2025) and atom-conserving CRNNs (2023) show data-driven reaction models routinely VIOLATE mass/atom conservation, producing 'hallucinatory' unbalanced reactions, and fix this ARCHITECTURALLY by hard-coding electron/atom-balance layers—treating conservation as an external constraint, never asking whether a standard model internally represents it. 'Circuits, Features, and Heuristics in Molecular Transformers' (2025) finds molecular transformers implement ring/branch SYNTAX circuits and a steerable valence-capacity direction, and 'Physics Steering' (2025) shows physics foundation models have steerable concept directions—but neither studies reactions or the conservation invariant, and neither asks whether a global conservation law (as opposed to a local property) is a steerable handle. Conservation-law discovery work (Noether-from-DNN 2021; stoichiometry-nullspace methods 2014/2024) extracts laws from PREDICTIVE dynamics models, never from a generative reaction LM's internal features, and never tests steering reliability. No prior work (a) asks whether a generative reaction model represents mass/atom conservation as a causal, steerable feature, (b) surfaces the conservation-mirage phenomenon where chemistry-steering silently unbalances a reaction, or (c) provides an internal balance-reliability audit. This introduces the content-vs-conservation-law axis into interpretability-of-generation for chemical reactions—a new object class where conservation is an exact, instantly computable oracle (element-count matching / stoichiometry null space)—distinct from all prior single-property steering and from all architectural conservation fixes. Positioning as a three-row contrast with explicit deltas: (i) architectural conservation-enforcement (FlowER 2025; atom-conserving CRNNs 2023) CHANGES the model to force balance—we FREEZE the model and ask whether balance is an internal steerable law; (ii) local feature-steering (Circuits/Features/Heuristics 2025; Physics Steering 2025) steers a LOCAL property and never audits a global invariant's side-effect nor tests the invariant's own steerability; (iii) conservation-law discovery (Noether-from-DNN 2021; stoichiometry-nullspace 2014/2024) extracts laws from PREDICTIVE dynamics models, not a generative reaction LM's features. A non-obvious setting distinction: a global stoichiometric invariant in sequence generation is qualitatively unlike local property steering because it is a conserved relation between the reactant and product SIDES that no single local edit satisfies in isolation, so local steerability gives no reason to expect the global law is steerable. Contributions are threefold and typed—empirical phenomenon (C1, the mirage), mechanistic diagnosis (C3, heuristic-not-law), and a released element-residual balance-audit benchmark plus detector reusable across reaction generators—not a new reaction-prediction method.
Abstract: Mass conservation is chemistry's most basic law: a valid reaction has identical element counts on both sides. Data-driven reaction models are known to hallucinate unbalanced reactions, and the field fixes this by hard-coding balance into the architecture—never asking whether a standard model represents conservation internally. We surface a phenomenon we call the conservation mirage and make three typed claims. (C1) An autoregressive reaction transformer emits mostly balanced reactions via a shallow atom-copying heuristic, not a genuine internal law: steering an interpretable feature to change a product's chemistry (add a methyl, swap a halogen, remove an oxygen) reliably changes the chemistry but silently breaks atom balance, invisible to SMILES-validity checks and evident only from element counting. (C2) Conservation is linearly decodable from activations yet, under every intervention family we test, has no robust steerable direction the way local chemistry features do—a decodable-but-weakly-steerable global invariant. (C3) A cheap intervention-free balance-consistency signal flags mirage reactions better than validity or likelihood. Reactions are the ideal testbed because balance is an exact, free oracle (element-count vectors and the stoichiometry null space).
