We quantify how often validity-only screening would pass unbalanced outputs and translate it into wasted effort for retrosynthesis filtering, reaction editing, and autonomous-discovery loops. Either outcome is actionable: a real mirage changes how steered reactions are screened; a null certifies steering as conservation-safe. We release an open balance-audit benchmark and detector, and test the broader lesson that a global invariant can be non-steerable even where local properties are steerable.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Model: an autoregressive reaction transformer (Molecular-Transformer-style, ~30M params) trained on USPTO-MIT reaction SMILES (479,035 reactions), filtered to the atom-balanced subset with atom-mapping retained; FROZEN after training. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka SAEs (Ordered can recover steerability that TopK's decodable-but-inert features lack), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M residual-stream activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen mid layer, seeds 0/1/2. Oracle (exact, free via RDKit): the reactant-minus-product element-count residual - a reaction is atom-balanced iff the residual is the zero vector (charge balance and atom-mapping completeness also computed). LOCAL-CHEMISTRY oracle: presence/absence of specified product functional groups/atoms via SMARTS. Validity gate: RDKit-parseable, valence-valid on both sides. BASELINE (needed for the absence claim): confirm the frozen model natively emits atom-balanced products at rate >= 0.80 on held-out reactants, well above a token-shuffle chance rate; if it does not, the mechanism claim is reframed. Steering = add alpha*d_hat during product decoding given fixed reactants; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - local-chemistry features are causally steerable): Identify chemistry features (fire when a product contains a given functional group/atom; probe AUROC >= 0.8) and steer to add/remove that group in the product given fixed reactants. Generate 500 completions per (feature, alpha, seed). Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: chemistry-installation rate (intended group/atom change appears in the product). Decision band: rate >= 0.60 AND >= 0.40 over control for >=2/3 of groups => chemistry control genuine (H1 holds); gain [0.15,0.40) => inconclusive; gain < 0.15 => chemistry not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - the conservation mirage: chemistry steering silently breaks mass balance; SMILES-validity checks miss it): Steer chemistry features and generate 500 completions per level. Decisive metric FIRST: SILENT-IMBALANCE RATE = fraction of chemistry-satisfying, SMILES-valid reactions whose element-count residual is nonzero, plus the mirage slope d(|residual|)/d(chemistry gain) and Spearman rho between cheap checks (SMILES-validity, pseudo-perplexity) and true balance. Decision band: imbalance rate >= 0.30 AND |rho| <= 0.20 => mirage + blind spot confirmed; imbalance [0.10,0.30) or |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; imbalance < 0.10 or |rho| >= 0.40 => steering is conservation-safe (positive result).

Experiment 3 (H3 - conservation is decodable-but-not-steerable and rests on a shallow atom-copying heuristic, not a compact conservation-LAW feature): (a) DECODABILITY: probe 'is-balanced' / the element residual from activations, reporting AUROC and the earliest product-decoding position at which balance status is decodable. (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: steer the best conservation direction (SAE feature, difference-of-means balanced-vs-unbalanced, activation-patching from balanced runs) to RESTORE balance (drive residual->0) while holding product chemistry fixed; ratio r = conservation efficacy / chemistry efficacy from Experiment 1. (c) MECHANISM (heuristic vs law): using the 4,000 controlled pairs that hold the same product functional group in balanced vs deliberately unbalanced reactions, test whether the located 'conservation' unit tracks the GLOBAL residual (law) or LOCAL product content (heuristic). Decisive metric FIRST: r, read together with the mechanism contrast. Decision band: r <= 0.33 AND the unit predicts local content (AUROC >= 0.80) but the global residual only at <= 0.60 => H3 confirmed (inert + shallow heuristic); r in (0.33,0.67) or residual-AUROC in (0.60,0.75) => partial; r >= 0.67 => a genuine steerable conservation handle exists, refuting H3.

Experiment 4 (H4 - an intervention-free internal balance-consistency signal flags the mirage): No-intervention score = conservation-probe confidence / SAE-feature coherence read mid-generation. Decisive metric FIRST: AUROC detecting the mass-unbalanced reactions from Experiment 2. Systems: internal signal vs output-side (SMILES-validity, pseudo-perplexity, model likelihood). Decision band: internal AUROC >= 0.75 AND >= 0.10 over the best output-side detector => flag confirmed; margin (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; margin <= 0.05 => no better (reported honestly). ROBUSTNESS: two model sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, forward-prediction vs retrosynthesis framing; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.

PRE-REGISTERED DEFINITIONS (set before results). A 'compact steerable feature' = a single SAE latent (or a <=3-dim difference-of-means direction) whose steering yields on-target efficacy (Cohen's d) >= the chemistry features' median at matched activation-norm and matched KL; 'decodable' = probe AUROC >= 0.75. The internal BALANCE-AUDIT SIGNAL is defined mathematically: s = sigmoid(w . h_t + b), a logistic probe on the mid-layer residual h_t predicting zero element-residual, trained on the TRAIN split only and frozen; evaluation uses held-out TEST generations, split 80/10/10 by reaction scaffold to prevent leakage. Pseudo-perplexity here = mean per-token negative log-likelihood of the generated product conditioned on the reactants (left-to-right)—the same quantity a practitioner reads off the model—making it a fair output-side comparator.

NON-SAE BASELINES (so a null is not blamed on the SAE): (i) raw-activation linear representation editing (difference-of-means / logistic-probe direction on the un-decomposed residual stream); (ii) a decoder-logit balance constraint (down-weight product tokens that increase |element residual|). Both run head-to-head with SAE steering in Experiments 1 and 3. CAUSAL ATOM-SOURCE control: test whether steering changes atom-source alignment/copy patterns (attention-to-reactant-atom maps), not just final element residuals, supporting the atom-copying-heuristic claim.

EXPERIMENT 5 (incremental-insight sanity): compare the internal diagnosis against an explicit balance-aware constrained-decoding baseline (reject/repair products whose running element residual cannot reach zero). Report whether the internal audit adds information beyond this trivial output check—specifically whether it flags mirages EARLIER in decoding (earliest-reliable-detection position) and at lower compute. STAKES ESTIMATE: on a fixed 5,000-reaction steered set, report the fraction of SMILES-valid outputs that are mass-unbalanced (the rate at which validity-only screening passes unusable reactions) and translate it into wasted-effort terms for retrosynthesis proposal filtering, reaction editing, and autonomous-discovery loops.

ADDED ROBUSTNESS: a second dataset (USPTO-50k / Open Reaction Database temporal split) and a second tokenization (SELFIES) show the phenomenon is not a USPTO-MIT or SMILES artifact; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Mass/atom balance is an EXACT, non-proxy oracle (element counting is deterministic), which is a strength; the main proxy is downstream 'feasibility', which we deliberately do not claim—core claims concern the objectively-computable conservation invariant, not reaction viability. 2) The conservation-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK and Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching), sweeping strength, and head-to-head calibrating that CHEMISTRY features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null conservation result is meaningful rather than a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable conservation handle) is equally publishable and directly useful for building balance-aware reaction models without architectural surgery. 3) The mirage could be confounded with generic off-distribution drift; we use random-direction and matched-non-chemistry-feature controls and test whether the mirage tracks chemistry-specific displacement. 4) Chemistry and balance are partly entangled (a chemistry edit that adds an atom must be sourced from a reactant); the controlled dissociation pairs (step 5) and the atom-source diagnostics are designed to separate 'model knows the atom must come from somewhere' from 'model copies atoms locally', and we report where separation is impossible. 5) Some USPTO reactions are themselves unbalanced/incompletely recorded; we filter to a curated balanced-reaction training/eval subset and report label quality. 6) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 7) An internal balance probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (chemistry-decodable, conservation-weakly-steerable, heuristic-vs-law) and the audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 8) If no mirage is found (chemistry steering preserves balance), that is a valuable positive result establishing that reaction-model feature steering is conservation-safe and that the model represents conservation robustly.

Name: magnitude_dial_blindspot
Title: On/Off but Not How-Much: Do Interpretable Features Give a Calibrated Magnitude Dial for Scientific Design, or Only a Presence Switch?
Short Hypothesis: Scientific sequence/graph generative models represent a design property's categorical PRESENCE as a cleanly causally-steerable feature, but we hypothesize they do NOT hold a calibrated internal representation of its quantitative MAGNITUDE. One crisp, falsifiable claim: for the SAME property and the SAME steering direction, steering moves the property monotonically yet cannot dial it to a specified numeric target (a set-point calibration failure), and the internal magnitude code is logarithmically compressed so control degrades sharply at high magnitudes. We name this the 'magnitude blind spot' and define it operationally before experiments: presence-flip success is high while numeric set-point hit-rate is low, with set-point error rising with the requested value. Consequently 'set logP to 2.5' or 'set helix content to 40%' silently misses while presence/validity checks pass. Separate contributions: the FINDING (presence-steerable, magnitude-uncalibrated), an INTERPRETATION (log-compression), a FIX (log-reparameterized dial, evaluated on held-out targets), and an AUDIT (internal magnitude-consistency flag).
Related Work: A robust cognitive-science-inspired line shows LLMs encode numeric magnitude in low-dimensional, logarithmically-compressed, causally-manipulable subspaces (Language Models Represent Space and Time 2023; The Geometry of Numerical Reasoning 2024, which causally intervenes on numeric-comparison subspaces; Number Representations in LLMs 2025 showing sublinear/log compression; Numeric Magnitude Comparison Effects 2023 showing human-like distance/size effects). Separately, interpretability-of-generation for scientific objects (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; chemistry-LM SAEs 2025; Steering PLMs/ASPO 2025) steers features toward a property and evaluates whether the property is INCREASED or PRESENT, always reporting directional/binary gains and never a QUANTITATIVE set-point. No prior work (a) transfers the log-compressed magnitude-representation phenomenon from text LLMs into scientific GENERATIVE design, (b) distinguishes presence-steerability from calibrated magnitude-steerability for the same property, or (c) exposes that hitting a numeric design set-point is an unrecognized blind spot with a level-dependent (worse-at-high-magnitude) failure profile. This is distinct from my prior proposals, which contrast intrinsic vs relational/global/pathway properties; here the contrast is categorical presence vs quantitative magnitude of the SAME property, and it borrows a specific human-numeracy finding. Compact contrast: [directional/binary property steering] InterPLM/ProtSAE/chemistry-LM SAEs/Steering-PLMs—report the property increased or is PRESENT; [numeric magnitude in text LLMs] Geometry of Numerical Reasoning 2024 / Number Representations 2025—log-compressed, causally-manipulable magnitude subspaces, but in TEXT, not generative scientific design; [THIS proposal] exact numeric SET-POINT steering of the SAME property, exposing a level-dependent calibration failure. The delta from steering work is not a new property or direction but target-VALUE calibration and high-end degradation. Who uses it: interpretability researchers, protein/chemistry generative-model builders, and benchmark authors (set-point error as a new axis). Downstream, whole workflows need numbers not directions—formulation logP windows, a target TPSA for permeability, a specified helix quota—and presence-steering silently under/overshoots them. Deliverable: a set-point-error benchmark plus the log-reparameterized dial as a drop-in fix.
Abstract: Real scientific design specifies numbers, not directions: a chemist needs logP = 2.5, an enzyme engineer needs 40% helix content, not merely 'more'. Interpretability-guided design steers language-model features to hit properties, but every demonstrated result reports only that the property increased or appeared. Our single falsifiable claim: scientific design features are presence-steerable but not set-point calibrated—steering the SAME property along the SAME direction moves it monotonically yet cannot dial it to a specified numeric target, and control degrades sharply at high magnitudes. We name this the magnitude blind spot and define it operationally before any experiment. Borrowing a well-established cognitive-science result—that language models encode numeric magnitude in a logarithmically-compressed, causally-manipulable subspace—we test whether scientific generators inherit this compression and whether it undermines quantitative control. Using ESM-2 protein LMs and a SMILES chemical LM with sparse autoencoders and exact continuous oracles (RDKit logP/MW/TPSA; DSSP helix/sheet; GRAVY), we LOCATE presence features and magnitude directions; CAUSALLY test presence-steerability vs calibrated set-point steerability, measuring set-point error and reporting calibration and error-vs-target curves; INTERPRET whether the code is log-compressed and whether a log-reparameterized dial—evaluated separately on held-out targets, so the fix is not confused with the finding—restores precision; and AUDIT whether an internal magnitude-consistency signal flags off-target designs. Exact numeric targets matter for formulation logP windows and secondary-structure quotas. Either way changes evaluation: presence-only steering must report set-point error, and a calibrated dial would be a usable quantitative design knob.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (FROZEN): ESM-2 (150M/650M) for proteins and a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~15M params) for molecules. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered SAEs (Ordered can recover steerability TopK's decodable-but-inert features lack), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. Properties are chosen to have EXACT continuous oracles so 'magnitude' is unambiguous: molecules - logP, molecular weight, TPSA, aromatic-ring count (RDKit); proteins - alpha-helix and beta-sheet fraction (DSSP on ESMFold), GRAVY. Validity gates: RDKit-validity + synthetic accessibility (molecules), ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity (proteins). Data: 20,000 held-out objects per domain to fit probes/directions; first confirm the frozen model natively spans a wide magnitude RANGE per property. Steering = add alpha*d_hat; alpha searched over a dense grid within the validity budget per target.

Experiment 1 (H1 - categorical PRESENCE is cleanly, causally steerable): On held-out objects, train a presence classifier (property above/below median) from SAE features and raw activations and identify the top presence feature. Steer to push the property across the median (the presence task). Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: presence-flip success rate. Decision band: success >= 0.80 AND >= 0.40 over random control for >=2/3 of properties => presence is a clean handle (H1 holds); [0.15,0.40) over control => inconclusive; < 0.15 => presence not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - the internal magnitude code is not calibrated: steering is monotone yet cannot dial to a specified numeric target): For each property, define a ladder of numeric set-points spanning the native range (e.g., logP = -1, 1, 3, 5). Steer the top magnitude direction (difference-of-means high-vs-low bins and regression-weight direction) and search alpha to best hit each target. Decisive metric FIRST: SET-POINT HIT-RATE within a tolerance band (logP +/-0.5; helix-fraction +/-0.05), plus the mean |achieved - requested| SET-POINT ERROR and a monotonicity check Spearman(alpha, property). Decision band: property is monotone in alpha (rho >= 0.90) BUT hit-rate <= 0.40 AND the presence-vs-set-point success gap >= 0.40 => monotone-but-uncalibrated confirmed (H2); hit-rate in (0.40,0.60) => partial; hit-rate >= 0.60 => a calibrated dial exists out of the box, refuting H2.

Experiment 3 (H3 - the magnitude code is logarithmically compressed, so control degrades sharply at high magnitudes): Fit both linear and log(value) regressions of the property on steering displacement and compare fits; regress SET-POINT ERROR on the requested magnitude. Decisive metric FIRST: the slope of set-point error vs requested magnitude, and the log-vs-linear Delta-R^2. Decision band: error slope > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 (error grows with magnitude) AND log-fit Delta-R^2 >= 0.10 over linear => log-compression confirmed (H3); slope CI crossing 0 or Delta-R^2 in (0.03,0.10) => inconclusive; flat error and Delta-R^2 <= 0.03 => not log-compressed (refutes H3).

Experiment 4 (H4 - the miss is a blind spot: presence/validity checks pass while the number is wrong): Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between output-side checks (validity, presence-classifier confidence, pseudo-perplexity, model likelihood) and the true set-point error from Experiment 2. Decision band: |rho| <= 0.20 => checks pass while the number is wrong (blind spot confirmed); |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; |rho| >= 0.40 => checks already reveal the miss (weakens H4). ROBUSTNESS: both domains, two model sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, multiple properties; report where the compression exponent and blind spot are stable vs artifact; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.

ADDED BASELINES (beyond SAE-feature steering): (i) generic activation steering on the raw residual stream (difference-of-means/regression direction, no SAE); (ii) black-box prompt/latent optimization toward the numeric target (search decoding/latent to minimize set-point error). Both compared on set-point hit-rate and error-vs-target curve. FINDING-vs-FIX SEPARATION (pre-registered): Experiments 1-3 establish the failure; the log-reparameterized dial is fit on a held-out strength sweep and evaluated ONLY on unseen targets, so the fix cannot be confused with the finding. REPORTING: calibration plots (achieved vs requested) and error-vs-requested-magnitude curves, not just success rates. ABLATIONS: target range, tolerance-band width, layer choice, SAE sparsity/width, and direction-construction method (difference-of-means vs regression-weight vs SAE latent); the compression exponent must be stable across seeds. ORACLE LIMITS: lead with exact molecular oracles (RDKit) for core claims; DSSP-on-ESMFold helix fraction is a structure-prediction proxy and reported as corroborating, with fidelity noted so claims do not hinge on proxy noise.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Property oracles differ in exactness—RDKit logP/MW/TPSA are effectively exact for the definition, while DSSP-on-ESMFold helix fraction is a structure-prediction proxy; we lead with the exact molecular oracles for core claims and treat protein results as corroborating, reporting oracle fidelity. 2) The magnitude-blind-spot is partly an ABSENCE-of-calibration claim; we mitigate by trying multiple directions (SAE feature, difference-of-means, regression-weight), TopK and Ordered SAEs, strength search per target, and by head-to-head confirming the PRESENCE task succeeds in the same pipeline—so failure to hit numbers is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuinely calibrated dial exists) is equally publishable. 3) Set-point error could be confounded by validity collapse near range extremes; we restrict to strengths within the validity budget and separately report the in-validity error curve. 4) The log-reparameterization fix could merely fit noise; we fit the calibration on a held-out strength sweep and evaluate on unseen targets, and report the exponent's stability across seeds. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with multiple SAE variants, layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) An internal magnitude probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (presence-steerable, magnitude-log-compressed-and-uncalibrated) and the calibration fix and audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If calibrated set-point control already works out of the box, that is a valuable positive result establishing that interpretable features provide a usable quantitative dial for scientific design.

Name: convergence_order_rigidity
Title: Coarse Before Fine, or Broken: Is the Property Convergence Order of Scientific Diffusion Generators a Rigid Physical Schedule or a Controllable Design Knob?
Short Hypothesis: During iterative generation of proteins and molecules, structural/property attributes get 'locked in' in a stable coarse-to-fine ORDER (global topology/scaffold early, fine local detail late). We run the first causal test of whether this order is a RIGID model-internal schedule or a controllable design knob, and separate three contributions: (i) MEASURING the convergence order, (ii) a CAUSAL reordering test, and (iii) an ORDER-VIOLATION alarm. We hypothesize order rigidity: interpretable-feature interventions can shift a property's timing WITHIN its natural slot, but REORDERING—forcing a fine property to converge before its coarse prerequisite—silently produces invalid objects because coarse-then-fine is a model-internal dependency (we deliberately say model-internal, not 'hard physical,' since external validity is not directly tested). We further hypothesize an intervention-free order-violation signal (early firing of a late-slot feature before its coarse prerequisite has stabilized) predicts these silent failures and enables early abort during expensive sampling. Unlike architected coarse-to-fine molecular diffusion, we study EMERGENT order in frozen generators.
Related Work: A consistent coarse-to-fine convergence ORDER during iterative generation is documented across modalities but only DESCRIPTIVELY and never in scientific design: TIDE (2025) shows DiTs lock in 3D structure, then object class, then fine concepts; the audio-SAE paper (2025) finds DiffRhythm converges pitch first, then timbre, then loudness; 'Emergence and Evolution of Interpretable Concepts in Diffusion Models' (2025) finds composition locks early and style mid-process; DLM-Scope (2026) analyzes decoding order in diffusion language models. In scientific generation, my prior causal_timing_window_design proposal maps WHEN to intervene for a FIXED property (its causal window) but assumes the property's slot is given; all other scientific-steering work (InterPLM, ProtSAE, FoldSAE, ProtoMech) is single-pass or uniform-strength and never studies the convergence schedule at all. NO prior work (a) establishes that scientific diffusion generators have a stable coarse-to-fine property convergence order, (b) tests whether that ORDER is causally reorderable via interpretable features vs a rigid physical dependency, or (c) shows that violating the natural order silently breaks validity and provides an internal order-violation alarm. This reframes convergence order from a descriptive curiosity into a hard design constraint and a controllability/validity question—distinct from both the descriptive cross-modal order literature and from timing-window steering. One-sentence novelty: this is the first causal test of whether the property convergence ORDER of scientific diffusion generators is rigid or reorderable. Positioning: descriptive cross-modal order work (TIDE 2025; audio-SAE 2025; Emergence of Interpretable Concepts 2025; DLM-Scope 2026) documents a coarse-to-fine order but never intervenes on it and never in scientific design; my prior causal_timing_window work maps WHEN to intervene for a FIXED property but assumes its slot is given. Crucially, coarse-to-fine molecular diffusion models that are ARCHITECTED to be hierarchical do not bear on our question—we study EMERGENT order in FROZEN generators, asking whether order is a model-internal dependency rather than a design choice. Why scientific generation differs from image/audio/language: here 'coarse' (fold topology, scaffold) is a physical prerequisite for 'fine' (a motif-in-fold, a substituent-on-scaffold), so violating the order plausibly breaks structural VALIDITY, a failure mode with no analogue in style-before-detail image generation. Beyond the niche, interpretability and controllable-diffusion researchers would cite the reordering test and the order-violation alarm.
Abstract: Iterative generative models—across images, audio, and language—lock in attributes in a strikingly consistent coarse-to-fine order: global structure before fine detail. We run the first causal test of whether this convergence ORDER is rigid or reorderable in scientific diffusion generators of proteins and molecules. This matters because real design often wants to prioritize a fine property (a motif, a functional group) while a coarse prerequisite (fold topology, scaffold) is still forming, and it is unknown whether a frozen model can honor such a request or will silently fail. Unlike coarse-to-fine molecular diffusion models that are ARCHITECTED to be hierarchical, we study EMERGENT order in frozen generators. We separate three contributions: measuring the property convergence order, a causal reordering test, and an order-violation alarm. We hypothesize order rigidity: interpretable-feature interventions shift a property's timing WITHIN its natural slot, but REORDERING—forcing a fine property to converge before its coarse prerequisite—yields objects that pass fluency/validity spot-checks yet are structurally broken, indicating a model-internal (not merely stylistic) coarse-to-fine dependency. Using protein and molecular diffusion generators with sparse autoencoders on per-timestep denoiser activations, we MEASURE convergence order against hard oracles, CAUSALLY test reordering versus in-slot timing shifts with strength sweeps and null controls, test whether coarse features gate fine ones, and AUDIT whether an intervention-free order-violation signal flags silently-broken designs for early abort during expensive sampling. Either way is informative: rigidity tells wet-lab pipelines not to request fine properties before coarse prerequisites; free reorderability would overturn the cross-modal coarse-to-fine dogma for scientific generators.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models with accessible per-step denoiser activations (FROZEN): a discrete/masked-diffusion protein LM (DPLM-style) and a molecular diffusion model over SMILES/graphs. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and temporally-conditioned (TIDE-style) SAEs on the denoiser residual stream at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations, seeds 0/1/2. COARSE properties: protein overall secondary-structure content / fold topology (contact-order proxy via DSSP on ESMFold), molecule scaffold/ring-system and aromatic-ring count (RDKit). FINE properties: protein single local motif (HMMER/regex) or a specific loop, molecule single functional group (SMARTS). Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity (proteins), RDKit-validity + synthetic accessibility (molecules). Data: 10,000 unsteered generations per domain to establish convergence order, and >=10 matched coarse/fine property pairs. Steering/forcing = clamp or add alpha*d_hat to the property-linked feature at chosen denoising timesteps; alpha within the validity budget.

Experiment 1 (H1 - attributes lock in in a stable coarse-to-fine ORDER): For the unsteered generations, at each denoising timestep measure how well each property's SAE feature/probe on partial activations predicts the FINISHED object's property; define each property's CONVERGENCE TIME as the timestep at which this prediction stabilizes above threshold. Cross-check with an SAE-independent raw-activation probe. Decisive metric FIRST: the coarse-minus-fine convergence-time gap, paired across property pairs and both domains. Decision band: coarse converges earlier than fine with mean gap >= 15% of the denoising schedule, paired-test p < 0.01, effect size dz >= 0.5 => coarse-to-fine order confirmed (H1); gap in (0,15%) => weak/inconclusive; gap <= 0 => no coarse-to-fine order (refutes H1).

Experiment 2 (H2 - the order is a RIGID schedule: in-slot timing shifts succeed but REORDERING silently breaks the object): For matched coarse/fine pairs run (a) an IN-SLOT timing shift (move a property earlier/later while keeping coarse-before-fine) and (b) a REORDER (clamp the fine feature strongly at early timesteps to converge before its coarse prerequisite has stabilized). Systems also include random-direction and matched-non-property controls. Decisive metric FIRST: the REORDER-VALIDITY GAP = (structural-validity/property-success under in-slot) minus (under reorder) at matched steering budget, and the SILENT-BREAKAGE RATE = fraction of reordered generations that satisfy the fine property and pass fluency/RDKit checks yet fail structural validity (pLDDT < 50 or broken scaffold). Decision band: in-slot validity retention >= 0.80 while reorder validity <= 0.50 (gap >= 0.30) AND silent-breakage >= 0.30 => rigid coarse-then-fine dependency confirmed (H2); gap in (0.10,0.30) => partial; gap <= 0.10 => order is freely reorderable (refutes H2). A dependency-asymmetry check (ablating the coarse prerequisite delays/prevents fine convergence, while the reverse ablation does not) supports a directional coarse->fine gate.

Experiment 3 (H3 - an intervention-free order-violation signal predicts the silent failures): First show invisibility: Spearman rho between output-side checks (pseudo-perplexity, RDKit-validity, the fine-property predictor's confidence) and true structural validity of reordered generations; band |rho| <= 0.20 => breakage is silent. Then deploy the no-intervention ORDER-VIOLATION signal = early firing of a late-slot feature while its coarse-prerequisite feature has not yet stabilized. Decisive metric FIRST: AUROC predicting the eventually-broken reordered generations, plus the earliest-reliable-detection timestep. Systems: order-violation signal vs the output-side detectors. Decision band: internal AUROC >= 0.75 AND >= 0.10 over the best output-side detector => the alarm is confirmed (and enables early abort); margin (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; margin <= 0.05 => no better (reported honestly). ROBUSTNESS: both domains, two checkpoints, shared vs temporally-conditioned SAEs, multiple property pairs; test whether rigidity is stronger for physically-dependent pairs (motif-in-fold) than weakly-coupled pairs; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.

PRE-REGISTERED DEFINITIONS. CONVERGENCE TIME of a property = the earliest denoising timestep t* at which a frozen probe on partial activations predicts the finished object's property above a threshold theta and stays above it for the rest of the schedule (theta = midpoint between the probe's random-init and final-step accuracy; pre-set, not tuned on results). CAUSAL-NECESSITY control: directly intervene on the coarse-prerequisite feature (clamp/ablate) and test whether fine convergence changes ASYMMETRICALLY—ablating coarse should delay/prevent fine convergence while ablating fine should not affect coarse; this asymmetry is the direct test of a coarse-to-fine gate. STRENGTH SWEEPS & NULL CONTROLS: sweep reorder-forcing strength and include random-direction and matched-non-property clamps, so a reorder failure is not an underpowered-steering artifact. ORACLE UNCERTAINTY: correlate proxy validity (ESMFold pLDDT, RDKit) with any available stronger structural metric and report sensitivity of convergence-time and breakage conclusions to ESMFold/RDKit error (bootstrap over oracle noise). ALARM BASELINES: compare the interpretable order-violation signal against (i) a black-box raw-activation probe-only alarm and (ii) a random alarm, to show the claimed signal is not trivially matched.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Requires generators with accessible per-step denoiser activations; scope limited to instrumentable open iterative models (masked-diffusion protein/molecule generators). 2) In-silico oracles (ESMFold, DSSP, RDKit, HMMER) are proxies for wet-lab truth; claims concern model-internal convergence scheduling, controllability, and structural validity, not experimental function—stated explicitly. 3) The rigidity claim is partly an ABSENCE claim (reordering cannot be done without breakage); we mitigate by trying multiple reordering interventions (feature clamping, difference-of-means, activation forcing) and strengths, and by confirming that IN-SLOT timing shifts DO succeed in the same pipeline—so a reordering failure is meaningful, not a weak-intervention artifact. A positive result (order is freely reorderable) is equally publishable and would overturn the cross-modal coarse-to-fine dogma for scientific generators. 4) Convergence-order and validity may be confounded with generic off-distribution drift; random-direction and matched-non-property controls, plus the in-slot-vs-reorder contrast, isolate the order-specific effect. 5) Coarse and fine properties may be irreducibly entangled for some pairs; we select pairs with a clear physical coarse→fine dependency (motif-within-fold, substituent-on-scaffold) and report weakly-coupled pairs separately. 6) SAE quality / layer / temporal-conditioning could confound convergence-time measurement; controlled with shared and temporally-conditioned SAEs, multiple layers, and raw-activation probes. 7) The internal order-violation alarm might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, its interpretability (naming the violated dependency) and the early-abort compute savings are the contributions, reported honestly. 8) Checkpoint/timestep spacing may miss sharp convergence transitions; we densify timestep sampling around detected transitions.

Name: steering_hysteresis
Title: No Undo Button: Does Interpretable-Feature Steering Leave Irreversible Scars on Scientific Generative Designs?
Short Hypothesis: We ask whether interpretable-feature steering in scientific generative models is a reversible knob. We hypothesize it is NOT: applying a feature-steer and then removing it (or applying the exact opposite steer) does not return generation to its original design, but leaves a persistent scar -- residual, often unintended changes in the finished object. We predict this steering hysteresis is SYSTEMATIC (a stable residual direction across seeds, above a sampling-noise floor AND above permuted-vector/random-switch nulls, not noise), LARGER for iterative/autoregressive generation where an early perturbation contaminates all downstream decisions, and PREDICTED by how early the steer is applied and by feature-decoder overlap. If so, the naive undo/adjust workflow designers assume is silently unreliable, and REVERSIBILITY -- not just forward property gain -- must become a standard evaluation axis for controllable design. If false, steering is validated as reversible, strengthening confidence in undo/adjust workflows.
Related Work: Nearly all interpretability-guided design work (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; 'Interpreting and Steering PLMs through SAEs' 2025; the chemistry/diffusion SAE steering papers; DLM-Scope 2026; 'Enabling Precise Topic Alignment via SAEs' 2025) treats a steering vector as a reversible, dial-like control: add it to move a property, implicitly assuming you can dial it back or fine-tune around it. Steering is always evaluated in the FORWARD direction (does the target property appear?) and never for REVERSIBILITY. Separately, a physics/biology literature on representation irreversibility (Nonequilibrium Latent Cycles 2025; Measuring irreversibility from learned representations 2023; LENS 2025) shows learned dynamics can break detailed balance and be time-asymmetric, and the position paper 'Beyond Equilibrium' (2025) argues generative processes are often irreversible—but none connects this to feature-steering controllability of DESIGNS. No prior work (a) tests whether steer-then-unsteer returns a scientific generator to its original design, (b) quantifies steering hysteresis as a controllability-reliability failure, or (c) ties hysteresis magnitude to steer timing and feature geometry. This reframes the ubiquitous assumption of reversible control—distinct from all my prior proposals (compositionality, off-mode reach, side-effect drift), which assume a single forward steer and never study the undo operation. We separate three contributions so reviewers can weigh them independently: a FINDING (steer-then-unsteer leaves systematic scars), a MECHANISM hypothesis (early perturbations contaminate later autoregressive/iterative decisions, so scar size tracks steer earliness and feature-decoder overlap), and a BENCHMARK/protocol (reversibility measured under matched seeds, a sampling-noise floor, and permuted-vector nulls, on valid reversed objects only). The exact delta: prior steering work tests the FORWARD direction (does the property appear?) and, in text LLMs, at most re-steering; none tests steer-then-unsteer reversibility on scientific generators with valid-object controls. If the result holds, SAE-steering researchers and molecular/protein design practitioners should report a reversibility metric alongside forward property gain and treat iterative design/optimization loops as accumulating irreversible scars.
Abstract: Designers using interpretable-feature steering treat it like a knob: add a feature vector to increase a property and, implicitly, dial it back or adjust around it if you overshoot. We ask whether this reversibility assumption holds for scientific generative models. Because generation is a nonlinear, path-dependent process (especially autoregressive decoding and iterative diffusion), a steering perturbation applied partway through generation may contaminate every subsequent decision, so removing the steer -- or applying the exact opposite steer -- need not return the model to where it started. We call this candidate effect steering hysteresis: the finished object after a steer-then-unsteer cycle differs persistently from the unsteered baseline, leaving unintended scars in properties the designer never touched. Whether it exists, and how large it is, is exactly what we test. Using ESM-2 protein language models and a SMILES chemical language model with sparse autoencoders, we (1) MEASURE hysteresis via a steer-then-reverse protocol against a sampling-noise floor and permuted-vector nulls; (2) test whether it is SYSTEMATIC rather than noise; (3) INTERPRET whether its magnitude is predicted by steer earliness and feature-decoder overlap; and (4) AUDIT whether the naive undo workflow silently fails and whether a simple scheduling fix reduces scars. If hysteresis is real, reversibility -- not just forward property gain -- becomes a necessary evaluation axis, and SAE-steering researchers and molecular/protein designers must treat undo/adjust and iterative optimization loops as accumulating irreversible change; if false, steering is validated as reversible, directly strengthening those same workflows.
Experiments:
Shared setup (fixed once, reused below). MODELS (frozen): ESM-2 at 150M and 650M params (public checkpoints) for proteins; a GPT-style autoregressive SMILES chemical LM (~85M params, trained on the ~1.9M-molecule MOSES corpus, or an equivalent public checkpoint) for molecules. Models are FROZEN; only SAEs/probes are trainable. SAEs: TopK SAE on the residual stream at one layer chosen by an intrinsic-dimension elbow heuristic (plus a second layer for robustness), dictionary width 16x, k=32, Adam lr 1e-3, ~40M activation tokens, seeds {0,1,2}; reconstruction accepted only at fraction-variance-unexplained <=0.2. Difference-of-means directions serve as a non-SAE baseline. ORACLES (exact/cheap): proteins -- alpha-helix/beta-sheet content via DSSP on ESMFold structures, GRAVY, molecular weight, motif presence (HMMER/regex); molecules -- logP, QED, ring/aromatic count, functional groups (RDKit SMARTS). VALIDITY gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity (proteins), RDKit-validity + synthetic accessibility (molecules); core analyses restricted to reversed objects that remain valid. DISTANCE metrics: sequence identity / edit distance and embedding distance (proteins); Tanimoto / canonical-SMILES match and graph edit distance (molecules). FEATURE BANK: ~30 property-linked features per domain (concept-correlation / probe AUROC on held-out natural objects). Compute: two frozen ESM-2 sizes + one small SMILES LM on 1-2 GPUs, academic-feasible. Statistics: per-feature tests are paired, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control across the feature/layer/property grid and bootstrap CIs on all effect sizes.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- feature steering leaves a persistent scar; it is not a reversible knob): Tests that steer-then-reverse does not return generation to the unsteered design. Data: from the SAME initial condition (fixed seed / masked template / prompt), 500 matched triplets per feature per domain, features drawn from the bank. Each triplet: (A) unsteered baseline, (B) steer forward with feature f at strength s for part of generation, (C) steer-then-reverse -- apply +s then, after a switch point, either drop the vector ("remove") or apply -s ("symmetric reverse"); both reversal modes are run and reported separately (not assumed equivalent). MATCHED-PERTURBATION CONTROL: a steer-then-reverse run using a matched-norm RANDOM/permuted vector (same total perturbation budget, same switch point) isolates path dependence from generic perturbation. Decisive metric first: PERSISTENT-FRACTION = fraction of the forward property change (B vs A) that remains in C vs A on the TARGET property; then off-target scar magnitude across the full off-target oracle battery; then object distance (identity / Tanimoto) between C and A. Convincing: median persistent-fraction >= 0.2 with a paired test clearing Experiment 2's noise floor, for a majority of features in both domains. Undecidable band: persistent-fraction in [0.05, 0.15) and within the noise floor -> not distinguishable from reversible; report as no-scar. Negative result (persistent-fraction < 0.05, off-target scar within noise): steering IS reversible -- a clean, publishable positive result validating the undo/adjust workflow.

Experiment 2 (H2 -- the hysteresis is systematic, not sampling noise): Tests that scars exceed stochastic drift and point in a consistent direction. Noise floor: 500 pairs of independent UNSTEERED runs from seed-perturbed initial conditions per domain, giving the baseline property/distance spread. NULL MODELS for path dependence: rerun the protocol with (i) permuted steering vectors and (ii) randomized switch points -- genuine hysteresis must exceed BOTH nulls, not merely the sampling-noise floor. Decisive metric first: standardized effect size of steer-then-reverse persistent-fraction ABOVE the noise floor (Cohen's d), then residual-DIRECTION consistency across seeds (cosine of the C-minus-A property/embedding shift, tested against a matched-norm random-direction control) via a mixed-effects model with CIs. Convincing: d >= 0.8 above floor AND mean residual-direction cosine >= 0.3 with CI excluding 0. Undecidable band: d in [0.2, 0.5) OR direction cosine CI overlapping [−0.1, 0.1] -> scar not separable from noise; H1 is downgraded to "not established". Negative result (d < 0.2): hysteresis is indistinguishable from sampling noise -- reported as reversibility.

Experiment 3 (H3 -- hysteresis is larger for iterative/autoregressive generation): Tests that an early perturbation contaminates downstream decisions more in sequential generation. Systems compared: autoregressive SMILES generation and autoregressive vs masked-infilling ESM-2 protein generation, versus a near-instantaneous single-step steer as a low-hysteresis control. Decisive metric first: persistent-fraction (and off-target scar) for iterative/autoregressive vs single-step generation at matched forward property gain. Convincing: iterative/autoregressive persistent-fraction exceeds the single-step control by an effect size d >= 0.5, and autoregressive exceeds masked-infilling. Undecidable band: d in [0.1, 0.3) -> generation-mode dependence present but weak; report, do not headline. Negative result (d < 0.1 or reversed sign): hysteresis is not driven by sequential contamination -- refines the mechanism claim and is reported as such.

Experiment 4 (H4 -- scar magnitude is predicted by steer earliness and feature-decoder overlap): Tests the two named predictors. Design: sweep the SWITCH POINT across >=5 positions from early to late in generation, and for each feature compute feature-decoder overlap (cosine of f's decoder direction with other property directions). Decisive metric first: out-of-sample R^2 of a regressor predicting per-steer persistent-fraction from {switch-point, feature-decoder overlap}, compared against a concept-correlation-only baseline (nested-model comparison). Convincing: the two predictors reach R^2 >= 0.3 and add >= 0.1 R^2 over concept-correlation, with earlier switch points and higher overlap both associated with larger scars (signs as hypothesized, CIs excluding 0). Undecidable band: predictor R^2 in [0.1, 0.2) or added-R^2 in [0.03, 0.1) -> weak predictors; report coefficients, withhold the predictive claim. Negative result (added-R^2 < 0.03): earliness/overlap do not predict scars -- the hypothesized mechanism is unsupported; report which alternative correlates (e.g., strength) if any.

Experiment 5 (payoff -- forward-only evaluation misses hysteresis, and a scheduling fix reduces it): Tests the "silently unreliable" claim and a mitigation. Blind spot: decisive metric first -- correlation between forward property gain/validity (B vs A) and residual scar (C vs A); convincing if |r| <= 0.2 (a "successful" steer carries no signal about its scar). Mitigation: apply/remove the steer only within a late causal window (or ramp strength); decisive metric -- scar reduction at MATCHED forward property gain, tracing a control-vs-reversibility frontier. Convincing: >= 30% scar reduction at matched gain. Undecidable band: forward-vs-scar |r| in [0.2, 0.4) (blind spot partial) or scar reduction in [10%, 30%) (fix marginal) -> report the frontier without a strong claim. Negative result: forward metrics already predict scars (|r| > 0.4) or the fix gives <10% reduction -- the workflow is not silently unreliable / the fix does not help, reported honestly.

Experiment 6 (robustness of H1-H4): Repeat across both domains, both ESM-2 sizes, autoregressive vs masked-infilling protein generation, TopK vs difference-of-means directions, two layers, and >=3 properties per domain; report the fraction of cells where hysteresis, its systematicity, the generation-mode effect, and the predictors replicate. A result stable in <50% of cells is reported as regime-specific.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) In-silico oracles (ESMFold, DSSP, RDKit, HMMER) are proxies for wet-lab truth; claims concern model-internal controllability and design reproducibility, not experimental function—stated explicitly. 2) Generation is inherently stochastic, so distinguishing hysteresis from sampling noise is essential; we mitigate with a carefully matched noise-floor baseline (independent unsteered runs), paired same-seed comparisons, direction-consistency tests, and random-direction controls—if hysteresis does not exceed the floor, that is itself a clean, publishable positive result establishing that steering IS reversible. 3) 'Remove steer' vs 'symmetric reverse' may behave differently; we report both rather than assume equivalence. 4) Hysteresis could be trivially explained by validity collapse; we restrict core analysis to the regime where reversed objects remain valid and report scars separately. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound both scar and geometry; controlled with multiple SAE variants, layers, and difference-of-means baselines. 6) The timing/geometry predictors may be property- or model-specific; we test multiple properties, sizes, and generation modes and report where they fail. 7) The scheduling fix may reduce forward property gain; we quantify the control-vs-reversibility tradeoff rather than assume a free lunch.

Name: causal_timing_window_design
Title: The Right Feature at the Right Time: Causal Intervention Windows for Interpretable Control of Biomolecular Diffusion Models
Short Hypothesis: Our claim is not the general idea that timing matters (already established for image/text diffusion) but a biomolecule-specific stratification law plus a hard-property causal test. During iterative diffusion generation of proteins and molecules, each interpretable feature has a distinct CAUSAL WINDOW—a range of denoising timesteps where clamping it actually decides an objectively verifiable property (fold topology, secondary-structure content, a motif, a functional group), outside of which the same intervention is inert or destroys validity. We hypothesize (i) a stratification law: property classes order by window—coarse/topological properties decided early, fine/local properties late—more sharply than in pixel-space diffusion because biomolecular validity is a hard physical constraint; and (ii) intervening only inside a feature's causal window hits the target property with far higher validity and far fewer wasted intervention steps than steering uniformly across all timesteps or at a single pass.
Related Work: Image-diffusion interpretability shows temporally-structured concept emergence: 'Emergence and Evolution of Interpretable Concepts in Diffusion Models' (2025) finds composition locks in early and style mid-process; TIDE (2025) builds temporal-aware SAEs; 'Unraveling the Temporal Dynamics of the Unet' (2023) finds composition/denoising phases. DLM-Scope (2026) does diffusion-time SAE steering for text but does not characterize property-specific causal windows. In the scientific-object space, all steering work (InterPLM 2024, ProtSAE 2025, ProtoMech 2026, antibody-SAE 2025, automated-neuron-labelling 2025) either uses masked/autoregressive models with single-pass interventions or applies steering uniformly, and none studies WHEN during a diffusion denoising trajectory an interpretable feature is causally decisive for a hard, verifiable property. The protein-DPO paper (2026) reports a training-time temporal decoupling of structure vs property, but concerns fine-tuning dynamics, not inference-time feature interventions. We are the first to (a) map property-class-specific causal intervention windows for interpretable features in biomolecular diffusion generation, (b) show that window-targeted intervention beats uniform/single-pass steering on the validity–control frontier, and (c) turn timing into an efficiency lever (fewer intervention steps, cheaper compute) for scientific design. The exact delta from the closest prior family (temporal-SAE and diffusion-time steering papers on images/text): they show concepts emerge at different times and can be steered per-timestep, but never establish, on a hard verifiable property, a per-feature window OUTSIDE of which intervention is causally inert, nor a property-class stratification law, nor an efficiency accounting of intervention steps saved.
Abstract: Controllable design of proteins and molecules increasingly clamps interpretable features to hit target properties, but nearly all methods apply the intervention at the same strength at every step of an iterative generative process—wasting compute and often breaking validity. Work on image diffusion shows interpretable concepts emerge and lock in at different stages (composition early, style late), implying that WHEN you intervene matters as much as WHAT. We ask whether biomolecular diffusion models have analogous property-specific causal windows and whether exploiting them makes design more valid and efficient. Using protein diffusion models and a SMILES/graph molecular diffusion model, we train sparse autoencoders on per-timestep denoiser activations, link features to hard, verifiable properties (secondary structure, fold topology, motifs; ring systems, functional groups, logP band), and measure each feature's causal effect on the finished object when clamped only within a sliding timestep window—yielding a Causal Timing Map. We test two hypotheses: (1) a stratification law, coarse/topological properties decided early and fine/local ones late; (2) window-targeted intervention Pareto-dominates uniform and single-pass steering on a control-validity frontier while using far fewer intervention steps. A designer who wants a specific fold AND a late-stage functional motif would otherwise fight interference by steering everything everywhere; a timing schedule assigns each property to its window instead. We report timing maps, frontier comparisons, an accounting of intervention steps saved, and a simple scheduling recipe—establishing timing as a first-class, efficiency-boosting control axis for interpretable scientific design.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Generators (both instrumentable for per-step denoiser activations, frozen): (a) a discrete/masked protein diffusion or order-agnostic protein LM (a masked-diffusion ESM-style model or a DPLM-type model) and (b) a molecular diffusion model over SMILES/graphs. Hard automated evaluators so "the property in the finished object" is unambiguous: proteins - alpha-helix/beta-sheet % (DSSP on ESMFold), a fold-topology/contact-order proxy, GRAVY, molecular weight, motifs (HMMER/regex, e.g. zinc-finger); molecules - ring count / aromatic-ring presence, specific functional groups (RDKit SMARTS), a logP band, QED. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT and pseudo-perplexity (proteins); RDKit-validity and synthetic accessibility (molecules). Temporal SAEs: TopK SAEs (k=32, dictionary 16,384) on the denoiser residual stream, both a timestep-shared variant and a temporally-conditioned (TIDE-style) variant, at the intrinsic-dimension-elbow layer; reconstruction fidelity and per-timestep concept-correlation with each hard property reported on held-out generations. "Clamp within a window" = fixing a feature to a strong value only for timesteps inside a specified window. Generation seeds: 5; 200 objects per condition.

Experiment 1 (H1 - each feature has a distinct causal window): Tests whether clamping a property-linked feature decides the finished-object property only inside a specific timestep window and is inert or destructive outside it. Decisive metric: window-localized causal effect = property change in the finished object per intervened step, as a function of window position/width (the Causal Timing Map). Convincing result: for >= 70% of property features there exists a window whose per-step effect is >= 2x the effect of clamping uniformly across the whole trajectory, AND clamping only outside that window changes the property by < 25% of the in-window effect. Decision band: an above-baseline window exists but its per-step effect is only 1.3-2x uniform -> weak localization; report as partial support. Negative result (no window beats uniform clamping) refutes H1. Data: non-overlapping timestep bins covering the trajectory plus growing/shrinking windows, per feature, with strength swept inside each window so timing effects are reported controlling for steering strength. Controls disentangle timing from confounds: a random/non-semantic-feature clamp (matched activation magnitude) must show no localized window, and window-localized effects are compared across properties of matched difficulty and features of matched prevalence, so a 'window' is not merely an easy-property or high-prevalence artifact.

Experiment 2 (H2a - properties stratify by window: coarse early, fine late): Tests whether coarse/topological properties are decided earlier than fine/local ones. Decisive metric: difference in mean causal-window center (as a fraction of the trajectory) between coarse properties (fold class, overall structure content, scaffold ring system) and fine ones (a single motif, one functional group), from a mixed-effects regression of window-center on property class. Convincing result: coarse centers earlier by >= 15% of the trajectory with the 95% CI excluding 0, in both domains. Decision band: difference in [5%, 15%] of the trajectory -> a trend, not decisive. Negative or reversed result (fine decided as early or earlier) refutes H2a but is still an informative characterization. We also test whether window center aligns with when the feature's concept-correlation first becomes predictive of the final object during unsteered generation.

Experiment 3 (H2b - window-targeted intervention dominates uniform/single-pass and saves steps): Tests whether intervening only inside each feature's mapped window beats standard uniform or single-pass steering. Decisive metric: control-validity frontier area (property success rate vs validity retention). Convincing result: window-targeted steering dominates the frontier AND uses >= 40% fewer intervention steps than uniform steering at matched property success. Decision band: frontier parity but >= 40% fewer steps, OR frontier dominance with < 40% step savings -> a partial win on one axis; report both. Negative result (no frontier or efficiency advantage) refutes H2b. Systems: (a) uniform steering across all timesteps, (b) single-pass/late-only steering, (c) window-targeted steering. Multi-property scheduling: for 2-3 properties with different windows, assign each to its own window and test whether temporal separation lowers interference versus co-applying all interventions at every step. Robustness across both domains, two checkpoints/sizes, and shared vs temporally-conditioned SAEs.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Requires generators with accessible per-step activations; if a target model's diffusion process is not easily instrumented we substitute alternatives, limiting generality to instrumentable models. 2) In-silico evaluators (ESMFold, DSSP, RDKit) are proxies for wet-lab function; claims concern model-internal causal timing and controllability, not experimental viability. 3) Causal windows may be entangled with steering strength; we sweep strength within each window and report timing effects controlling for strength. 4) Temporally-shared SAEs may blur timestep-specific features; we mitigate with temporally-conditioned SAEs and report differences. 5) The stratification hypothesis could fail (some fine properties decided early); a null or reversed result is still an informative, publishable characterization. 6) Feature-property linkage relies on concept-correlation, which can be non-causal; the sliding-window clamp is itself the causal test, so we treat correlation only as a candidate-selection step. 7) Efficiency gains depend on how much of the trajectory the causal window occupies; if windows are broad, savings shrink—this is directly quantified rather than assumed.

Name: dimensional_consistency_blindspot_symbolic_regression
Title: Right Numbers, Wrong Units: Do Neural Symbolic-Regression Models Represent Dimensional Consistency, or Fit Numbers That Silently Violate the Laws of Physics?
Short Hypothesis: Transformer-based neural symbolic-regression (NSR) models possess interpretable, causally-steerable internal features for the NUMERICAL fit of a candidate equation (how well it matches data), but do NOT possess a compact, causally-steerable internal representation of DIMENSIONAL CONSISTENCY — the requirement that added/equated terms carry matching physical units. Consequently, steering a feature to improve numerical fit silently produces dimensionally invalid equations (adding a length to a time, taking log of a dimensioned quantity), a blind spot that R^2/accuracy checks miss but an exact unit-checking oracle exposes; and an intervention-free internal dimensional-consistency signal flags it. PRIMARY CLAIM (single crisp headline): in NSR transformers dimensional consistency is DECODABLE from activations but NOT compactly causally steerable, so fit-steering silently breaks units; the internal audit and the concept-vs-token-statistics test are secondary.
Related Work: Transformer/generative symbolic regression is mature: SymbolicGPT (2021), DGSR (2023), DiffuSR (2025), Controllable NSR / NSRwH (2023, which conditions on hypothesized STRUCTURE but not units), and LaSR (2024, learned concept library). Mechanistic interpretability has JUST reached this domain: PATCHES (2026) discovers operator-generating circuits in an SR transformer and finds probing/DLA capture correlational not causal features; closed-form-gradient interpretation (2024) reads symbolic concepts from latent neurons. Separately, dimensional analysis / units-aware discovery is known to matter (Buckingham-Pi-constrained SR, physics-informed SR like StruSR 2025, domain-prior SR 2025), and dimensional consistency is a HARD, exactly-checkable physical law that most black-box SR ignores. Crucially, NO prior work asks whether a neural SR model INTERNALLY represents dimensional consistency as a causal, steerable feature, contrasts fit-steerability against unit-steerability, surfaces the phenomenon that improving fit silently breaks units, or provides an internal dimensional audit. This introduces the numerical-fit vs physical-law-consistency axis into interpretability-of-generation for symbolic/mathematical objects — a genuinely new object class relative to my prior protein/molecule/DNA/RNA/crystal/reaction/cell proposals — and turns dimensional analysis (an exact oracle) into a mechanism-and-audit target. It also directly answers PATCHES's call to treat SR as a high-potential interpretability domain, by moving from operator circuits to a physically-meaningful invariant. Unlike units-constrained/physics-prior SR (Buckingham-Pi SR, StruSR), which ENFORCES dimensional consistency architecturally, we do the opposite -- we leave the model free to violate units and ask whether it INTERNALLY represents the invariant, an interpretability/audit question rather than a constraint-enforcement method, which is why this is not just another physics-prior paper. Who cares: symbolic-regression and AI-for-science practitioners (who risk publishing dimensionally-invalid 'laws'), physics-informed-discovery researchers, and interpretability researchers seeking exact, free oracles.
Abstract: Symbolic regression promises interpretable governing equations from data, and neural symbolic-regression (NSR) transformers now generate candidate equations directly. But a valid physical law must be dimensionally consistent: you cannot add a length to a time, and log/exp require dimensionless arguments. We ask a mechanistic question no prior work addresses: do NSR models internally represent dimensional consistency as a causal, steerable feature the way they represent numerical fit, or do they optimize numbers while silently violating units? We surface a behavioral phenomenon we call the dimensional blind spot: steering an interpretable feature to improve numerical fit reliably lowers error while pushing the generated equation toward dimensional inconsistency — invisible to R^2/accuracy checks but exposed exactly by unit-checking. Dimensional consistency is the ideal testbed because it is an exact, free, symbolic oracle (propagate SI dimensions through the expression tree; a valid equation has matched units at every operator). Using a transformer NSR model (SymbolicGPT/DGSR-style) trained on the Feynman equations with per-variable units, plus sparse autoencoders on its residual stream, we (1) LOCATE candidate numerical-fit features and candidate dimensional-consistency features via probing; (2) CAUSALLY test the steerability of each, contrasting fit control against unit control; (3) INTERPRET whether located units encode a genuine dimensional-type concept or shallow token statistics; and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an intervention-free dimensional-consistency signal flags silently-invalid equations better than fit or model likelihood. We predict fit is steerable while dimensional consistency is decodable-but-weakly-steerable. So what: better-fitting equations can be physically meaningless, and a cheap internal audit that prunes dimensionally-invalid candidates from the beam raises true-law recovery and saves search compute -- turning an exact, free oracle into a diagnostic and control target.
Experiments:
Shared setup (fixed once, reused below). MODEL (frozen): a transformer neural-symbolic-regression model, SymbolicGPT/DGSR-style, autoregressive over expression-tree tokens (~30-100M params), using a public checkpoint or one trained by us on the Feynman Symbolic Regression Database (100 physics equations, each with KNOWN SI units per variable) augmented with synthetic dimensioned datasets (assign SI units to variables, sample values, compute targets); ~8k train / 1k val / held-out equations for testing. The NSR model is FROZEN; only SAEs/probes are trainable. SAEs: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka on the residual stream at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer (plus a second layer), width 16x, k=32, Adam lr 1e-3, ~40M activation tokens, seeds {0,1,2}; reconstruction accepted at fraction-variance-unexplained <=0.2. DIMENSIONAL oracle (exact, deterministic, free): a unit-propagation checker that walks the generated expression tree, propagates each variable's SI dimension vector through operators (add/subtract require equal dimensions; multiply/divide add/subtract dimension vectors; log/exp/trig require a dimensionless argument; the whole equation must match the target dimension), returning a binary CONSISTENT flag and a graded VIOLATION SCORE (count/severity of mismatched operator nodes). FIT oracle: R^2 / normalized MSE of the generated equation against held-out data points. VALIDITY gate: parseable, well-formed expression tree. PRECONDITION: confirm the model natively produces a RANGE of both fit qualities AND dimensional-consistency states (consistent and inconsistent equations both occur), so absence-of-control claims are meaningful; also confirm variable units are ingested so the model COULD represent dimensions. Compute: one frozen NSR transformer + <=4 SAEs on a single GPU, academic-feasible.

PRE-REGISTERED PRIMARY ENDPOINT: the decodable-but-inert result (Experiment 2) on ONE model family (SymbolicGPT/DGSR-style) and ONE dataset (Feynman + its synthetic dimensioned augmentation) -- dimension-probe AUROC >= 0.75 with dimensional-restoration success <= 0.2 and effect < 1/3 of fit steerability; DiffuSR, second size, and second layer are secondary robustness. Steering STRENGTH is matched across fit and dimensional interventions by equalizing the induced activation-norm perturbation, making the fit-vs-units contrast budget-fair. The decision tree (support / undecidable / negative bands per experiment) is fixed before running.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- numerical-fit features ARE causally steerable): Tests that fit-linked features exist and steer the generated equation's fit. Data: 2,000 held-out (data, equation) pairs, used as-is. Identify NUMERICAL-FIT features (probe AUROC / concept-correlation for "will fit well" on held-out partial equations, retain AUROC >= 0.7). For each of >=8 fit features, sweep steering strength (6 levels), generate 100 equations per level given fixed data, and measure the DECISIVE metric first: fit gain (Delta R^2) per unit steer, with specificity and a matched-norm random-direction control. Convincing: median fit gain per unit steer with Cohen's d >= 0.8 vs random control and monotone dose-response (Spearman |rho| >= 0.6) for a majority of features. Undecidable band: d in [0.2, 0.5) or |rho| in [0.2, 0.4) -> fit-steerability unestablished for that feature; drop it from H2's head-to-head. Negative result (d < 0.2 across features): fit itself is not steerable, the blind-spot premise collapses; reported as a controllability null.

Experiment 2 (H2 -- NO compact, causally-steerable dimensional-consistency handle): Tests that dimensional consistency is decodable-but-inert. (2a decodability) Probe SAE features and raw activations to predict the running dimension type of the partial expression / whether the next operator is dimensionally legal, using partial correlation to remove fit confounds; decisive metric: dimension-probe AUROC. (2b steerability) In the SAME pipeline as Experiment 1, attempt to lower the violation score / flip to CONSISTENT while HOLDING R^2 fixed, using four interventions (TopK SAE feature, Ordered/Matryoshka feature, difference-of-means between consistent/inconsistent completions, activation patching from consistent runs); decisive metric: dimensional-restoration success = fraction of steers that reduce the violation score to CONSISTENT while keeping |Delta R^2| within measurement noise. Convincing support for H2 (a real ABSENCE): dimension is decodable (2a AUROC >= 0.75) yet no intervention reaches > 0.2 restoration success and its effect size is < 1/3 of fit steerability (Experiment 1) -- decodable-but-inert. Undecidable band: 2a AUROC in [0.6, 0.7) (decodability itself unresolved -- report, do not claim inertness) OR restoration success in [0.2, 0.4) (a weak handle may exist -> claim "weak/partial", not absence). Negative result for H2 (restoration success >= 0.4 for any intervention, effect within 1/3 of fit): a genuine dimensional handle EXISTS -- an equally publishable positive enabling units-aware equation discovery; reported as refutation.

Experiment 3 (H3 -- fit-steering silently produces dimensionally invalid equations, invisible to R^2/likelihood): Tests the core blind spot. Reuse Experiment 1's fit-feature steers; at each strength measure the DECISIVE metric first: SILENT-INCONSISTENCY RATE = fraction of well-formed, better-fitting equations (Delta R^2 > 0) that are dimensionally INVALID; then blind-spot magnitude = increase in violation score per unit fit gain (dose-response); then INVISIBILITY = correlation between fit gain / model likelihood and true dimensional consistency. Random-direction and matched-non-fit-feature controls. Convincing: SILENT-INCONSISTENCY RATE >= 0.3 among better-fitting equations AND invisibility |r| <= 0.2 (better-fitting equations are no more dimensionally valid). Undecidable band: rate in [0.1, 0.3) or |r| in [0.2, 0.4) -> mild blind spot; report magnitude only. Negative result (rate < 0.1 or |r| > 0.4): fit-steering preserves dimensional consistency -- a valuable positive result that NSR feature-steering is dimensionally safe.

Experiment 4 (H4 -- an intervention-free internal dimensional-consistency signal flags and prunes invalid equations): Tests the audit payoff. Systems compared: internal dimensional-consistency score (dimension-probe confidence / feature coherence read mid-generation) vs output-side signals (fit, well-formedness, model likelihood) vs a black-box raw-activation probe. Labels from Experiment 3's oracle. Decisive metric first: detection AUROC for the fit-OK/units-broken class, then calibration ECE, then two operational payoffs -- search compute saved by pruning dimensionally-invalid candidates from the beam before full data-fitting, and improvement in TRUE-Feynman-equation recovery rate when the internal signal re-ranks/prunes the beam vs fit-only selection. Convincing: internal AUROC >= 0.75 and >= 0.1 above the best output-side signal, ECE <= 0.1, and dimensional re-ranking improves true-equation recovery by >= 5 percentage points over fit-only. Undecidable band: internal-minus-output-side AUROC gap in [0.0, 0.05] or recovery improvement in [1, 5) points -> marginal payoff; report without headline. Negative result (internal AUROC < 0.6 or recovery not improved): no usable internal dimensional signal; the audit payoff is withdrawn, leaving the blind-spot demonstration (Experiment 3) as the contribution.

Experiment 5 (interpretation + robustness of H2-H4): Test whether located dimensional units encode a genuine dimension-TYPE concept (invariant to specific variables/constants) vs shallow token/operator statistics, using controlled expression pairs that dissociate dimension from surface form (same structure, variables reassigned so consistency flips; different structure, identical dimension type); auto-label top features via max-activating contexts. Minimal training ablation (probe-leakage / units-awareness control): compare the SAME probes on models trained (i) with per-variable units ingested, (ii) with units withheld, and (iii) with RANDOM-label units; genuine dimensional decoding must appear only with real units and must survive the same-structure/different-dimension dissociation pairs, ruling out surface-token leakage. Repeat Experiments 2-4 across two model sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, two layers, autoregressive vs diffusion (DiffuSR-style) NSR, and Feynman vs synthetic datasets; report the fraction of cells where the blind spot and non-steerability replicate and whether dimensional steerability is worse for equations needing transcendental-function dimensionlessness than pure polynomials. A finding stable in <50% of cells is reported as regime-specific.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Dimensional consistency is an EXACT, non-proxy symbolic oracle (unit propagation is deterministic), which is a core strength; the main proxy is 'physical validity' beyond units, which we deliberately do not claim — claims concern the objectively-checkable dimensional invariant, not full physical correctness. 2) The dimensional-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK/Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching from consistent runs), sweeping strength, requiring the model to natively span a consistency range, and head-to-head calibrating that FIT features ARE steerable in the same pipeline — so a null dimensional result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable dimensional handle) is equally publishable and directly enables units-aware equation discovery without architectural surgery. 3) Fit and dimensional consistency are partly entangled (the true equation is both well-fitting and consistent); the partial-correlation feature selection and dimension-flipping dissociation pairs (step 5) isolate genuinely fit-independent dimensional signal, and we report where separation is impossible. 4) Some NSR checkpoints do not ingest units at all; we ensure the training data provides per-variable units (Feynman + synthetic) so the model COULD in principle represent dimensions, making the absence claim substantive. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes (which PATCHES shows are partly correlational, so we corroborate with causal patching), and random-direction controls. 6) An internal dimensional probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (fit-steerable, dimensions-decodable-but-weakly-steerable, type-concept-vs-token-statistics) and the audit/search-pruning payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If no blind spot is found (fit steering preserves dimensional consistency), that is a valuable positive result establishing that NSR feature-steering is dimensionally safe and that these models robustly represent physical units.

Name: chirality_syntactic_shortcut
Title: A Tag, Not a Concept: Do String-Based Molecular Generators Represent Chirality Causally or Copy It as Syntax?
Short Hypothesis: String-based (SMILES/SELFIES) molecular generative models emit stereochemistry tokens (@/@@, E/Z) not because they possess a semantically-grounded internal representation of 3D chirality, but as a largely syntactic copy-from-context habit. We hypothesize that (i) NO compact intervention was FOUND -- under multiple intervention types, layers, and strengths -- that causally flips a stereocenter's configuration while holding the rest of the molecule fixed; (ii) instead, the model tracks a shallow 'stereo-parity bookkeeping' signal tied to local ring/branch syntax; and (iii) this makes controlled enantiomer design (asking for the R vs S form of a specified scaffold) systematically unreliable in a way ordinary validity/property checks never reveal. We keep decodability, steerability, and design-reliability as three separately-tested claims, and confirm the intervention pipeline works on a known non-chiral feature before reading any null on chirality.
Related Work: Chirality is known to break geometric ML: 'E(3)-equivariant models cannot learn chirality' (2024) proves 3D-invariant GNNs discard it, and chirality-aware GNNs (MolKGNN 2023, ChiENN 2023, tetrahedral MPNNs 2020, ChiDeK 2026) add architecture to recover it. On the generative side, 'Stereochemistry-aware string-based molecular generation' (2025) shows string models CAN emit stereochemistry but says nothing about the internal mechanism. Mechanistic work on molecular transformers ('Circuits, Features, and Heuristics in Molecular Transformers' 2025) finds ring/branch syntax circuits and a steerable valence-capacity direction, and SynFlowNet interpretability (2025) finds decodable physicochemical features - but NEITHER examines chirality, the one property where 2D connectivity is uninformative and a genuine internal 3D concept would be required. No prior interpretability study asks whether a string-based generator's stereochemistry tokens are backed by a causal, steerable chirality representation or are a syntactic shortcut, nor audits controlled-enantiomer design reliability through this lens. This distinguishes the proposal from all prior chirality-architecture work (which changes the model) and from my own prior steering proposals (which assumed the target property has a genuine internal handle). Here the central claim is the ABSENCE of such a handle for the hardest, most safety-critical property.
