DELTA vs 'Circuits, Features, and Heuristics in Molecular Transformers' (2025): that work analyzes attention/residual-stream circuits correlationally and never intervenes on stereochemistry; our causal edit test can FALSIFY a chirality representation by showing an intervention cannot flip a stereocenter while holding the graph fixed -- something correlational analyses cannot establish. This is a new causal test, not a claim that chirality has never been studied. Three separable claims -- decodability, steerability, design-reliability -- each with its own acceptance criterion; a positive control on a known non-chiral steerable feature guards against a weak-pipeline artifact.
Abstract: Chirality determines whether a drug heals or harms -- enantiomers share identical 2D connectivity yet can differ drastically in safety and potency -- and it is the one molecular property that cannot be read off a graph, requiring genuine 3D reasoning. String-based generative models (SMILES/SELFIES language models) routinely emit stereochemistry tokens (@/@@, E/Z) and pass validity checks, but whether they hold an internal, causally-manipulable representation of chirality or merely copy stereo tags as local syntax is unknown. Prior mechanistic work on molecular transformers analyzes attention and residual-stream circuits for ring/branch syntax and valence, but never causally intervenes on stereochemistry; our delta is a causal edit test that can FALSIFY a chirality representation -- showing an intervention cannot flip a stereocenter while holding the graph fixed -- which correlational attention/probe analyses cannot. Training sparse autoencoders on SMILES/SELFIES language models, we separate three claims: (1) DECODABILITY -- probe stereocenter configuration, net of a purely syntactic control probe; (2) STEERABILITY -- whether any compact intervention flips a targeted stereocenter (R->S) in the finished molecule while holding the rest of the graph, other centers, and validity fixed, with a POSITIVE CONTROL steering a known non-chiral feature (valence capacity) to prove the pipeline can steer; and (3) INTERPRETATION plus a DESIGN-RELIABILITY AUDIT -- whether located units track true CIP parity or shallow syntax, and how often requesting a specified enantiomer silently returns the wrong one, undetected by validity/likelihood. We predict no clean causal chirality handle, stereo tokens riding syntax, and silent enantiocontrol failure -- yielding a concrete pre-flight enantioreliability check, for medicinal chemists and generative-model builders, for when generated stereochemistry can be trusted. A positive (steerable handle) result is equally actionable, enabling controllable stereochemical generation.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: autoregressive SMILES and SELFIES language models (~90M parameters), trained by us (or public checkpoints where available) on a stereochemistry-rich subset of ChEMBL/PubChem that retains @/@@ and E/Z tags (~2M molecules with defined stereocenters); two model sizes (~30M, ~90M) for scaling. Base weights frozen. SAEs: TopK (k=32, dictionary 16384) on mid-layer residual streams (two layers), seeds {0,1}, FVU reported. Ground truth via RDKit: canonical CIP labels (R/S) per stereocenter, E/Z per double bond, enantiomer/diastereomer relations. Validity gates: RDKit-parseable, valence-valid, stereochemically well-defined (no undefined-but-implied centers). Interventions: SAE-feature clamp/steer, difference-of-means (R-minus-S) direction, and enantiomer activation-patching; norm-matched random-direction and matched-non-chirality-feature controls; strength swept.

Experiment 0/1 (H1 -- Baseline that stereochemistry is genuinely emitted, then: is chirality decodable?). Establishes that the model emits correct, non-trivial stereochemistry (so a later null steering result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact), and locates candidate chirality directions. Data: 5,000 generated valid molecules with defined stereocenters; 2,000 held-out natural molecules for probing. Baseline metric: fraction of generated stereocenters whose CIP label matches a chemically sensible completion and stereo-token accuracy vs a copy-context null. Probing: at token positions surrounding each stereocenter, train linear/MLP probes to predict CIP R/S from residual activations and from SAE features; report AUROC vs generation-progress and layer, against an SAE-independent raw-activation probe AND against a purely syntactic control probe (predict whether the next stereo token is @ vs @@ from the partial string). Decisive metric: chirality-probe AUROC minus syntax-probe AUROC. Convincing baseline+location: model stereo-token accuracy clearly above the copy-context null AND chirality-probe AUROC>=0.75. Decision band: chirality-minus-syntax AUROC gap in [0.0, 0.1] means the "chirality" decodability is largely syntax prediction -- flagged, and location is treated as syntactic. Negative baseline: if the model does not emit correct stereochemistry above the copy null, the study is under-powered for absence claims and reported as inconclusive rather than confirming H1.

Experiment 2 (H1 -- No compact causal stereocenter-flip handle). Tests whether any compact intervention flips a targeted stereocenter R->S while holding the rest of the graph, other centers, and validity fixed. Data: 3,000 single-stereocenter molecules and 1,500 multi-stereocenter molecules. Systems: SAE-feature intervention, difference-of-means direction, and enantiomer activation-patching, each vs random-direction and matched-non-chirality-feature controls; dose-response swept. PIPELINE POSITIVE CONTROL: on the same molecules we steer a known NON-CHIRAL feature (valence capacity, per prior molecular-transformer mechanistic work) and require it to change the intended structural property above the random control, proving the intervention pipeline can steer before any null on chirality is interpreted as absence. Decisive metric (primary): ENANTIOFLIP SUCCESS RATE = fraction of interventions producing the exact mirror configuration at the TARGET center while (a) keeping the 2D graph identical, (b) leaving other centers unchanged, (c) preserving validity. Convincing support for H1 (no handle): best-intervention enantioflip success <= 15% (barely above the random-direction control) despite the confirmed baseline, with failures dominated by graph corruption / wrong-center flips / racemization. Decision band: success in (15%, 40%] is a PARTIAL/UNRELIABLE handle -- reported as neither clean absence nor clean presence; center-specificity (multi-center bleed rate) decides how it is framed. Negative (refutes H1): success >= 40% with high specificity means a genuine steerable chirality handle EXISTS -- an equally publishable positive finding that overturns the hypothesis.

Experiment 3 (H2 -- The signal is shallow syntactic parity bookkeeping, not 3D parity). Tests whether the located units track true CIP parity or local @/@@ ring/branch syntax. Data: controlled substrate pairs -- (i) molecules where the same @/@@ token maps to opposite CIP labels depending on neighbor ordering, and (ii) matched pairs where CIP label is constant but ring/branch context varies; plus SMILES-rewriting/canonicalization that preserves the molecule (random non-canonical SMILES re-enumeration via RDKit with fixed atom mapping, so the molecule and its CIP labels are provably unchanged while token order and ring-closure syntax vary). Decisive metric: feature-meaning INVARIANCE under molecule-preserving SMILES rewriting = correlation of feature activation with true CIP parity vs with raw @/@@ syntax. Convincing support for H2: feature tracks raw syntax (syntax correlation >= 0.7) and flips meaning under rewriting (CIP-parity correlation <= 0.3). Decision band: mixed loadings (both correlations in [0.3, 0.7)) means the unit is partly conceptual, partly syntactic -- reported as intermediate, not a clean shortcut. Negative: feature stays invariant to rewriting and tracks true CIP parity (parity correlation >= 0.7) means the model has a genuine 3D-parity representation, refuting H2.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Controlled-enantiomer design is silently unreliable, missed by output-side checks). Tests that requesting a specified enantiomer often returns the wrong one and that validity/likelihood do not detect it while an internal probe does. Data: request a SPECIFIED enantiomer of given scaffolds, stratified by number of stereocenters and scaffold complexity; 3,000 requests. Decisive metric (primary): SILENT ENANTIO-ERROR RATE = fraction of valid outputs returning the wrong enantiomer, opposite/undefined configuration, racemate, or chirality at a different center; secondary: detection AUROC/calibration of output-side signals (RDKit-validity, likelihood/perplexity, a property-predictor's confidence) vs the internal chirality-probe score from Experiment 1 for catching wrong-enantiomer outputs. Convincing positive: silent enantio-error rate rising with stereocenter count to >= 30% at >=2 centers, with output-side detection AUROC in [0.45, 0.60] (near chance) while the internal probe reaches AUROC>=0.75 -- a usable pre-flight enantioreliability filter. Decision band: error rate in [15%, 30%) means unreliability is present but modest; internal-probe AUROC in [0.6, 0.75) is a weak filter -- reported with its error. Negative: error rate < 15% and output-side signals already detect errors (AUROC>=0.7) means enantiocontrol is reliable / already checkable, refuting H3. Robustness across SMILES vs SELFIES, two model sizes, two SAE variants, and E/Z stereochemistry; test whether enantioflip success or error rate improves with scale or training stereochemistry density.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The core claim is partly an ABSENCE claim (no clean causal handle), which requires strong effort to steer before concluding failure; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (SAE features, difference-of-means, enantiomer activation-patching), sweeping strength, and requiring the baseline in step 1 to confirm the model does emit correct stereochemistry - so a null enantioflip is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. 2) A positive result (a genuine steerable chirality handle exists) is equally publishable and would itself be a novel, useful finding for stereocontrolled design. 3) Stereochemistry ground truth relies on RDKit CIP assignment, which can be ambiguous for exotic centers; we restrict to well-defined central and E/Z stereochemistry and report assignment confidence. 4) Claims concern model-internal representation and string-level stereochemistry, not wet-lab bioactivity; the safety framing is about reliably producing the REQUESTED enantiomer, an objective structural fact. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound location; controlled with multiple SAE variants, layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) SMILES/SELFIES tokenization differences may complicate cross-encoding comparison; we standardize the stereochemistry evaluation on RDKit-parsed finished molecules. 7) An internal probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, the interpretability (syntactic-vs-conceptual diagnosis) and the reliability-audit payoff are the contributions and are reported honestly.

Name: evolutionary_time_steering
Title: Steering Backward Through Deep Time: Is the Phylogenetic Manifold of Protein Language Models a Causal Design Lever for Ancestral Sequences?
Short Hypothesis: Protein language models internally encode a decodable phylogenetic 'evolutionary-time' manifold, but we hypothesize this manifold is DECODABLE-BUT-WEAKLY-STEERABLE. This proposal is the first causal steering test of evolutionary DEPTH in a protein LM. ONE primary hypothesis, ONE primary metric (placement-depth error): interpretable features let you READ a sequence's evolutionary position, yet steering generation along the phylogenetic direction to design a plausible ANCESTRAL sequence at a specified evolutionary distance systematically fails—silently producing sequences that preserve family identity while landing at the wrong evolutionary depth and violating true-ancestor substitution/indel statistics, a blind spot that family-membership and validity checks miss but a phylogenetic-placement oracle exposes. All other analyses (family steerability calibration, mechanism interpretation, internal audit) are secondary/robustness. Novelty is typed: the FINDING (depth decodable but not steerable), the SETTING/ORACLE (gold-standard ML-ASR placement as clean ground truth), distinct from prior decodability, latent-interpolation-ASR, and static-property SAE steering.
Related Work: Multiple works establish that pLMs DECODE phylogeny: 'Do protein language models learn phylogeny?' (2024) shows <10% of ESM2 neurons recapitulate classical phylogenetic distances; MSA-Transformer column attentions correlate with Hamming distances (2022); Evo 2 encodes phylogeny as a curved manifold ('Finding the Tree of Life in Evo 2', 2025); mBERT encodes language phylogeny (2020). Separately, deep-learning ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) is advancing (autoregressive-generative ASR 2024; BetaReconstruct 2026; LASE 2023) but treats generative models as black-box reconstructors, NOT as interpretable steerable systems. Critically, 'Ancestral Sequences Cannot be Accurately Reconstructed via Interpolation in a VAE Latent Space' (2025) shows latent interpolation fails for ASR despite the latent space containing phylogenetic signal—exactly the decodable-but-not-usable gap—but never tests SAE-feature steering of a pLM, never contrasts family-identity steerability against evolutionary-depth steerability, and never audits silent failure. SAE-steering work (InterPLM, ProtSAE, Steering PLMs, low-N SAE design) steers toward static structural/functional properties and never touches the temporal/evolutionary axis. No prior work (a) asks whether the phylogenetic manifold is CAUSALLY steerable for generation, (b) contrasts steering family-identity (easy) vs evolutionary-depth (hypothesized hard), or (c) provides an internal evolutionary-placement audit. This introduces the temporal/evolutionary-time axis into interpretability-of-generation, distinct from all my prior static/endpoint/relational/pathway proposals. One-sentence novelty: the first causal steering test of evolutionary DEPTH in a protein LM. Typed novelty—FINDING (depth decodable but not generatively steerable), MECHANISM (whether depth units are a genuine evolutionary-distance concept), and ORACLE/SETTING (gold-standard ML-ASR + tree-placement as clean ground truth). Contrast with closest prior and what each CANNOT test: 'Do pLMs learn phylogeny?' 2024 and MSA-Transformer 2022 show DECODABILITY but not causal steering; 'Finding the Tree of Life in Evo 2' 2025 shows a phylogenetic manifold but not that it is a design lever; generative ASR (autoregressive-ASR 2024; BetaReconstruct 2026; LASE 2023) reconstructs ancestors black-box, without interpretable steering; the VAE-interpolation-ASR failure 2025 shows decodable-but-not-usable but never tests pLM SAE-feature steering or contrasts family vs depth steerability; static-property SAE steering (InterPLM, ProtSAE) never touches the temporal axis. Concrete users: ASR researchers, ancestral-protein engineers, and mechanistic-interpretability researchers. If steering fails, ancestral-design workflows should keep using ML-ASR and treat pLM depth as read-only; if it succeeds, feature steering becomes a fast interpretable ASR knob.
Abstract: A protein's sequence carries not just what it does but WHEN in evolutionary history it existed: ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) is foundational in evolutionary biology and a promising route to robust enzymes. Protein language models are known to encode phylogeny as a decodable geometric manifold, and generative models are increasingly proposed for ASR—yet whether this encoded structure is a CAUSALLY STEERABLE design lever is unknown, and prior latent-interpolation ASR fails despite the latent containing phylogenetic signal. We run the first causal steering test of evolutionary DEPTH in a protein LM. Our single primary hypothesis is an evolutionary-depth blind spot with a single primary metric (placement-depth error): steering an interpretable feature to move a sequence 'back in time' reliably preserves protein-family identity while failing to place it at the intended depth or match the substitution/indel statistics of true ancestors—invisible to family-membership and validity checks but exposed by a phylogenetic-placement oracle. Using ESM-2 (and optionally Evo 2 for DNA) with sparse autoencoders, we LOCATE family-identity and depth features, CAUSALLY contrast their steerability against gold-standard maximum-likelihood ASR ancestors and tree placement, interpret whether depth units are genuine or shallow proxies, and audit whether an internal phylogenetic-consistency signal flags misplaced designs. Silent misplacement wastes resurrection experiments and misleads biological inference. Either way is actionable: a steerable evolutionary-time handle would be a striking advance for interpretable ASR and ancestral-protein engineering; a decodable-but-unsteerable result tells ASR practitioners that reading phylogeny from a pLM does not license generating ancestors by feature steering.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (FROZEN): ESM-2 (150M and 650M); generation by masked infilling. Optionally Evo 2 (DNA) at its published biologically-relevant layer as a cross-substrate check. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka SAEs, expansion 16x, k=32, 30M residual-stream activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. GOLD-STANDARD EVOLUTIONARY ORACLE: for ~10 curated Pfam families with high-support trees, run classical maximum-likelihood ancestral-sequence reconstruction (RAxML/IQ-TREE + FastML/PAML) to obtain reference ancestral sequences at each internal node and each node's evolutionary DEPTH (normalized root-distance); a simulated-evolution benchmark with known ground-truth ancestors is included alongside the empirical families. PLACEMENT oracle: pplacer/EPA-ng places any candidate on the reference tree (inferred depth, node position) and scores its substitution/indel statistics vs the model. FAMILY oracle: Pfam/HMMER assignment + family-classifier probe. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity. First confirm the model natively spans a meaningful evolutionary-depth RANGE. Steering = add alpha*d_hat during infilling; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - PLMs internally encode a decodable phylogenetic evolutionary-time manifold that features can READ): On held-out extant + reconstructed-ancestral sequences, probe SAE features/raw activations for tree-depth (root-distance), controlling for family identity via partial correlation / family-matched sets; also test the flat phylogenetic subspace reported in Evo 2. Decisive metric FIRST: the family-controlled partial R^2 for evolutionary depth. Decision band: partial R^2 >= 0.40 => depth is decodable independent of family (the readable manifold of H1 exists); R^2 in (0.20,0.40) => weak/inconclusive; R^2 < 0.20 => depth not decodable (refutes H1's readable-manifold clause).

Experiment 2 (H2 - the manifold is decodable-but-weakly-steerable: designing an ancestral sequence at a specified evolutionary depth systematically fails, preserving family identity while landing at the wrong depth): Steer extant leaf sequences 'back in time' along the depth direction (SAE feature, difference-of-means deep-vs-shallow, activation-patching from true ancestral-node sequences, family-orthogonalized direction) at swept strength and complete by masked infilling. Baselines: VAE latent interpolation (known-failing) and classical ML-ASR (gold standard). Decisive metrics FIRST: ancestor-recovery accuracy (sequence identity to the true ML ancestor at the target node) and placement-depth error (|pplacer depth - requested|, in normalized root-distance), plus the SILENT-MISPLACEMENT RATE = fraction of depth-steered, valid, in-family sequences whose inferred depth deviates from the request by > 0.20 (or whose substitution/indel profile is inconsistent with a real ancestor); and the ratio r = depth efficacy / family efficacy (family steerability calibrated in the same pipeline). Decision band: family membership preserved (>= 0.80) AND steering ancestor-recovery no better than VAE-interpolation + 0.05 and far below ML-ASR AND misplacement >= 0.30 AND r <= 0.33 => decodable-but-weakly-steerable confirmed (H2); r in (0.33,0.67) or recovery between VAE and ML-ASR => partial (test Ordered SAEs); steering matching ML-ASR within 0.05 => depth IS steerable, refuting H2.

Experiment 3 (H3 - family-membership and validity checks miss the failure but a phylogenetic-placement oracle exposes it): For the Experiment-2 sequences, Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between output-side checks (family-membership confidence, pseudo-perplexity, pLDDT, model likelihood) and the true depth-match from the placement oracle. Decision band: |rho| <= 0.20 => family/validity checks are blind while the placement oracle exposes the wrong evolutionary depth (H3 confirmed); |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; |rho| >= 0.40 => cheap checks already reveal it (weakens the blind-spot framing). ROBUSTNESS & CROSS-SUBSTRATE: two ESM-2 sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, families spanning slow/fast rates, deep vs shallow targets; optionally replicate on Evo 2; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.

PRIMARY vs SECONDARY (pre-registered). PRIMARY hypothesis: depth is decodable-but-weakly-steerable; PRIMARY metric: placement-depth error (|pplacer-inferred depth - requested|, normalized root-distance). All else—family-steerability calibration, mechanism interpretation, internal audit, cross-substrate Evo 2—is secondary/robustness. THRESHOLD JUSTIFICATION & SENSITIVITY: the 0.20 depth-error and 0.80 family-preservation bands are reported with a sensitivity sweep (0.10-0.30 and 0.70-0.90) so conclusions do not hinge on a single cutoff. DECODER vs REPRESENTATION controls: (i) same steering direction with a randomized/reinitialized decoder head; (ii) non-phylogenetic SAE directions; (iii) matched-magnitude interventions—to separate representation failure from decoding failure. SPECIFICITY ablation: test whether failure is specific to DEPTH rather than any continuous latent attribute, by running the identical pipeline on a control continuous property (e.g., sequence length or hydrophobicity) known to be steerable. UNCERTAINTY: propagate tree-inference and ASR uncertainty—stratify all results by tree-support and ancestral-node posterior confidence, reporting distributions not just point estimates. Robustness across layers, SAE types (TopK/Ordered), and intervention operators (feature add, difference-of-means, activation patching).
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The evolutionary-depth oracle relies on classical ML ancestral reconstruction and tree placement, which are themselves inferential (uncertain trees, indel handling); we mitigate by curating well-resolved Pfam families with high-support trees, using simulated-evolution benchmarks (known ground-truth ancestors) alongside empirical ones, and reporting results stratified by tree-support/oracle confidence. Claims concern model-internal, oracle-verified evolutionary-time controllability, not biological ground truth of extinct proteins—stated explicitly. 2) The depth-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK/Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching from true ancestral-node sequences, family-orthogonalized directions), sweeping strength, requiring the model to natively span a depth range, and head-to-head calibrating that FAMILY features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null depth result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuinely steerable evolutionary-time handle) is equally publishable and would be a striking, useful advance for interpretable ASR and ancestral-protein engineering. 3) Family identity and evolutionary depth are partly entangled (deep ancestors of a family are less family-typical); the partial-correlation feature selection and dissociation pairs (step 5) isolate genuinely family-independent depth signal, and we report where separation is impossible. 4) The known VAE-interpolation failure suggests depth steering may fail for decoding-fidelity reasons rather than representation reasons; we distinguish these by comparing steering (which uses the pLM's own decoder) against probe decodability and by the activation-patching test, and treat 'decodable but not generatively usable' as itself the informative finding. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes (including the flat phylogenetic subspace), and random-direction controls. 6) An internal phylogenetic-consistency probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (family-steerable, depth-decodable-but-weakly-steerable) and the audit/compute-saving payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If evolutionary-depth steering unexpectedly succeeds, it overturns the hypothesis but yields a strong positive finding that pLMs offer a controllable evolutionary-time design lever for ancestral reconstruction.

Name: periodicity_repeat_steering_blindspot
Title: Copy, Don't Just Contain: Do Interpretable Features Control the Periodic Repeat Structure of Generated Proteins, or Only Local Motif Content?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable sparse-autoencoder features of protein language models afford causal, steerable control over LOCAL, single-position content (which residues/motifs appear), but NOT over PERIODIC REPEAT STRUCTURE—the long-range copy-consistency that makes a sequence a genuine tandem-repeat protein (near-identical units repeated at a specified period and count). Consequently, steering a feature to 'make it repetitive' silently produces sequences with repeat-like local content but broken periodicity (wrong unit length, degraded copy-consistency, collapsed foldable repeat topology), a blind spot that local-content and validity checks miss but an exact repeat-detection oracle exposes; and an intervention-free internal periodicity-consistency signal flags it. Stated as four hypotheses: (H1) local single-position content is causally steerable; (H2) periodicity -- exact PERIOD, copy COUNT, and copy-CONSISTENCY -- is decodable from activations but NOT compactly steerable; (H3) 'make it repetitive' steering therefore yields repeat-like content with broken periodicity (the blind spot); (H4) an internal periodicity-consistency signal flags it. PRIMARY CLAIM: the decodable-but-inert periodicity result (H2) with the blind-spot demonstration (H3); the audit (H4) is secondary.
Related Work: All protein-LM interpretability/steering work targets LOCAL or single-position properties: InterPLM (2024) and 'Interpreting and Steering PLMs through SAEs' (2025) steer toward local motifs (zinc fingers, transmembrane regions, binding sites); 'Automated Neuron Labelling' (2025) and 'Steering Protein Language Models'/ASPO (2025) steer molecular weight, GRAVY, instability index, secondary-structure content and thermostability; CB-pLM (2024) controls per-position interpretable concepts. Every one evaluates whether a local property/motif appears—none studies PERIODIC REPEAT STRUCTURE, a global, position-coupled property requiring copy-consistency across widely separated positions. Separately, a mature biology literature establishes tandem repeats as ubiquitous (present in ~14% of proteins), functionally important, and exactly detectable with well-established tools (RepeatsDB, CE-Symm, TRIPS; Tandem Repeats in Proteins survey 2015), and difficult even for humans/DNA to synthesize precisely (TReSR 2023). No prior work asks whether the periodic/repeat structure is a causally-steerable design lever, contrasts local-content steerability against periodicity steerability, surfaces the phenomenon that 'repetitive' steering silently breaks periodicity, or provides an internal periodicity audit. This introduces the local-content vs global-periodicity axis into interpretability-of-generation, is distinct from my prior fold/symmetry/epistasis/count proposals (repeats are an exact, countable, copy-consistency invariant, not a fold or an element count), and turns exact repeat detection into a mechanism-and-audit target. Contrast: InterPLM/ASPO/CB-pLM control LOCAL properties (motifs, GRAVY, molecular weight, per-position concepts) evaluated by appearance; this proposal uniquely tests control of a GLOBAL, position-coupled invariant (period/count/copy-consistency). Concrete applications of exact repeat control: modular repeat-protein scaffolds, repeat-based binders (e.g., designed solenoids), and symmetric architectures -- design targets currently bottlenecked by the difficulty of enforcing faithful long-range copies.
Abstract: Tandem-repeat proteins—sequences built from near-identical units repeated at a regular period—make up roughly 14% of all proteins and underpin scaffolds, binders, and designable modular architectures. Building one requires not just repeat-like local content but long-range COPY-CONSISTENCY: the same unit reproduced faithfully at a specified period and count. Interpretability-guided protein design increasingly steers language-model features to install desired properties, but every demonstrated target is LOCAL (a motif, hydrophobicity, molecular weight). We ask whether interpretable features can causally control periodic repeat structure at all, or only local content. We surface a behavioral phenomenon we call the periodicity blind spot: steering a feature to make a sequence 'repetitive' reliably raises local repeat-like content while failing to enforce the correct period, unit count, and copy-consistency—invisible to composition and validity checks but exposed exactly by repeat-detection tools (T-REKS/HHrepID/CE-Symm on ESMFold structures). Repeats are the ideal testbed because periodicity is an exact, cheap, position-coupled oracle. Using ESM-2 with sparse autoencoders, we (1) LOCATE candidate local-content features and candidate periodicity/copy-consistency features via probing; (2) CAUSALLY test the steerability of each, contrasting content control against periodicity control; (3) INTERPRET whether located periodicity units encode a genuine copy-consistency concept or shallow local-composition proxies; and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an internal periodicity-consistency signal flags silently-broken repeats better than content or model likelihood. Who cares: protein designers building modular scaffolds and interpretability researchers auditing controllability claims -- if the blind spot holds, steering benchmarks must add global position-coupled invariants; if periodicity proves steerable, that is a new design capability. We predict content control succeeds, periodicity is decodable-but-weakly-steerable, and a cheap internal audit (primary endpoint: H2 plus the blind-spot rate H3 on ESM-2 650M) catches broken repeats before costly structural validation.
Experiments:
Shared setup (fixed once, reused below). MODEL (frozen): ESM-2 150M and 650M (proteins; public checkpoints), generation by masked infilling. Frozen; only SAEs/probes trainable. SAEs: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka on the residual stream at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer (plus a second layer), width 16x, k=32, Adam lr 1e-3, ~40M activation tokens, seeds {0,1,2}; reconstruction accepted at fraction-variance-unexplained <=0.2. PERIODICITY oracles (exact/cheap): sequence-level repeat detection (T-REKS / HHrepID / XSTREAM) returning unit length (PERIOD), copy COUNT, and COPY-CONSISTENCY (mean pairwise identity among detected units); plus a structural repeat check (CE-Symm on ESMFold structures) for foldable repeat topology -- sequence-level oracles lead the core claims, structural repeats corroborate. LOCAL-CONTENT oracles: amino-acid composition, motif/tract presence (regex/HMMER), and a composition-preserving shuffled-sequence control that destroys periodicity (isolating content from structure). VALIDITY gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity. PRECONDITION: confirm the model natively spans a meaningful RANGE of periodicity states (non-repetitive to well-formed repeats); assemble a labeled corpus of repeat vs non-repeat proteins from RepeatsDB (thousands of annotated repeat proteins available; we use ~2,000 repeat + 2,000 non-repeat held-out) plus composition-matched shuffled controls. Compute: two ESM-2 sizes + ESMFold + repeat tools on 1-2 GPUs, academic-feasible.

OPERATIONAL DEFINITIONS (fixed in one place): PERIODICITY = a detected repeat with unit length (PERIOD) p and copy COUNT c; COPY-CONSISTENCY = mean pairwise sequence identity among detected units; SILENT-BROKEN-REPEAT = a valid, repeat-like-composition sequence for which the exact oracle finds no period / a wrong period / copy-consistency below a pre-set threshold; the INTERNAL periodicity score = the periodicity-probe confidence read from the steered activation. PRE-REGISTERED PRIMARY ENDPOINT: the decodable-but-inert result (Experiment 2) plus the silent-broken-repeat rate (Experiment 3) on ESM-2 650M with sequence-level oracles; second size, layers, SAE variants, and structural (CE-Symm) corroboration are secondary. A power/variance analysis on a pilot of 200 sequences sets the N needed for the main AUROC/effect-size comparisons to resolve the stated bands.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- local single-position content IS causally steerable): Tests that SAE features steer which residues/motifs appear. Identify LOCAL-CONTENT features (probe AUROC / concept-correlation for composition / motif presence on held-out sequences, retain AUROC >= 0.7). For each of >=8 content features, sweep steering strength (6 levels) during masked infilling, generate 100 sequences per level, and measure the DECISIVE metric first: local-content gain (composition/motif shift) per unit steer, with specificity and a matched-norm random-direction control. Convincing: median content gain per unit steer with Cohen's d >= 0.8 vs random control and monotone dose-response (|rho| >= 0.6) for a majority of features. Undecidable band: d in [0.2, 0.5) or |rho| in [0.2, 0.4) -> content-steerability unestablished for that feature; drop from H2's head-to-head. Negative result (d < 0.2 across features): local content is not steerable, the blind-spot premise collapses; reported as a controllability null.

Experiment 2 (H2 -- NO compact, causally-steerable periodicity/copy-consistency handle): Tests that periodicity is decodable-but-inert. (2a decodability) Probe SAE features and raw activations to predict repeat presence, period, and copy-consistency, controlling for composition via partial correlation AND via composition-matched shuffled controls; decisive metric: periodicity-probe AUROC/R^2 above the composition-matched-shuffle floor. (2b steerability) In the SAME pipeline as Experiment 1, calibrate that content features steer, then attempt to install a specified period/count with high copy-consistency while HOLDING composition fixed, using four interventions (TopK SAE feature, Ordered/Matryoshka feature, difference-of-means repeat-vs-shuffled direction, activation patching from true repeat proteins); also test SET-POINT control -- request specific unit lengths (20, 30, 40) and copy counts and measure exact-target hit-rate vs merely "more repetitive". Decisive metric: periodicity-steering success = fraction of steers installing the intended period/count at copy-consistency above a chosen threshold, with composition held fixed. Convincing support for H2 (a real ABSENCE): periodicity is decodable (2a AUROC >= 0.75 above shuffle floor) yet no intervention reaches > 0.2 set-point success and its effect size is < 1/3 of content steerability (Experiment 1). Undecidable band: 2a AUROC in [0.6, 0.7) above floor (decodability unresolved -- report, do not claim inertness) OR set-point success in [0.2, 0.4) (a weak handle may exist -> claim "weak/partial"). Negative result for H2 (set-point success >= 0.4 for any intervention, effect within 1/3 of content): a genuine periodicity handle EXISTS -- an equally publishable positive enabling modular repeat-protein design; reported as refutation.

Experiment 3 (H3 -- "make it repetitive" steering silently yields repeat-like content but broken periodicity): Tests the core blind spot. For each candidate periodicity feature, sweep steering strength and infill N=100 sequences per level. Decisive metric first: SILENT-BROKEN-REPEAT RATE = fraction of "repetitive-steered", valid sequences with repeat-like composition but FAILING the exact repeat oracle (no detected period / wrong period / copy-consistency below threshold); then blind-spot magnitude = fraction of periodicity-steering displacement landing on the local-content axis rather than the periodicity axis (dose-response); then INVISIBILITY = correlation between composition/validity/pseudo-perplexity and true periodicity, with composition-matched shuffles scoring high on content but zero on periodicity. Random-direction, matched-content-feature, PERIOD-MATCHED-nonrepeat, and composition-matched-but-periodicity-orthogonalized direction controls. Convincing: SILENT-BROKEN-REPEAT RATE >= 0.3 among "repetitive" valid sequences AND invisibility |r| <= 0.2 (standard checks miss broken periodicity). Undecidable band: rate in [0.1, 0.3) or |r| in [0.2, 0.4) -> mild blind spot; report magnitude only. Negative result (rate < 0.1 or |r| > 0.4): content steering yields well-formed repeats -- a valuable positive result that PLM feature-steering can control long-range periodic structure.

Experiment 4 (H4 -- an intervention-free internal periodicity-consistency signal flags silently-broken repeats): Tests the audit payoff. Systems compared: internal periodicity-consistency score (periodicity-probe confidence / feature coherence read from the steered activation) vs output-side signals (composition, validity, model likelihood) vs a black-box raw-activation probe. Labels from Experiment 3's oracle. Decisive metric first: detection AUROC for the content-OK/periodicity-broken class, then calibration ECE, then compute saved by flagging non-periodic designs before running CE-Symm/ESMFold structural validation. Convincing: internal AUROC >= 0.75 and >= 0.1 above the best output-side signal, ECE <= 0.1. Undecidable band: internal-minus-output-side AUROC gap in [0.0, 0.05] -> no added value; report parity. Negative result (internal AUROC < 0.6): no usable internal periodicity signal; the audit payoff is withdrawn, leaving the blind-spot demonstration (Experiment 3) as the contribution.

Experiment 5 (interpretation + robustness of H2-H4): Test whether located "periodicity" units encode a genuine copy-consistency concept (invariant to which residues fill the unit, tracking period/consistency) vs shallow local-composition proxies, using controlled pairs that dissociate periodicity from composition (same composition, repeat vs shuffled; different compositions, same period); auto-label top features via max-activating contexts (do they fire at unit boundaries / on high-identity duplications?). Repeat Experiments 2-4 across two model sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, two layers, and short vs long unit lengths / low vs high copy counts; report the fraction of cells where the blind spot and non-steerability replicate and whether periodicity steerability degrades with longer periods and higher copy counts. A finding stable in <50% of cells is reported as regime-specific.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Periodicity is measured by well-established repeat-detection tools (T-REKS/HHrepID/CE-Symm), which are near-exact for sequence period/count/copy-consistency and slightly noisier for structural repeats (CE-Symm on predicted structures); we lead with sequence-level oracles for core claims and treat structural repeats as corroborating, reporting oracle sensitivity to thresholds. Claims concern model-internal, oracle-verified periodicity controllability, not wet-lab function—stated explicitly. 2) The periodicity-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK/Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching from real repeat proteins, content-orthogonalized directions), sweeping strength, requiring the model to natively span a periodicity range, and head-to-head calibrating that LOCAL-CONTENT features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null periodicity result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable periodicity/copy-consistency handle) is equally publishable and directly enables modular repeat-protein design. 3) Composition and periodicity are partly entangled (repeats bias composition); the partial-correlation feature selection and composition-matched shuffled controls (steps 2,3,5) isolate genuinely composition-independent periodicity signal, and we report where separation is impossible. 4) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 5) An internal periodicity probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (content-steerable, periodicity-decodable-but-weakly-steerable) and the audit/compute-saving payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 6) Masked-infilling steering of long-range copy-consistency is nontrivial; we standardize on finished-sequence oracle evaluation and use activation patching from true repeats as an architecture-agnostic cross-check. 7) If no blind spot is found (content steering yields well-formed repeats), that is a valuable positive result establishing that PLM feature-steering can control long-range periodic structure.

Name: interpolation_path_validity
Title: Cliffs on the Morphing Path: Do Interpretable-Feature Interpolations Between Two Valid Designs Traverse Valid, Monotone Ground?
Short Hypothesis: When a designer morphs one valid scientific object into another by interpolating in the interpretable SAE feature space of a frozen foundation-model generator, the intermediate designs are NOT reliably valid nor monotone in the property being morphed: the path silently crosses validity 'cliffs' (invalid/unfoldable/unsynthesizable intermediates) and exhibits non-monotone property overshoot, even though both endpoints are valid and the endpoints' property values bracket the intermediates'. We further hypothesize that interpolating in the SAE feature space stays valid and monotone MORE often than interpolating in the raw activation space, and that a cheap intervention-free path-curvature/off-manifold signature predicts where a given interpolation will break. PRIMARY CLAIM: the path-cliff/non-monotonicity PHENOMENON in interpretable SAE feature space (an empirical audit, not a new theory of why cliffs form); the SAE-vs-raw comparison, the geometry predictor, and the reroute are secondary.
Related Work: Latent-space interpolation and manifold traversal for design is a mature line: ACAI (2018) regularizes autoencoders for realistic interpolation; STONED (2021), ChemFlow (2024), ChemSpacE (2022), ChemoVerse (2020), and Navigating Chemical Space with Latent Flows all traverse or interpolate WHOLE-OBJECT VAE/GAN latent spaces for molecule discovery; 'Revisiting Latent-Space Interpolation' (2021) benchmarks interpolation ALGORITHMS (linear vs slerp) on VAEs. Crucially, ALL of these (a) operate on bespoke VAE/GAN latent spaces, not the INTERPRETABLE SAE feature space of a frozen foundation-model generator, (b) evaluate interpolation by endpoint recovery, smoothness, or aggregate validity, and (c) never test whether property change along the path is MONOTONE or whether intermediates cross validity CLIFFS, nor tie failures to named interpretable features. SAE-steering work (InterPLM 2024, ProtSAE 2025, chemistry/RNA SAEs) only does single-point steering and never studies interpolation paths at all. My own prior proposals study endpoint steering, off-mode reach, and side-effect drift, but never the reliability of a design-MORPHING trajectory. This is the first to reframe interpolation-for-lead-optimization as a path-validity/monotonicity reliability question in interpretable feature space, and to contrast SAE-feature vs raw-activation interpolation on that axis. Exact delta: the same broad interpolation-invalidity concern as ACAI/ChemFlow/ChemSpacE, but a NEW representation class -- the interpretable SAE feature space of a FROZEN foundation-model generator rather than a bespoke VAE/GAN latent trained for smooth interpolation -- plus a new predictability claim. Prior latent-interpolation results do not transfer because SAE features are sparse, over-complete, and not optimized for geodesic smoothness, so linear feature-space paths can leave the model's activation manifold where a purpose-built VAE latent would not. The novelty is thus the setting and the diagnostic, not the base phenomenon.
Abstract: Lead optimization and design exploration routinely proceed by morphing one good design into another—interpolating between two valid objects and picking intermediates. With interpretable sparse autoencoders (SAEs) now decomposing frozen protein and molecule generators into named feature directions, a natural and appealing workflow is to interpolate in this interpretable feature space, reading off which concepts turn on and off along the way. We ask whether that morphing path is trustworthy. Even when both endpoints are valid and their property values bracket the intermediates', the path between them need not stay on the valid manifold or change the property monotonically. We surface a behavioral phenomenon we call path cliffs: interpolations between two valid designs silently cross validity cliffs (invalid, unfoldable, or unsynthesizable intermediates) and exhibit non-monotone property overshoot, a failure invisible to endpoint checks. Using ESM-2 protein language models and a SMILES chemical language model with SAEs and cheap oracles (ESMFold pLDDT, RDKit validity/logP, DSSP, GRAVY), we (1) quantify path-validity and monotonicity along interpolations between valid endpoint pairs; (2) test whether SAE-feature-space interpolation stays valid and monotone more often than raw-activation interpolation and simple sequence/graph edits; (3) LOCATE where cliffs occur and which interpretable features flip at the cliff; and (4) validate a cheap intervention-free path-curvature/off-manifold signature that predicts where an interpolation will break, plus a cliff-avoiding reparameterization. Lead-optimization chemists and protein engineers picking such intermediates would otherwise ship a seemingly-safe but silently-invalid design; if cliffs are real, path vetting/rerouting becomes mandatory. Pre-registered primary endpoint: the cliff rate for logP-bracketed molecule pairs, with the phenomenon standing even if the predictor/fix fail -- recasting interpretable interpolation from an assumed-smooth tool into an auditable, geometry-predictable one.
Experiments:
Shared setup (fixed once, reused below). MODELS (frozen): ESM-2 150M and 650M (proteins); a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~85M, MOSES-trained or public checkpoint). Frozen; only SAEs/probes trainable. SAEs: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka on the residual stream at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer (plus a second layer), width 16x, k=32, Adam lr 1e-3, ~40M activation tokens, seeds {0,1,2}; reconstruction accepted at fraction-variance-unexplained <=0.2 AND encode/decode round-trip fidelity verified (object -> activations -> SAE features -> reconstructed activations -> regenerated object recovers the source object within a stated identity/Tanimoto tolerance; paths on SAEs failing round-trip are excluded so cliffs are not round-trip artifacts). PROPERTY/VALIDITY oracles: proteins -- ESMFold pLDDT (validity/foldability), DSSP secondary-structure content, GRAVY, molecular weight, pseudo-perplexity; molecules -- RDKit-validity, logP, QED, ring count, synthetic accessibility. Compute: two ESM-2 sizes + small SMILES LM + ESMFold on 1-2 GPUs, academic-feasible.

PRE-REGISTERED PRIMARY ENDPOINT: the cliff rate and endpoint-blindness (Experiment 1) for logP-bracketed valid molecule PAIRS on the SMILES model; proteins, sizes, SAE variants, and slerp are confirmatory. Bands below are fixed before running, and the phenomenon claim (Experiment 1) is evaluated independently of the predictor/reroute claims (Experiment 3).

Experiment 1 (H1 -- feature-space interpolation crosses validity cliffs and is non-monotone, despite valid endpoints that bracket the property): Tests the core phenomenon. Data: 500 endpoint PAIRS per domain of VALID objects whose property values bracket a target range (e.g., low-logP and high-logP valid molecules; high-helix and high-sheet valid proteins); encode both to SAE feature space, interpolate along the straight line (and a slerp variant) at K=16 steps, decode each intermediate to an object. Decisive metric first: CLIFF RATE = fraction of paths with >= 1 intermediate that fails validity gates despite valid endpoints; then per-path MONOTONICITY = overshoot/violation score on the morphed property (max deviation outside the endpoint-bracketed range, plus count of step-wise sign reversals); then the BLIND SPOT = predictive power of endpoint validity and endpoint property values for intermediate validity/monotonicity. Convincing: cliff rate >= 0.3 and median monotonicity-violation clearly above a within-object sampling-noise floor, while endpoint features predict intermediate failure at AUROC <= 0.6 (endpoints do not warn of the cliff). Undecidable band: cliff rate in [0.1, 0.3) or endpoint-predictor AUROC in [0.6, 0.7) -> mild/partly-predictable cliffs; report distributions, do not headline. Negative result (cliff rate < 0.1 and monotone within noise): interpolation is reliably valid and monotone -- a valuable positive result establishing feature-space interpolation as a safe design tool.

Experiment 2 (H2 -- SAE-feature interpolation stays valid/monotone MORE often than raw-activation interpolation): Tests the comparative claim. Systems compared, on the SAME endpoint pairs at matched path length: (a) SAE feature-space interpolation, (b) raw residual-activation interpolation (sharing the same decode pathway, with SAE-vs-raw reconstruction error matched, to isolate the SAE effect rather than decode noise), (c) direct object-space interpolation (SMILES edit-path / sequence crossover) as a baseline. Decisive metric first: paired difference in cliff rate (SAE vs raw), then paired difference in monotonicity violation, with random-pair controls and control for endpoint distance. Convincing: SAE cliff rate is lower than raw by an absolute >= 0.1 with a paired test CI excluding 0, and monotonicity is no worse. Undecidable band: paired cliff-rate difference in [0.0, 0.05] -> SAE and raw are equivalent; report parity. Negative result (SAE cliff rate >= raw): SAE interpolation is no safer than raw -- an informative, publishable null about the value of interpretable interpolation, reported honestly.

Experiment 3 (H3 -- a cheap intervention-free path-geometry signature predicts cliffs, and a reroute reduces them): Tests the predictor and fix. Predictor: per path, before decoding, compute local off-manifold distance of intermediates (distance to nearest natural-object embedding / SAE reconstruction error) and feature-path curvature (nonlinearity of feature activations along the interpolant). The geometry signature is compared against simple baselines -- endpoint feature-space distance, per-intermediate latent norm, a path-linearity score, and decode entropy/pseudo-perplexity -- and must beat all of them (nested comparison). Decisive metric first: Spearman rho / precision@k of the geometry signature for predicting cliff location and monotonicity violation, then, for cliffed paths, whether the drop coincides with abrupt on/off switching of a small feature set (Location) vs smooth blends. Fix: reroute the path to minimize off-manifold distance (small on-manifold projected steps), compared against standard path-smoothing and an embedding shortest-path baseline; decisive metric -- reduction in cliff rate and monotonicity violation at MATCHED endpoint fidelity, traced as a cliff-rate-vs-fidelity frontier. Convincing: geometry signature reaches |rho| >= 0.5 / precision@10 >= 0.7 for cliff location, and the reroute cuts cliff rate by >= 30% at fidelity within tolerance. Undecidable band: predictor |rho| in [0.2, 0.4), or reroute cliff reduction in [10%, 30%) -> weak predictor/fix; report the frontier without a strong claim. Negative result (|rho| < 0.2 or reroute reduction < 10%): path geometry does not predict or prevent cliffs -- the predictor/fix contribution is withdrawn, leaving the phenomenon (Experiment 1) as the result.

Experiment 4 (robustness of H1-H3): Repeat across both domains, both ESM-2 sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, linear vs slerp interpolation, and >=3 properties per domain; report the fraction of cells where cliffs, the SAE-vs-raw advantage, and the geometry predictor replicate, and cliff rate as a function of endpoint distance. Monotonicity claims are restricted to the single property being interpolated toward, with off-target drift reported separately. A finding stable in <50% of cells is reported as regime-specific.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) In-silico oracles (ESMFold, RDKit, DSSP) are proxies for wet-lab truth; claims concern model-internal path reliability of interpretable interpolation, not experimental viability - stated explicitly, though validity/property values are objective given the oracle. 2) SAE encode/decode round-trip is lossy and could itself introduce apparent cliffs; we quantify round-trip fidelity and, as a control, compare against a no-SAE (raw-activation) interpolation that shares the same decode pathway to isolate SAE-specific effects. 3) Cliffs might trivially reflect endpoints being far apart in feature space; we control for path length and report cliff rate as a function of endpoint distance, and use random-endpoint-pair controls. 4) Monotonicity is only meaningful for a chosen morphed property; we restrict monotonicity claims to the single property being interpolated toward and report off-target drift separately. 5) The SAE-beats-raw hypothesis may be property- or model-specific; we test multiple properties, sizes, and SAE variants and report where it fails - a null (SAE no better than raw) is itself an informative, publishable result about the value of interpretable interpolation. 6) The path-geometry predictor may be underpowered; mitigated by many endpoint pairs and both domains. 7) The cliff-avoiding fix may lengthen paths or reduce endpoint fidelity; we quantify the tradeoff on a cliff-rate-vs-fidelity frontier rather than assume a free lunch. 8) If interpolation turns out reliably valid and monotone, that is a valuable positive result establishing interpretable feature-space interpolation as a safe design tool.
